### D219 · A booking post knows its round — posts.scheduled_round_id, and Home draws the round once
*(2026-09-02, same review. Implementation level (6) with one IA consequence — a row becomes a door (D94). BUILT 2026-09-02 — migration `20260902203000_a_booking_knows_its_round.sql` + client (`HomeStream`'s select, `HomeView`'s post row, the Up Next chip). Sources: `20260712150000_declared_rounds_and_roster.sql:21` (`public.scheduled_rounds` — the table); `20260712090000_round_posts_traceable.sql:4,20` (`round_to_board` stamps `posts.round_id`, FK to `rounds` — the precedent); `20260831170000_declare_round_posts_and_guards.sql:101-110` (the booking insert: one `system` post per league, no reference; `posts` has no `meta` column); `HomeStream.swift:99` (the select carries `live_round_id` and no other id); `HomeView.swift:524-530` (a row is a `Button` only when `live_round_id` is set); E1: 18 of the 20 rows Home rendered had it null, and three moment rows carried `posts.round_id` in prod that the client never selected; `shots/home-light-bottom.png` ("MON SEP 7 · LEAGUE MATE · 1 in", and above it "Galen put a round on the books … with Jerecho Fischbeck"); `ScheduleModels.swift:352,359` (the Up Next slot has no rung for a tagged round); `home-review/SYNTHESIS.md` §2 #5 and #8. Amended 2026-09-02: the Next-round chip is a plan you are PLAYING — a tag you declined is not, and neither is your own booking once you have declined it (`my_rsvp = 'out'`, `ScheduleModels.swift` `plans`); the row keeps "with you" on the board either way. The web's `upcomingFromSchedule` (`index.html:10978-10990`) differs on BOTH axes — it keeps the host's own declined booking as their next round AND drops rounds booked WITH you (`if (r.mine === false) return;`, never reading `tagged_me` / `my_rsvp`) — a web task under this entry.)*
- **Current mechanic:** `declare_round` fans one system post per league the host belongs to — date, tee, course, tagged names — with no reference to the `scheduled_rounds` row it describes. `round_to_board` has stamped `posts.round_id` since July; a booking has no equivalent. So the booking is told twice on Home — a dead row in the lane and the live Coming-up card at the foot — and the row addresses the reader by their own full name ("with Jerecho Fischbeck"), because the string was built server-side for a league, not a viewer. Home's select fetches `live_round_id` only, so even rows that do carry `round_id` (moments, clash settles) cannot open their receipt. And a round you are tagged in is your next round in every sense but the slot's: "Next round" keeps only rounds you own and "Buddy's playing" drops `tagged_me`, so the one card on the page that is yours renders last and the chip built to lift it renders nothing.
- **Problem:** D201 — one fact, one place: a round that is a card at the bottom of the page is also a note in the middle of it, and neither knows about the other. §16 — every line taps to its receipt, and eighteen of twenty could not.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** (1) **`posts.scheduled_round_id uuid null references public.scheduled_rounds(id) on delete set null`**; **`declare_round` stamps it** on the booking post it fans out (body verbatim, one column on the insert); a scrapped booking leaves a null pointer and the post stays — the board keeps every post. (2) **Home's post select adds `round_id` and `scheduled_round_id`**, both optional on the client — skew-safe against today's payload. (3) Doors follow the pointer: `round_id` → the receipt (round, moment, clash-settle rows); `scheduled_round_id` → the schedule card; month seals → the ledger pane; a row with no door stays a note and loses its glyph disc — never a dimmed button. (4) **Home draws the round once:** a booking row whose round is already on the page as a calendar card is hidden — the card is the authoritative surface — and where the row does render it says *with you* from the schedule row's `tagged_me`, never by substituting a name into a server string. (5) Ruled with it: a round you are tagged in **is your next round** — an Up Next chip (*Mon Sep 7 · Gold Canyon with Galen*) → the round; the card's eyebrow reads WITH YOU, its pill reuses YOU'RE IN and never asks "In or out?" once `my_rsvp` is set. **No slot reorder** — moving Coming up above the feed is a separate ruling, not taken.
- **Principle served:** D201 (one fact, one place) · §16 (every line taps to its receipt) · D94 (a row with a door is a door; one without is a note) · D104 (ask the tagged) · D176 A (every chip names a destination).
- **Benefit:** the page gets doors — round, moment and settle rows open the receipt, a booking opens its sheet; the same round is drawn once; nobody is addressed by their own full name on their own Home; the round you are in is the first chip, not the last card.
- **Tradeoffs:** one more FK on `posts` (set-null, so scrapping a booking never blocks). The web's booking row keeps rendering the server string until it reads the same column. Two different rules can now remove a system row from the lane — D217's fold and this hide-when-carded — and both leave the board untouched; the board is where the whole record lives.
- **CONFLICT (named):** D201 (one fact, one place) v `declare_round`'s per-league fan-out with no reference (`20260831170000:101–110`). `declare_round` stamps the id; Home hides the row when the round is already a calendar card and says "with you" from `tagged_me`; the board keeps the post. No upward conflict.

- **Amended 2026-09-02 (the write seal — `20260902210000_a_booking_pointer_is_the_servers.sql`).** This entry reasoned about who could READ `scheduled_round_id` and never about who could WRITE it. `authenticated` holds table-level INSERT on `posts` (`relacl = authenticated=arwdDxtm`) and the only INSERT policy, `posts_chat`, constrains kind, member and suspension — it says nothing about which COLUMNS a row may carry. Proven in prod (2026-09-02, inside a rolled-back transaction): a member could insert a chat post carrying any `scheduled_round_id`, including one pointing at another golfer's round. Nothing leaked — `scheduled_rounds` RLS is `profile_id = auth.uid()` and the round door is gated by `can_see_round()`, so a forged pointer opens exactly what the forger could already open — but the column comment asserted "Null on every other kind of post", an invariant the database did not hold, and §4 above hides a booking row on the strength of that pointer. A lie about provenance, not a disclosure: P2. Fixed with the repo's oldest grant lesson (CLAUDE.md; `20260721214500` learned it on `profiles.email`) — the TABLE grant comes off, an explicit column list goes back on: `league_id, season_id, kind, member_id, body`, which is byte-for-byte what both clients send on the one insert the policy admits (`index.html:6008`, `BoardRepository.swift:205`). Every other column is the server's, and all 39 `public` functions that insert into `posts` are SECURITY DEFINER (read out of prod), so none is affected. Verified in a rolled-back prod transaction: the ordinary chat insert still succeeds, the spoofed one fails 42501. SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE unchanged; anon still holds nothing. **Deliberately deferred to a housekeeping pass:** the trigger functions `round_refresh_index()` and the zero-arg `score_round()` carry an inert EXECUTE grant to `authenticated` while their sibling `round_achievements_on_delete()` is revoked — calling either returns "trigger functions can only be called as triggers", so it is noise, not a hole. Also deferred: `tests/db-checks.sql` check 3's RPC array is stale (18 client-called names missing, `lock_league` and `cup_final_race` among them — the two this wave replaced), so the check that catches a forgotten grant is blind for exactly those; it needs regenerating from both clients, and the guest/anon-only names must not be added to a list that asserts a grant to `authenticated`.

### D220 · A refresh that fails keeps what is on screen — and a failed read is never an empty one
*(2026-09-02, same review — raised by the batch-5 refuters, not by the audit. Implementation level (6) with a UX consequence. BUILT 2026-09-02 — client only, no migration, no copy. Sources: `SessionStore.swift:100-116` (`reload()`'s catch); `RootView.swift:25,52` (`.failed` → `BootFailedView`, the only reader of the state); the 32 `store.reload()` call sites, none of which inspect `store.state` afterwards; `CardGateView.swift:231-242` (the gate's save: `set_handle` → `set_profile` → telemetry/growth/haptic/push-ask → `await store.reload()`, all inside one `do`, and `reload()` neither throws nor returns); `HomeStream.swift:91-127` (`Result`, `home_feed` under `try?`); `HomeView.swift:268-290` (`HomeModel.run`); `YouScreen.swift:66-67` ("a career read that failed is nil too, and a failed read is not an empty card" — the precedent this generalises); `ScheduleScreen.swift:328-340`, `EventRoom`'s "The room did not load · Try again" (the silent-keep convention and its one inline line); supabase-swift `APIClient.swift:59-62,117-123` (a terminal refresh removes the session and emits `.signedOut`); `20260827130400_native_home.sql:80` (`raise exception 'Sign in first'` — what the anon-role call comes back with).)*
- **Current mechanic:** every failure inside `reload()` set `state = .failed(…)`, and `.failed` swaps the whole tab bar for "Boot stalled · Try again". `reload()` is the app's post-write refresh — 32 call sites — and Home's pull-to-refresh calls it first. So a pull on a bad signal, or a reload after any write while the lift is between bars, evicted a signed-in golfer to the boot screen and threw away every tab's navigation. Below it, `HomeStreamRepository.load` reads `home_feed` under `try?` and returns `[]`, so Home could not tell a quiet week from an unreachable server.
- **Problem:** #1 the app never lies about state — "Boot stalled" is a boot fact, and nothing had stalled; the payload was in hand. And the two failures compose: with the boot eviction gone, the failed pull now reached Home's stream, whose empty result would paint *"No rounds from your buddies yet. Post one, or add some buddies."* over the rounds that were on screen a second earlier — the same lie one screen down, and one the You screen had already ruled out for the career card.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** (1) **A refresh keeps what it has.** `reload()`'s catch keeps `.ready(me)` — the payload on screen stays, the golfer stays where they were, the failure is silent (the repo's read convention). Every other state still falls to `.failed`, because a session with nothing on screen has nothing to keep. (2) **`.cardGate` is not kept** — the gate holds no navigation worth saving, and its one caller reloads immediately after the save RPCs; kept, the golfer would sit on step 2 with the card already saved and no sign that only Home failed. Try again is that sign. (3) **A gone session ends at the door, not at Boot stalled:** when the SDK has already removed a dead session mid-reload (`session == nil`), the catch sets `.signedOut` rather than showing the raw "Sign in first" behind a retry button — but only then; a door sign-in whose first reload fails still holds a session and must reach Try again. (4) **A failed read is never an empty one:** `HomeStreamRepository.Result` carries `failed`, and `HomeModel.run` keeps the feed, digest and social already in hand when the read failed — the empty state renders only when there was nothing to keep.
- **Principle served:** #1 the app never lies · D93 (one authoritative surface — the boot screen is boot's) · the You screen's read rule, generalised.
- **Benefit:** pull-to-refresh is safe on a bad connection everywhere, not just on Home; a post-write reload can no longer cost a golfer their place in the app; the boot screen means boot again.
- **Tradeoffs:** a failed refresh now says nothing at all — the spinner ends and the page is unchanged. That matches the repo's convention for reads (`try?` + silence, with an inline line only where a screen can tell it is partial), and a screen that needs to say more should say it inline, never as a toast (toasts are for writes). A stale payload can now persist while offline: correct for a snapshot Home, and every write path still surfaces its own failure.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. Downward it amends nothing ruled — `.failed`'s copy and `BootFailedView` are untouched; what changed is which failures reach them.

### D221 · A guard that compares against null is not a guard — the loose-ends sweep, four migrations
*(2026-09-04. Implementation level (6), no gameplay mechanic changes — recorded because three of the four touch who may do what, and rule 5's spirit is that nothing about authority moves silently. BUILT 2026-09-04, migrations `20260904170000_the_reviewer_cannot_be_mailed`, `20260904173000_a_null_uid_is_not_the_founder`, `20260904180000_one_leagues_bad_day_is_its_own`, `20260904183000_truncate_is_not_a_client_verb`, plus db-checks 21/22/23. Raised by a five-agent read-only sweep of prod, the repo and the field after the D215–D220 wave shipped; none of it came from the audit backlog. Sources: prod reads on 2026-09-04 (`pg_proc.prosrc`, `pg_class.relacl`, `pg_attribute.attacl`, `pg_default_acl`, `cron.job_run_details`, `client_events`); `dig MX cupseason.app` (no MX) and a refused connect to port 25 on its A record; `20260902120000_the_month_close_that_can_miss.sql` (the isolation pattern this copies); `AuthRules.swift:36-39` and `DoorView.swift:4` (the reviewer's password door); D194, D193, D188, D37.)*
- **Current mechanic (four of them):** (1) `is_undeliverable()` knew about RFC 2606 reserved TLDs, so D194's five armed bounces became one — `reviewer@cupseason.app`, on an ordinary TLD but with no MX and no SMTP listener anywhere. (2) Nine SECURITY DEFINER functions guarded themselves with `if auth.uid() <> owner then raise`. (3) `daily_season_tick` ran every live season in one transaction with no per-season isolation, alone among the four cron entry points. (4) `authenticated` held TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER and MAINTAIN on most of `public`.
- **Problem:** (1) the first product email in this app's life would have been a 100% hard bounce, on the same Brevo reputation that carries every sign-in code, on 2026-09-08 07:20 UTC. (2) `x <> y` is NULL when either side is NULL, so those guards fail OPEN, and two of the nine compare against a column (`scrap_forfeit`'s `f.created_by`, `set_round_rsvp`'s `v_owner`) that can itself be null — no missing JWT required. (3) the tick's two busiest days of the year are 2026-09-07 (five leagues roll a week) and 2026-09-08 (the first `close_season` ever executed), and one league raising would have rolled back the others and left nothing in `job_failures`. (4) TRUNCATE bypasses RLS, so the second of this schema's two layers does not cover it.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** (1) name the reviewer address in `is_undeliverable` — the honest rule is "the domain has no MX" and a migration cannot see DNS; it is one clause to delete if a mailbox ever exists. Sign-in is untouched: that address is the one the door answers with a password. (2) `is distinct from`, in all nine, each body regenerated from prod's own `pg_get_functiondef` with one mechanical substitution — **the self-check searching for `auth.uid() <>` against ANYTHING is what found the two the sweep had missed**, and it stays in the migration and in db-checks 22 so the idiom cannot come back. (3) wrap the tick's per-season body in `begin/exception/end` writing `job_failures`, exactly as `run_month_closes` does; the `live_rounds` sweep stays outside the loop because it is nobody's league. (4) revoke the four client-useless verbs; SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE untouched.
- **Principle served:** D37 (grants are a layer, and a grant assertion is worth nothing until something fails on it) · D193 (a failure nobody can see is a failure that repeats) · D194 · #1 the app never lies.
- **Benefit:** the Sep 8 send has zero deliverable recipients and cannot bounce; nine guards fail closed; one league's bad tick is its own and lands in `cron_health()`; and the three new db-checks were each proven to FAIL against prod before their migration was written, so none of them is decorative.
- **Tradeoffs:** naming one address in SQL is a hard-coded fact that DNS could invalidate — it is commented as such. Re-generating nine bodies from prod means this migration is a snapshot: if any of the nine is edited between now and the push, the replace would silently revert that edit (the tree is clean and the window is hours).
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. **Left OPEN and deliberately not smuggled in here:** `pg_default_acl` still grants `arwdDxtm` — INSERT included — to `authenticated` on every NEW table in `public` (and to `anon` for tables created by `supabase_admin`). That is the systemic version of the hole `posts` had in D219's amendment: every future table is born wide and relies on someone remembering to seal it. Closing it makes every future migration responsible for its own grants, which is a posture change that deserves its own ruling rather than a line in a housekeeping file. db-check 23 is the tripwire until then.

## The UX overhaul — D222–D253 / IOS-028–IOS-036 (2026-09-05)

*The design set is `docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/`; the owner’s eight rulings are `OWNER_RULINGS.md`, which
outranks every artifact in that directory. The entries are appended **wave by wave, in the same commit as the
code they govern**, so a number missing from this section is a wave that has not shipped yet — not an entry
that was skipped. Each carries the date the owner authorised it and, where a ruling settled it, which ruling.*

### D226 · ME leads for everyone, including the Pro

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** — the owner ruled the eight open questions in `docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md` and authorised the overhaul; no ruling was needed on this entry itself, and **R-A**'s five destinations are what give the Pro's tools their own home. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 1a, in part:** `native_home` v3 gives every membership a `pro_name` — the Pro's first name in the board's own form — and the ME strip renders above the hero for every viewer, Pro and member alike, off the same producer and with the same four facts. **What is NOT built yet, and where it lands:** the Pro's pending action as one ranked item is wave 1b's ranker (D231), and the Pro's verb row at the foot of the season page is wave 4 (D223 / IOS-031). Until then the role × stage hero is still under the strip; it is replaced, not amended, in 1b. **Level 3 (IA).** Carries **O-05**. Sources: `INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.2, §7.5; D119 `:4222-4231`; D96; persona D's walk ("the Pro's job description where a standing should be").)*

- **Current mechanic:** the hero is a role × stage matrix — (Pro or member) × (setup, draft, preseason) — with every cell carrying a move the viewer can make. The Pro's Home says "Lock it in and invite your crew" / "Draw the squads" / "Plan the first round".
- **Problem observed:** the Pro is a golfer with a job, not a different kind of user. Addressing a whole screen to the job puts an administrative checklist where a standing belongs, and it means the Pro's own golf is the thing Home does not talk about.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** the ME strip and the lead are the same objects for every viewer. **The Pro's pending action becomes one ranked item** (Tier 6, once per condition), and the Pro's tools are **a row at the foot of the season page**, never a mode and never the identity of a screen — seven verbs, each already an RPC, each with a stated moment where it surfaces (`INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.5). D96's forming card survives as that item. **D40's guarantee — a member never sees the Pro's configuration tool — is a mechanic and stays**, moved to the intent sheet's choke point. **D132's noun is not overridden**: "the Pro" is kept and finally *defined at first contact* ("Galen runs the season (the Pro)"), which has 0 hits on both clients today — and `native_home.membership.pro_name` is the read that makes the definition possible, shipped in this wave.
- **Principle served:** vision #1 ("the golfer is the product… never optimize for league management at the expense of making golfers excited to return").
- **Expected user benefit:** the Pro opens the app and sees their own golf first, like everybody else; the job is one row away and is never lost.
- **Tradeoffs:** a Pro with a genuinely blocking task (an unlocked league on the eve of a first tee) sees it as an item rather than a hero. Mitigated by Tier 1 firing on a real clock. **And the split is real, not cosmetic:** wave 1a puts the four ME facts above the hero for everyone, but the hero underneath is still the role × stage matrix until 1b retires it, so for two waves a Pro sees their own golf *and* the job description. That is the price of not shipping the ranked list and the retirement of the producers it replaces in one push.
- **CONFLICT (named):** D119 `:4222-4231` · D96 — **superseded at IA level.** D40 and D132 are explicitly untouched.

### D234 · Two clients, one product, one set of producers, two shapes — the phone at the turn, the web at the desk

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** — the owner ruled the eight open questions in `docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md` and authorised the overhaul; this entry is settled by **R-C, as revised on 2026-09-05**. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 0** — no migration: `platform` stamped centrally in `CSTelemetry`, the four metric events (`app_open` · `home_state_seen` · `cta_tapped` · `first_act`), the web’s six false facts, and the `CLAUDE.md:301-303` correction. The web’s own desktop shape is built wave by wave beside the phone’s, starting in wave 1a. **Level 3.** Carries **O-15**, answers the question IOS-018 deferred, and is **rewritten to `OWNER_RULINGS.md` R-C as revised on 2026-09-05**. Sources: R-C; `DECISIONS.md:179-189` (IOS-018); D100 `:3633-3658`; **`CLAUDE.md:301-303`, stale**; `index.html:20066, :10987, :10877, :14125, :17705`; `PostCard.swift:238-244`; the web landmines in `CLAUDE.md`'s Architecture section; telemetry: 8 web-only vs 5 phone-only golfers in 30 days.)*

- **Current mechanic:** "the phone gets the whole web first; the web is rethought after" (IOS-018/D100, level 6 sequencing). `CLAUDE.md:301-303` still states "The web client is the behavioural reference; the phone owns operating the league, the desk owns authoring it."
- **Problem observed:** there is no statement of which client is which **now**, the CLAUDE.md line is stale and was already superseded, and the web carries at least six false facts — a toast describing a control that does not exist (`:20066`), an inverted `mine` predicate (`:10987`), credits printed as rounds (`:10877`), a solo archive reading squad standings (`:14125`), a covenant that fails open at $0 (`:17705`) — plus the hand-typed-course defect whose twin is on the phone. Separately, an earlier draft of this entry answered the question by putting the web **outside** the programme, which the owner has now revised.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** **two clients, one product, one set of producers, two shapes.** (1) **Inline, not deferred** — every wave has a phone half and a web half and **is not done until both ship**. There is no "web owed" backlog because there is no lag to owe from; every such note in the design set is struck and no new one is written. (2) **Its own shape** — the web is **not** the five-tab phone IA reflowed into a browser; it is a **sidebar and a wide two-column body**, the record a golfer sits down and browses. **Shared:** every RPC and payload, every copy producer and copy law, the terminology table and its checks, the ranking rule, the object model, every decision entry. **Not shared:** layout, density, navigation chrome, and which facts sit beside which — the same sentence is *produced once and rendered twice*. (3) **What the web leans into**, because they are its arguments for existing and none is a port: the archive, the season's story at length, the table with its history beside it, the Pro's desk and its full dials, printing and export, and the wide read on a Sunday night. (4) **Into the existing file** — built into `index.html` alongside what is there, sharing its boot, auth and data layer, **not a second web app** — respecting the six named landmines (the classic↔module boundary and its silent demo-mode failure; `switchView` as the router; `supabase-js` never throwing; mixed middot encodings; the stamped version line; Netlify's build-time allowlist). (5) **Unchanged jobs:** the signed-out door, the anon links (`?join=`, `?claim=`, `?p=`, `?plan=`), the desk's authoring dials, the public share pages. (6) **The six false facts are fixed in Wave 0**, because a client may lag and it may not lie, and the invite door gains its **App Store link**. `CLAUDE.md:301-303` is corrected in the same change.
- **Principle served:** D201's producer rule (one producer per law per client); L-44 (the app never lies); the brief's own separation of the data model from the user's model, which is enforced in producers rather than in layouts.
- **Expected user benefit:** the majority of today's real golfers stop being told things that are not true **and** get the redesign in the same wave the phone does — in a shape that uses a 1,440-px screen rather than wasting it on one column down the middle.
- **Tradeoffs:** **it is roughly sixteen additional weeks of work** (`INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §17.2 prices each half), and two shapes over one set of producers is a discipline that fails quietly the first time somebody retypes a sentence instead of importing it — which is exactly what D201 exists to prevent and what the terminology checks now guard on **both** clients. Verification for a web half is CLAUDE.md's own recipe and is not optional: serve locally, clear the service worker and caches first, drive the flow, console clean but for the one known boot rejection.
- **CONFLICT (named):** IOS-018 `DECISIONS.md:179-189` · D100 `:3633-3658` · **`CLAUDE.md:301-303`** — **this brief is the later decision.** Level 3. **And it supersedes this entry's own earlier draft**, which read "the web is a door, a desk and the anon surface, at contract parity through shared producers" and left open whether Wave 1 shipped to both clients. That question is closed: **every wave ships to both.**

### D236 · The ME strip owns my number, my last round, my next round and my money

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul (`docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md`); **R-C, as revised**, is what makes it a two-client entry — the phone gets a strip across the head of Home, the web gets the same four facts as the desk's identity block in the sidebar, produced once and rendered twice. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 1a** — `MeStripCopy` (the Kit's producer), `MeStrip.swift` (the phone), `csMeStrip()` + `#sideMe`/`#homeMe` (the web), and `native_home` v3's `profile{last_round_on, last_gross, last_round_id, days_since_round}` and `standing{next_up, next_down}`. **It ships ON today's `HomeMode` Home, which is still there**; wave 1b replaces what is under it. **Level 5 (UI).** Sources: `INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.2; D129; L-34; L-10; `Models.swift:18`; `HomeView.swift:1001-1008` (`OweAction`); HM-35 (the live door offered twice on one screen).)*

- **Current mechanic:** my number, my last round, my next round and my unpaid state are scattered — the index on You, the last round found by the client in the feed's `is_me` row, the next round in the D219 chip, the owe line in the hero foot (D129, self-only, firing from state).
- **Problem observed:** the same fact renders more than once on one screen (a buddy's personal best rendered three times in one persona walk; the live door offered twice, HM-35), and nothing on Home is reliably about *me*.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** one always-present strip of four mono facts — `YOUR NUMBER · LAST · NEXT · STILL OWE` — plus one season context row naming the season with the nearest deadline, its rank, both gaps **with names**, and the endgame clause. **No card below repeats them**, enforced by the strip publishing a `suppress: Set<Fact>` that everything under it honours. **`STILL OWE` is D129's line relocated, not demoted**: it fires from state, on every open, on an always-present surface, in `neg` and never gold, with no countdown, absent entirely at $0, and tapping it opens the books where the Pro's payment terms live. **There is no tap-cycle across memberships** — that is the switcher, reintroduced in the tightest row on the screen; with two seasons the figure is the SUM and the tap lands on the one with the nearest due date. `LiveNowBar` stands down when the live card is the lead.
- **Two rules decide every branch, and both are tested rather than asserted.** **L-44** — a fact with **no read** renders NOTHING: against a `native_home` v2 payload (the one in prod until the owner pushes the migration) the LAST slot is simply absent, because "NO ROUNDS YET" would be a lie over nine posted rounds and "—" would be a guess. **A-5** — a gap is always attached to a name: without `next_up`/`next_down` the gap clause does not render, because "4 back" with nobody on the end of it is a number a golfer cannot act on. `days_since_round` rides the payload for a *ranker* and is never rendered — "N days since you played" is the shame line L-22 forbids, and the strip prints the DATE, which is the fact.
- **Principle served:** L-34; L-10; L-14; L-44; the brief's ME layer.
- **Expected user benefit:** every open answers "why does this matter to me" in one row, and the golfer who owes $50 is told so until they have paid, without ever being shamed for it.
- **Tradeoffs:** five-plus facts in one row is a dense object inside a design that forbids dashboards. **AX3 is an acceptance test, not an afterthought**: at AX3 the four facts reflow to two rows of two and the season row wraps to three lines, nothing truncates and nothing scrolls sideways. **And the two clients pay for it differently**: the phone spends a block above the hero, the desk spends the foot of a sidebar that was carrying a league name — which is the point of two shapes over one producer, and the reason the strings are asserted on both sides rather than typed twice.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. **D129 is executed, relocated within Home, and explicitly not demoted to a once-per-condition card.** D219's next-round chip and D94's Next tile both stand down under the strip's `suppress` set rather than being deleted — they return the moment a state exists where the strip does not carry NEXT.

### D246 · One week producer — `native_home.season.week_no` is the week

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul (`docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md`); no ruling was needed on this entry itself — it rides wave 1a because R3 is that wave's migration and the week is one of its keys. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 1a:** `native_home` v3 returns `season{week_no, weeks_total, week_ends_on, days_to_first_tee, days_left, final_opens_on}`, computed on the season's OWN calendar day; `LeagueDates.week/weeksTotal/weekEnds/finalOpens` are the phone's single readers and `csWeek/csWeeksTotal/csWeekEnds` the web's. **The migration is written and unpushed**, so both clients are running on the declared fallback until the owner pushes it. **Level 4 (mechanic) + level 6.** Sources: the six-formula hazard — `snapshot_week` (0-based, day-7 start) · `open_week_clash`/`home_clash`/`settle` (1-based) · `sandbox_week` (1-based) · web `weekCloseDate` (0-based) · the web hero (1-based, `+1`) · web weeks-left (`Math.ceil`) · phone `LeagueDates.currentWeek`; L-44; D201's producer rule; D120's `STAGE_LABEL` + preflight 20 as the precedent.)*

- **Current mechanic:** "what week is it" is computed in at least six places with at least two different bases.
- **Problem observed:** the same season can be week 7 on one surface and week 6 on another, which is L-44's exact failure ("every number that counts must count something"). It is not a copy problem and it cannot be fixed by a lint.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** **`native_home.season.week_no` (and `weeks_total`, `week_ends_on`, `days_to_first_tee`, `days_left`, `final_opens_on`) is the producer.** Both clients adopt it and **stop computing**; `LeagueDates.currentWeek` and the web's `currentWeek`/`totalWeeks`/`weekCloseDate` survive **only as the declared fallback**, reachable through the one reader and documented as such, because a client that predates the migration must still render a week rather than a blank. `snapshot_week`'s 0-based history is **re-labelled at read time** (`LeagueDates.snapshotWeekLabel` / `csSnapshotWeekLabel`) and never rewritten — the snapshot's own number is the record of which window it captured. A preflight check in the shape of check 20 fails the push if either client computes a week number locally; it lands with the vocabulary suite (D249 / IOS-036), which is where the extractor that can tell a producer from a call site is built.
- **One defect was fixed on the way, and it is the reason this is a mechanic entry rather than a tidy-up.** The web's `currentWeek()` divided an **instant** difference (`Date.now() − seasonS()`) by 604,800,000, while the phone floors **calendar days**. Those two disagree by a day across a DST boundary — the same class of bug as `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')` parsing as UTC midnight, which this repo has paid for twice. The web now counts calendar days, like the server and like the phone.
- **Principle served:** L-44; D201 (one producer per law per client).
- **Expected user benefit:** the week number is the same everywhere, which is the precondition for every sentence that says "with eight to play".
- **Tradeoffs:** one more key on a payload that already loops memberships; the client must render a season with the key absent (the fallback is what it renders today). And the server's answer is computed on the SEASON's timezone rather than the device's, so a golfer travelling two timezones east sees their league's week, not their phone's — which is the correct answer and a change from what the phone showed them.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. Closes the data layer's named hazard by ruling the producer rather than by fixing the copies.

### D249 · The vocabulary ships as a table, a producer per law, and a lint per law

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 9** — the sweep, the extractor, preflight checks 27 and 28, and two migrations (`20260930090000_one_band_name.sql`, `20260930093000_the_ledger_says_the_consequence.sql`) dry-run against prod in push order and unpushed. **Level 5 (UI) + level 6.** Sources: `INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §15.5; `docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/TERMINOLOGY.md` §4 (the ship list, which supersedes §15.5's shorter one); D131; D132; D128 (2); D126 (4); D127 (1); D13; D120's `STAGE_LABEL` + preflight check 20 (the pattern); `WizardState.swift:68-72` (a live L-16 violation at tip); D201; `OWNER_RULINGS.md` R-C, which makes both clients this entry's scope.)*

- **Current mechanic:** the noun rulings are half-built, no lint guards them, and one fact is produced in many places. D131 is self-described as copy-only (~90 strings, no schema); D132 is three definition lines; D128 (2), D126 (4), D127 (1) and D13 are sentences.
- **Problem observed:** rulings that are only sentences drift back. Four of D131's retired phrasings had been written back into this overhaul's own proposed copy before anybody noticed. The proven mechanism is **one producer per client per law plus a preflight lint per law** — roughly 25 lines each, the shape of D120's stage vocabulary and check 20.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** ship the vocabulary as a table grouped ME / NOW / COMPETE / COMMUNITY / HISTORY, with a producer and a lint per law, and **cite each existing ruling as executed here rather than re-proposing it**. **Twenty-nine checks fail the push at ship** (`TERMINOLOGY.md` §4): the ten originally named, plus the seat count, the gross-target-off-another-golfer's-PvI, the fabricated event split, the SQL ledger generators, the accessibility labels and the rest. **Three corrections to the original ten, each forced by a verifier finding.** (a) **`counts on your card` becomes `\bon your card\b`**, with the *profile* sense allowlisted **by call site**: the retired *record* sense has six phrasings — *counts on · lands on · it goes on · your rounds stay on · HIT YOUR CARD · Pinned to* — and a grep for one lets the other five ship. The record sense is **"posts to your rounds"**; where nothing is lost it is **"your rounds stay where they are"**. (b) **A seat count is added** — `scheduled_rounds` has no capacity column and no read returns one, so a printed seat count is a number that counts nothing (L-44). (c) **A gross target derived from another golfer's PvI is added** — `event_session_targets` returns PvI only and the conversion needs his index *and* a course he has not chosen. **The live L-16 violation is fixed** (`WizardState.swift`): the dials stopped being nouns a golfer must learn. **Four items move out of vocabulary and are filed where they belong:** the two PvI lenses → a correctness item under D123/L-13; the six week formulas → D246; the three head-to-head implementations → R4's one read; the seven band copies → `band_name(p_pvi)` (R13, in this wave's own migration).
- **Principle served:** D201; L-33; L-34; L-43; the brief's "never need a tutorial".
- **Expected user benefit:** a golfer meets one word for one thing, defined once, and never meets a schema noun.
- **Tradeoffs, re-measured.** "Roughly 20 files with small edits" was wrong: **12 of the 27 string patterns produced ~172 Swift hits at tip**, and the sweep as built moved **~420 strings across both clients** once the web's own were counted. **Four checks need machinery `preflight.mjs` does not have** — patterns 6, 9, 10 and 12 hit **identifiers**: column lists inside `.select(…)`, property paths inside interpolation, `class="pvi …"`, a `case "duel"` on a server kind. §4's rule is "exempt by call site, not by file", so `tools/extract-strings.mjs` was built first and the lint reads PROSE rather than grepping bytes.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. D11's "league is the container" is overridden **at UI level only** by D222's naming; the data model keeps `leagues`. **One naming correction rides here:** the component checks in `COMPONENT_SYSTEM.md` are renumbered **CL-1 … CL-12**, because they were `L-1 … L-12` in a document that also cites the wall's immutable laws as `L-02`, `L-04`, `L-05`, `L-11`, `L-12` — a leading zero was the whole distinction. **`CL-n` is a component check, `L-nn` is a law, and the terminology checks are numbered separately** in `TERMINOLOGY.md` §4.

**As built, and the five things the build learned.**

**(1) THE EXTRACTOR IS THE REASON THE LINT SHIPS AT ALL.** `tools/extract-strings.mjs` reads Swift, `index.html` and SQL and returns the strings a golfer could meet, with the call each sits in: it skips comments, `Tests/`, `Generated/`, arguments to `.select(`/`.eq(`/`.rpc(`, interpolation and `${…}` spans, enum raw values and `CodingKeys`, JSON payloads, regex patterns and bare snake tokens, and it reads `.accessibilityLabel` / `.accessibilityHint` as prose (A-2). Three real parser traps were found by running it rather than by reasoning about it: a `/'/g` **regex literal** inside a template expression opened a phantom string and desynchronised 900 lines of `index.html`; an HTML comment quoting the retired words counted as six offences; and `\u2713` came back as the letter u. Each is fixed in the scanner, which is why check 27 can be trusted to read 0.

**(2) THE SQL SCOPE IS "THE LAST DEFINITION OF A GENERATOR", AND THAT IS A RULE ABOUT L-05.** A migration that has run is never edited, so the sentence that ships is the newest `create or replace`. Check 27 parses the whole tree, keeps the live definition of every function, scans only those that write a board post, a nudge or a ledger reason, and never a `raise exception` — an error message is not the ledger's voice. Seven generators were copied forward with one sentence changed each. **`start_live_round` is the reason this rule is written down**: the first cut copied the EIGHT-argument definition, which `20260830220000` had DROPPED in favour of a nine-argument one — re-creating it would have left two overloads and an ambiguous call. The dry-run against prod caught it; `select count(*) from pg_proc` now answers 1 for each of the seven.

**(3) R13 IS ONE TABLE WITH THREE RENDERERS, AND CHECK 28 IS WHAT MAKES THAT TRUE.** `band_name(p_pvi)` sits beside `cup_points` with the same half-open edges, and `round_card` returns `band` beside `pvi` — driven as the owner's own account against prod, a real round came back `pvi -2.0 · band "A little loose" · points 6`. Both clients prefer the server's word and fall back to their own producer, so either deploy order renders the same five words. Preflight 28 re-derives the table **from the migration's SQL** on every push and asserts it against `tests/fixtures/bands.json`, `CSBands.bandName` and `index.html`'s `bandName()`; proven to fail by bending the web's −1.0 edge, which is the exact drift Q-20 had to rule back once already.

**(4) THE LEDGER SAYS THE CONSEQUENCE.** `close_month` wrote `Floor 2/mo — posted 1` and `Partial edge month — floors waived` into `season_adjustments.reason`, which both clients render. It now writes *"September's rounds are struck — the minimum wasn't met."* and *"Partial month — no minimum"*. Two push bodies said *"put you on the tee sheet"* after A-8 renamed the calendar and T-03 gave the live scorer *a live round*: `invite_golfer` now says *"invited you"*, `start_live_round` says *"started a live round with you"*, and `retag_round`/`declare_round` say *"put you on the schedule"*. Four board generators lost *Rosters locked* and *Fresh slate … seeds locked*.

**(5) ONE STRING WAS NOT A COPY CHANGE AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH.** The schedule row's `LEAGUE MATE` tag becomes **IN YOUR SEASONS** rather than A-7's **IN THE FELLAS**, because `my_schedule` returns `shared_league` as a BOOLEAN and carries no league name — naming the crew needs a payload change, not a copy change. The honest tag is the one the read can support (L-44), and the naming version is a note against R-F's schedule read rather than a promise this wave made and quietly missed.
