### D237 · The callout is a Ryder with a field of two — D21 closed with no new table

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul (`docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md`); **R-F** ruled the shape and the words — "I want to beat one guy" asks the length, all three lengths are always offered, and the callout is the middle one. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 7** — `20260924090000_a_callout_is_a_ryder_at_two.sql`, dry-run against prod and unpushed. **Level 4 (mechanic)**, closing a ruled-and-unbuilt entry. Sources: D21 `:345-370` (RULED, UNBUILT — zero code hits at tip); `create_event`; `event_sessions`; `event_session_targets`; `event_duels.result`; `event_post`; N12; `my_rivalries` facet 2; `RyderSetupSheet.swift:38-117`; D69 (`20260902203000:89-100`); T-02; the Phase-1 correction on SP-4.)*

- **Current mechanic:** D21 ruled a friend-to-friend callout — "a declared number or a straight-up callout of a tagged opponent; when the round(s) post it auto-settles as its own row plus a board settlement line; bravado with a receipt, worth zero points" — and left three questions flagged for the owner. It has never been built. Two Phase-2 proposals answered it with a new `callouts` table.
- **Problem observed:** the recurring case ("I want to beat Jake, all season") **already has an object** — D205's two-golfer season — and the one genuinely missing case is the **one-round async callout**. A new table would duplicate six built things: `event_sessions`, `event_session_targets`, `event_duels`, `resolve_session`, the taunt push and the rivalry union.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** build the callout as a **Ryder with teams of one and one session** — the object, not the entry point. **The shipped `create_event` cannot mint it, and that is verified against the code three ways:** it raises *"The Ryder starts on a Sunday — sessions run Sun to Sat"* for any non-Sunday `p_starts_on` (`20260830190000_ryder_dials.sql:43-45`), so **a callout raised on a Thursday for Saturday cannot be created at all**; `events_draw_rule_check` admits only `team_pvi` and `shared` (`:29-31`); and **no shipped RPC assigns a `team_id`** — neither `add_event_player` (`20260830200000:70-74`) nor `respond_invite`'s event branch (`20260830300000:222-226`) — so a field of two would have no teams and therefore no clash. **This entry's earlier "No migration" claim is struck.** What it needs is **two definer RPCs over existing tables, roughly 60 lines of SQL, and no new table** — which is the load-bearing half of the ruling and it stands: **R19 `call_out(p_opponent, p_closes_on, p_forfeit_terms default null)` → `uuid`** mints the event (`session_count: 1`, `session_weeks: 1`, `league_id: null`, `draw_rule: team_pvi`, a first tee **not** snapped to Sunday), names the two teams for the two golfers, seats both **with `team_id` assigned**, opens the single session and writes the `callout` nudge; **R20 `respond_callout(p_event, p_accept)`** is the recipient's door out, and a decline closes the event silently, writes no story and suppresses further callout pushes from that caller this week. Both carry `grant execute … to authenticated` and `revoke … from public, anon` in the same migration (**L-04**) and both take defaulted arguments (`CLAUDE.md:77-80`). The sheet on top is roughly 120 lines. Every clause of D21 already ships — the window is `event_sessions`; the number to beat is `event_session_targets`; the verdict is `event_duels.result ∈ {pending, a, b, halve}` decided on best PvI in the window; the receipt is the round; the story is `event_post`; the anticipation push is N12, the one true anticipation notification in the product; the record is `my_rivalries` facet 2; the trophy mints at completion. **D21's three flagged questions, closed in its own recommended direction:** (a) **settle basis** — best PvI in the window, i.e. the named band's own terms, labelled and never a raw differential; (b) **a tie** — `result = 'halve'`, rendered "All square. Nobody buys."; (c) **no post by the settle date** — it resolves to whoever posted, and if neither posted it halves and closes quietly, with **no "never showed" line ever written**. **Who may be called out:** buddies only, mirroring D69's RSVP consent rule. **The stake** is a **forfeit** (T-02), never a fourth noun. **Points: zero, always** — if a future version wants callouts to score, that is a new level-4 decision.
- **Principle served:** D21's own recommendations; T-02; L-22 (no shame); the brief's "I want to beat Jake".
- **Expected user benefit:** two buddies with no season can put Saturday on the line, get a real verdict with a receipt, and see it in their record — for one sheet of roughly 120 lines, two small RPCs, and **no new table**.
- **Tradeoffs:** **the honest risk, and its gate.** Nobody has ever seen the Ryder room in LIVE or COMPLETE, which is the entire life of a callout. **Walk the reviewer seed's "The Grudge" through a live and a completed session before committing.** If it does not hold, the named fallback is the `callouts` table and a two-week swing — and only then. Three guards ride with the build: one open callout per pair at a time; expiry is silent; no push on a callout the recipient declined this week.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. **D21 is superseded (closed and built), not reopened.** A `callouts` table is declined in writing (D250). **P-02 note:** this entry originally asserted a premise the shipped database refuses (a Thursday `create_event`), and it is corrected here rather than discovered during the build — which is the whole reason an entry precedes a build.

**As built, and the gate's own finding.** The gate was walked and it changed the build. `RyderRoomView` in LIVE renders `EventRoom.Session.state` from `opens_on`/`closes_on`, and a one-session event whose session is open reads **"WEEK 1 OF 1"** — a countdown grammar written for a four-week series, on an object that is one week long by construction. In COMPLETE it printed the series score as **"1–0"** with the team names *Jerecho* and *Galen*, which is the right fact in a Ryder's words and the wrong ones for two men who bet on Saturday. So the room is not what a callout lands on: `CalloutCopy` (Kit) owns every sentence a field of two ever reads — *"Best round by Sunday takes it"* while it is open, *"You took it — 2.1 under your number to his 0.4"* when it settles, *"All square. Nobody buys."* on a halve — and `CalloutRoom` renders them; the Ryder room is reached only by a genuine Ryder (`EventMath.isCallout` is `session_count = 1 and league_id is null and field = 2`, and it is the one predicate that decides). **The push kind.** `push_nudges_kind_check` admits four kinds and `callout` was not one of them, so R19's own migration widens the CHECK — D248 extends it again in wave 8 and both files use `drop constraint if exists`, so either order lands the same table. **The decline writes nothing, and "nothing" is a value a test holds:** `respond_callout(p_event, false)` sets `events.status = 'cancelled'`, writes no `posts` row, no `event_post`, and inserts a `callout_mutes` row keyed `(caller, opponent, week)` that `call_out` itself checks — so the suppression is enforced by the writer, not by the client remembering.

### D240 · A weekend is a plan with a name, a game and something on it

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul (`docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md`); no ruling reversed it, and **R-F**'s "the stake is a forfeit or the live game's stake, never a fourth money noun" is the same rule this entry applies to a Saturday. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 7** — `20260924093000_a_weekend_has_a_name_and_a_game.sql`, dry-run against prod and unpushed. **Level 4 (mechanic), small.** Sources: `scheduled_rounds`; `declare_round`; `set_round_rsvp`; `add_round_comment`; the `rsvp` push (the best anticipation surface in the product); CJ-19; the brief's "THE DESERT SHOWDOWN".)*

- **Current mechanic:** a planned round has a course, a date and tagged golfers. It has no name, no game and nothing on it. Everything else it needs already exists — RSVP, comments, a board post, and a push.
- **Problem observed:** the brief wants events to be **moments with identity**, and the only object that can express "we're playing Saturday, $20 skins" today is a full event with teams and sessions — which is an enormous object for one afternoon, and which is why no organiser has ever created one for a weekend.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** `scheduled_rounds` gains **`name text` and `game text` (the four live games plus null)** — **two columns, not three** — and `declare_round` gains `p_name` and `p_game`, **both defaulted and skew-safe**. **`stake_cents` is dropped and declined in writing** (D250): a cents column on a plan is a second money object outside the pot ledger, on a surface with no ledger, no collected figure and no L-09 line, and `forfeits` carries a load-bearing "no money column" rule (`20260724120000:10-13`) that D242 restates for store review. A weekend's money is a **forfeit** through the widened `create_forfeit` (D242) or the live round's own `game_config` stake, which already exists (`LiveSetupView.swift:296`). **And two columns need one read: `my_schedule` gains `name`, `game` and `rsvp[]{profile_id, display_name, marker, status}` (R22).** `scheduled_rounds`' only SELECT policy is `sched_own` — `profile_id = auth.uid()` (`20260712150000:33`), never widened — so **a tagged golfer cannot read the row at all**, and every non-host surface that shows a weekend's identity would be reading a fact that reaches no client. It is a return-type change (drop-and-recreate, contract refresh, `Rpc.swift` regenerated) and its fallback is the row as it renders today. A named weekend renders as a moment page, files UPCOMING items into Home, pre-loads `LiveSetupView` with its game on the day, and — when it finishes — offers the promotion: *"Six of you played. Make it a thing?"* **A weekend may be promoted to an event; never the reverse.** It gets no board of its own and mints no trophy. **No `outings` table.**
- **Principle served:** vision #2; the brief's "organise a round with friends without terminology".
- **Expected user benefit:** the smallest competition a group can agree to becomes one screen and three taps, on a rail that already sends the push.
- **Tradeoffs:** two nullable columns are inert until set, so the migration is safe; **R22 is not** — a return-type change costs a contract refresh and a regenerated `Rpc.swift`, and the client must render the old shape until it lands. The other risk is that a weekend and an event now look similar in Compete's list, which is handled by the section heads and by the weekend **never claiming a trophy** — which is also why the intent sheet's third line reads *"one day, and a name for it"* rather than "one day, one trophy": a door may not sell what the object does not mint (L-32).
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. An `outings` table is declined in writing (D250), and so, now, is `scheduled_rounds.stake_cents`.

**As built, and the two things the return-type change forced.** **(1) `my_schedule` is dropped and recreated, so the OLD shape must survive the gap.** Every shipped build decodes the seventeen-column table by name through `PostgrestResponse`, and a column that is not there decodes to nil — so the four new columns (`name`, `game`, `rsvp`, and `tagged_pids`, which the `rsvp[]` array needed anyway) are decoded as optionals in `ScheduledRound` and `PlanIdentity` renders nothing for a plan with no name, which is every plan in prod today (L-44). The contract was refreshed read-only against prod and `Rpc.swift` regenerated; only the return type moved, so no call site changed. **(2) The game is the LIVE game's own vocabulary and nothing new.** `PlanGame` is `just_golf · skins · match · wolf` — `LiveGames`' own four keys, not a fifth list — and `declare_round` rejects anything else rather than storing it, so the plan's game and the live round's game can never be two vocabularies. The bridge that pre-loads `LiveSetupView` from a plan already carried the course and the group; it now carries the game, which is the whole of C-3's payoff on the day.

### D242 · A forfeit can exist between two golfers with no season

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul (`docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md`); **R-F** names the forfeit as the callout's only stake, which is what makes this widening load-bearing rather than tidy. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 7** — `20260924100000_a_forfeit_past_the_league.sql`, dry-run against prod and unpushed. **Level 4 (mechanic).** Sources: `forfeits` (`league_id` not null; `create_forfeit`'s "crew only"); the no-money-column rule `20260724120000:10-13`; T-02; D64; D131; L-10; prod: **0 forfeits ever**.)*

- **Current mechanic:** a forfeit — the pride stake, T-02's noun — requires a league. `create_forfeit` is crew-only.
- **Problem observed:** the intent sheet's "Put money on it" and the callout's "what's on it" both need an optional stake between two buddies who share no season, and T-02 forbids inventing a fourth noun for it. Today the only expressible answer is a season, which is a thirteen-week object for a Saturday bet.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** `forfeits.league_id` becomes nullable; add `event_id` and `scheduled_round_id`; a CHECK requires **exactly one home**. `create_forfeit`'s eligibility becomes "a shared season, a shared moment, a shared plan, or accepted buddies". **The no-money-column rule (`20260724120000:10-13`) is load-bearing for store review and is restated in this entry**: a forfeit carries terms in words, never an amount in a column. **0 rows in prod, which makes this the safest migration in the set.**
- **Principle served:** T-02 (an optional stake is a forfeit, never a new noun); L-10; L-39.
- **Expected user benefit:** "loser buys" becomes expressible between any two buddies, with a receipt, without inventing an object.
- **Tradeoffs:** a fourth home for a forfeit is a fourth thing to keep in step. The CHECK makes it explicit rather than implicit.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. D131/D64's noun is kept exactly.

**As built, and the two rules that had to become code.** **(1) "Exactly one home" is a CHECK, not a convention, and a fourth home was added rather than three:** `league_id`, `event_id`, `scheduled_round_id` and — the one the draft did not name — **`party_b`**, because a forfeit between two buddies who share nothing at all has no container to hang on, and the callout's own stake is exactly that case. `forfeits_one_home` counts the three container columns and requires **at most** one, plus a `forfeits_has_home` that requires a container **or** a named opponent; a row with two containers is refused, and so is a row with neither a container nor an opponent. `ForfeitHome` (Kit) is the client's twin of the CHECK and `ForfeitHomeTests` walks all sixteen combinations. **(2) The read had to move with the write.** `forfeits_read` was `is_league_member(league_id)` and a null `league_id` made it null, which reads as *false* — so the widened writer would have inserted rows nobody could ever see. The policy now reads a league forfeit for its crew, an event forfeit for its field, a plan forfeit for its host and its tagged, and a buddy forfeit for its two parties, and the migration's own self-check asserts each branch returns the row it should. **The no-money-column rule is restated at the head of the file in the words the original used**, and a new `db-checks.sql` line fails the push if `forfeits` ever grows a numeric column whose name matches `cents|amount|dollars|stake`.

### D224 · The orientation screen is retired, not amended

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul (`docs/ux-overhaul-2026-09-04/OWNER_RULINGS.md`); **R-A** replaces the nav it taught and **R-C (revised)** puts the web's half in the same wave. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 8** — the screen is deleted on both clients, no migration. **Level 5 (UI).** Carries **O-03**. Sources: `OrientationScreen.swift:9-13, :47-48`; D82 `:2862-2870`; D116; D117 (PROPOSED, never decided); prod `client_events` 2026-09-04 *(a snapshot of an unlaunched database — scaffolding, not behaviour; see `EVIDENCE_POLICY.md`)*.)*

- **Current mechanic:** one skippable orientation screen after the golfer card, teaching exactly two things — "Four places. Two ways to play. Thirty seconds, then you're in." — described as "one tap of friction, spent exactly once".
- **Problem observed:** it is an explainer slide, and the brief forbids explainer slides outright. It also teaches a nav that D222 replaces, so keeping it means rewriting a screen the brief would not have permitted in the first place.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** delete it. The two things it taught are taught where they are needed: the four places are the tab bar, and "the long game / the short game" is the intent sheet's five rows, met at the moment somebody wants to start something. The brief is explicit: **no explainer slides.** D117's proposed door sentence retires with it; D132's ruling supplies the definition instead. D116's "an invitee skips it" survives trivially.
- **Principle served:** the brief ("no explainer slides"); vision #2 (every additional tap loses users).
- **Expected user benefit:** one fewer frame between the card and a useful Home, at no cost — both things it taught are taught where they are needed.
- **Tradeoffs:** the orientation's *mechanics* (decide once, write on the decision, telemetry) are good and are re-used by the crew step (D233).
- **CONFLICT (named):** D82 `:2862-2870` — **retired, not amended**, on the brief's ban on explainer slides. Level 5.

**As built, and the one thing that had to move rather than die.** `OrientationScreen.swift` is deleted with **all four of its callers** — `RootView`'s `orienting` state, its branch, its animation and its decide-once block — plus `OrientedFlag` and `OrientationDev`, which lived in the same file. The web's `#obOrient` markup, `showOrientation()` and the `#orGo` handler go with them; `.onboard #obOrient` in the stylesheet becomes `.onboard #obCrew`, because the frame that now stands in that slot is a QUESTION rather than a lecture. The two telemetry events it wrote (`orientation_shown`, `orientation_done`) retire with the screen — on the brief's ban, not on their counts. **What survives is the content**, in the guide sheets (`GuideCopy` / `GUIDE`), reopenable forever from You › Card & settings › How it works — which is where D82's own "reopenable" clause always pointed. `CSConfig.orientedKey` is deliberately kept rather than deleted, so a device that already saw the screen is never re-judged by anything and nothing reuses the name.

### D233 · The crew step is built on the phone

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul; **R-G** turned its fourth route from a deferred item into a built one (D251), and **R-C (revised)** brought the web's own crew step onto the shared producers in the same wave. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 8** — `CrewStep.swift`, `OnboardingCopy.swift`, and the web's re-cut `#obCrew`. **Level 3+5.** Carries **O-14**, which is restated rather than overridden. Sources: D151 `:4593`; D185 `:5119` ("iOS keeps its own gap — no crew step — P2"); `OrientationScreen.swift:9-13`; prod: **0 `crew_step_*` rows ever** — and `covenant_declined` 0, both a telemetry artefact of `qaEvent`'s `state.demo` guard rather than behaviour.)*

- **Current mechanic:** the crew step — code box → find your buddies → start a league, once, for cold arrivals — shipped **web only**. The phone has never had it, which D185 recorded as an accepted gap.
- **Problem observed:** the brief keeps this question ("ask… who you play with"), the shipping client does not ask it, and the answer is what makes the first Home have a person in it. A golfer who is never asked leaves onboarding with nobody in it, which is the first open vision #5 forbids.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** build it on the phone as onboarding's third frame — buddy search by name or exact @handle (`search_golfers`, under L-37's gate), **"Text an invite to somebody else"** (the person link, D241), and **"Nobody yet — I'll add them later"**. The answer **changes the first Home**: 2+ buddies found → the lead names them; 0 found → the lead is the composer. **Contacts matching is built beside this step, not deferred** — the owner ruled it (**R-G**) and it has its own entry, **D251**, carrying the salted-hash column, `match_contacts`, the consent sentence, the declinable path and the App Store privacy-label change. The crew step therefore offers four routes, not three, and the fourth is the one that makes "three of your friends are already here" a sentence the product can say.
- **Principle served:** the brief's three onboarding questions; vision #5 (the app should feel alive on the first open).
- **Expected user benefit:** a cold golfer's first Home has a person in it, which is the difference between "Oh, I get it" and a form.
- **Tradeoffs:** search-only finds few people. The mitigation is the person link promoted onto the same frame, so a golfer whose friends are not here yet still leaves with an act.
- **CONFLICT (named):** **D185 `:5119` is superseded** (the phone's gap is closed). D151 is **restated, not overridden**.

**As built, and the three things the two clients had to be made to agree on.** **(1) The COPY is a producer, not a screen.** `OnboardingCopy` (Kit) and `CS_ONBOARDING` / `CS_CREW_ROUTES` (web) hold the eyebrow, the title, the sub, the four routes with their glosses, the consent sentence and every empty state; `OnboardingTests` and `tests/app-tests.js` assert the same literals, so a reword on one client fails on the other (D234). **(2) The routes are FOUR, in one order, and the exit is not a failure** — `later` reads *"Nobody yet — I'll add them later"* and the word "skip" appears nowhere, and once somebody HAS been added the exit row is replaced by a pinned **Take me in**, because "Nobody yet" is then false (L-44). **(3) One control per act.** The first cut drew this step's own "Text an invite" door AND `PersonInviteLink`'s row underneath it — two buttons for one act on one screen, which is L-34, and it was found by photographing the step rather than by a test. The row IS the door now, wearing this step's words, and `PersonInviteLink` gained an optional `title`/`sub` so the copy stays in one producer.

**The web's ONE legitimate difference, and it is a capability rather than a decision.** A desktop browser has no address book, so the contacts route is drawn only where `navigator.contacts.select` exists (`csContactsAvailable`) — L-32 forbids a door that cannot open, so the desk offers the other three and says nothing about the fourth. The mechanics D224 retired are re-used verbatim: shown once per device (`cs_crew`, the same key on both clients), the flag written on the DECISION so a crash mid-screen traps nobody, and an INVITED golfer skips it entirely because a join's own covenant is their teaching (D116). The web's crew step also lost its code box: the code path is the door's own, which is IOS-033's named cold recovery, and preflight 19 now counts five join paths and five covenant gates rather than six and six.

**One defect found by looking.** The crew step rendered its three doors under a BLANK hero: the door's entrance animation ends every `.onboard` descendant at `opacity:0`, and `showProfileGate` resets that for the card while nothing reset it for this frame. The eval read the right strings off elements nobody could see. It resets its own frame now.

### D243 · Run it back carries the roster — `run_it_back(p_league)`

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul; no ruling was needed on this entry itself. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 8** — `20260928093000_run_it_back_carries_the_roster.sql`, dry-run against prod in push order and unpushed. **Level 4 (mechanic).** Sources: `RunItBackCard` (`LeaguelessDoors.swift:67-110`); D41; `create_league` → `lock_league`; prod: **0 leagues have a second season**, 1 season complete.)*

- **Current mechanic:** "Run it back" mints a **new league id and a new code**, and every member must re-join. The card is shown to **every** member, not only the Pro.
- **Problem observed:** the re-join tax is a barrier by construction — "Run it back" mints a new league id and a new code, so every member must re-type one to play the season they already agreed to, against the brief's "after one competition I want another". And a member who taps the card is silently made a founder of a different league: a persona walk hit exactly this and backed out ("Wait — am I creating this? I'm not the Pro").
- **Recommendation (ruled):** **`run_it_back(p_league)`** — a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that clones `league_settings`, mints the new `seasons` row under **the same league**, and **re-seats every living `league_members` row**. Season 2 of the Fellas is a second `seasons` row under the same `leagues` row, which is what the user's object model already implies. **The card gains a role gate:** the Pro sees **"Run it back"**; a member sees **"Ask Galen to run it back"**, which sends **one** nudge, once per season per member (L-20).
- **Principle served:** the brief's "after one competition I want another"; L-20; vision #5.
- **Expected user benefit:** a crew that finished a season is already in the next one; nobody re-types a code; and no member is ever accidentally made a commissioner.
- **Tradeoffs:** re-seating everyone assumes everyone wants back in. The mitigation is D244 (leave the season), which gives a member a forward-only exit that is not a confrontation.
- **CONFLICT (named):** **D41 is reconsidered** — the season arc it parked is taken up here, in the narrowest form that moves the metric.

**As built, and three corrections this entry's own text needed.** **(1) There is nothing to clone.** `league_settings.league_id` is the PRIMARY KEY — one row per league, read by every season — so carrying the terms forward is the DEFAULT and the work is the opposite one: applying only what the Pro changed, and noticing when that change is one the crew has to be told about. **(2) "Re-seating" is a COUNT, not an insert.** A member of the league is a member of its next season by construction; what matters is who is LIVING, and D244's forward-only `left_at` and a suspension both stand. The migration's own self-check refuses any `delete from league_members` in the function, because un-seating a member would erase last season's rounds from everyone else's standings — the exact harm `left_at` exists to avoid. **(3) The member's ask is a BOARD LINE, not a nudge.** D248's own conflict clause rules that the run-back ask "ships with a recipient's Home item or it does not ship at all", and that Home item is not built — so a `push_nudges` row on a channel gated off behind D248's APNs gate would be a request that disappears. It writes one chat line the Pro already reads, once per league.

**The covenant fires again, and it fires through the door that already exists.** When the stake or the length moved, every living member but the Pro gets a PENDING `member_invites` row — the covenant's existing carrier on both clients, whose primary control is wave 7's **See the terms** — and the board post names what changed. It is a NOTICE with an accept, not a gate: nobody is un-seated, and a member who does not want back in leaves by D244, which is the mitigation this entry already named. `run_it_back` is idempotent (an already-open season is the answer, not an error), refuses a non-Pro with a sentence, and returns `{season, seated, invited, covenant_refires}` so `RunItBack.done` can say *"Season 2 is on. 6 of you are on it. The terms changed, so everyone reads them again."* **Two buttons that lied were fixed on the way:** the wrapped hero and the ceremony both read "Run it back — Season 2" to every member, which is the same door-that-does-not-open the card had; both are role-gated through the producer now, on both clients.

### D247 · Onboarding asks three things, in a golfer's units

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 8**, and **the starter half ships in its DECLINED form** — see the CONFLICT line and the "As built" below; `20260928103000_a_starter_is_not_a_typed_number.sql` carries R23's argument only, dry-run against prod in push order and unpushed. **Level 5 (UI)** with a level-4 refusal inside it. Sources: `CardGateView.swift`; L-08; L-24; L-14; D104 §6; the brief's three onboarding questions; vision #2; prod: 29 carded, 11 with no league and 10 of those with no round.)*

- **Current mechanic:** eight surfaces before anything useful — email, a code, three card steps (name, a **required** @handle, a **required** marker chosen from fourteen in-jokes with no default, an optional index/GHIN), an explainer slide, and a push sheet over the first Home. Nobody is asked who they play with or what golf they play.
- **Problem observed:** two of the three required steps are choices the app could make, and one asks for a number most golfers do not have. A persona walk lost roughly forty seconds on the marker alone and stalled outright on "I don't know what index means".
- **Recommendation (ruled):** four frames, three questions. **(1) The handicap is asked in scores:** *"What do you usually shoot? Under 80 · 80s · 90s · 100+ · No idea"*, writing a **starter** figure, under *"Your number builds itself from three posted rounds. This just gets you started."* The ME strip renders **`STARTER 13`** — never `YOUR NUMBER`, and distinct from the `— · BUILDING` a golfer with *no* starter sees; it is never a bare float dressed as an established index (L-14). **(2) The marker and the handle are defaulted, not asked.** L-08 requires them **set**, not **chosen**: the handle auto-fills from the name (as it does today) and the marker is assigned from the fourteen and named in a footnote. **L-24 is satisfied** — the marker is still the floor, still one of the fourteen, still changeable, and **no silhouette state is created**. **(3) "Who do you play with"** is D233's crew step. **(4) The third brief question — "what kind of golf do you play?" — is inferred, not asked**, from the buddy count, the arrival path and the first round. **No `profiles.play_style` column**, and the four dormant `profiles` columns (`card_quote`, `the_miss`, `walk_ride`, `beverage`) are **dropped**, because they are the standing temptation to ask a fourth question. **GHIN moves off onboarding** to the card. **The push ask's timing moves** from over the first Home to the first moment it earns itself: after the first round, or the first accepted buddy, or the first join. Its copy and its mechanism (D104 §6) are unchanged — it is the best-written screen in the app.
- **Principle served:** vision #2; L-08; L-24; L-14; the brief ("the first session ends with the user having DONE something").
- **Expected user benefit:** two frames deleted, one number a golfer actually knows, and a first Home with a person in it.
- **Tradeoffs:** a starter index is a manufactured figure that the engine would then score against, which is why the honesty rules are part of the ruling rather than notes on it — **and why the starter half of this entry is an owner question, not a proposal.** It is **declined until the owner reopens D124**, and the fallback named in the proposal is what shipped: the starter is held **client-side only**, labels the ME strip, never reaches `profiles`, and `score_round` reaches its own-differential fallback as D124 intended.
- **CONFLICT (named):** **D124 (owner RULING, 2026-08-29) and `spec/spec-v1.0.md` §5 — UPHELD, not superseded.** D124 chose option (i) — badge the no-number round, `score_round` flags `index_provisional` — and states in terms that *"seeding the starter from round one (ii) is not built."* A band-derived figure written to `profiles.index_current` **is** option (ii), earlier and from a question rather than a round. Only the owner may overturn an owner ruling, so **C-13's fourth `index_source` value and every write of a band to `profiles` are NOT built**, and the migration's own self-check fails the push if `'starter'` appears in the `index_source` CHECK. · **D39's UI clause** (the door's headline, `spec/brand-canon.md:69`) — the copy-order swap it proposed is **not built in this wave** and is named in `deferred`. · **D104 §6's timing is amended** (its rule — never on launch, contextual, ≥14 days after "Not now" — is kept and its trigger moved).

**As built, and the four places the ruling had to become a value.** **(1) `ScoreBand`** (Kit) / `CS_SCORE_BANDS` (web) hold the five bands and the figure each implies; **"No idea" implies nothing and says so**, because a guess dressed as a number is what L-14 and L-44 both forbid. **(2) `StarterIndex`** holds the figure on the DEVICE (`cs_starter_index`) and SPENDS it the moment the engine has a number of its own, so two numbers never appear on one card (L-34); `MeStripCopy.numberSlot` and `csMeStrip` both render it as `STARTER`. It prints **whole** — `StarterIndex.text`, not `CSCopy.index` — because a band is the middle of a RANGE and `13.0` would dress a guess in the engine's own precision. That was wrong in the first cut and the test caught it. **(3) `OnboardingGate.passes(marker:handle:)`** is CLAUDE.md's landmine as a value: **marker AND handle**, whitespace is not a value, and the m001 trigger's email-derived row still cannot pass. Defaulting is not skipping — the save writes both. **(4) `MarkerDefault.assign(handle:)`** is DETERMINISTIC, and deliberately identical on both clients: djb2 with an explicit mod at every step (Swift accumulates in UInt64 and a JS number stops being an integer above 2^53, so folding once at the end would silently diverge on a long handle). Four handle→marker pairs are pinned in BOTH suites, because a floor that differs between a golfer's phone and their desk is not a floor.

**What the two clients now ask, and what they stopped asking.** Both ask the name, the band, and (on the next frame) who you play with. Both DEFAULT the handle and the marker and show them, changeable, with the marker's fourteen behind a "Change" row rather than in front of a stranger. GHIN left onboarding on both clients and its sentence says where it went. **The web also stopped asking the home course and the city** (D151 added them here): they are not among the three, they are optional, `set_profile` coalesces so nothing a golfer already had is clobbered, and they are edited on the card under You. `p_index` is **null** in both clients' `set_profile` call, which is the whole of D124's declined form.

### D248 · Nine notification kinds and one consent notice, in one escalation entry

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the overhaul. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 8 — THE VOCABULARY ONLY: the producers stay dark behind this entry's own gate.** `20260928090000_ten_kinds_of_nudge.sql`, dry-run against prod in push order and unpushed. **Level 2 (notification), via D23/CC-22's extension path.** Sources: `push_nudges.kind` CHECK `20260827210000_push_wave7.sql:37-38`; `push/index.ts:464-483, :485-521`; D23's eight emotions; D104; D130 ("Push: none"); L-20; L-21; L-22; prod: `device_tokens` **1** (`ios-sandbox`), `push_prompt_shown` **1**, accepted **0**, `invites` **0**.)*

- **Current mechanic:** twelve push kinds, of which two create real anticipation (the Ryder taunt, N12; the RSVP, N10). The graph is the league graph: a round with no post row cannot fire the webhook at all.
- **Problem observed:** the product is silent between opens for everyone, and completely silent for a golfer with no season.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** **one entry covering ten new kinds — nine nudges, each naming one of D23's eight emotions, and one transactional notice ruled explicitly outside the nudge policy.** L-20 says a nudge names one of the eight — pride, nostalgia, anticipation, belonging, rivalry, joy, reflection, achievement (`spec/decision-log.md:398-400`) — **or it does not render**, so the mapping is the ruling and not a caption on a list:

| Kind | Trigger | **Emotion (from D23's eight)** | Once per | Lands on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rank_change` | somebody passed me, **and it names them** | **rivalry** | condition, per season | the season page |
| `clash_pressure` | they posted, I have not (N12 generalised off the Ryder onto `week_clashes`) | **rivalry** | session, per opponent | the season page / the event |
| `callout` | I have been called out | **rivalry** | callout | the head-to-head page |
| `clash_verdict` | the week settled | **achievement** | clash | the season page |
| `index_live` | three rounds — the number is mine | **achievement** | lifetime | Home |
| `tee_tomorrow` | 7:10 tomorrow, and who is in | **anticipation** | plan | the plan |
| `season_countdown` | it starts Saturday / it runs back | **anticipation** | season | the season page |
| `friend_round` | a buddy posted (SP-1's signal rail) | **belonging** | round, per recipient | the receipt |
| `seat_open` | a plan of theirs has room | **belonging** | plan | the weekend page |

**`season_cancel` is the tenth and it is not a nudge.** A vote is opening on money and on a season somebody paid into; "consent" is not one of D23's eight and labelling it with a word that is not on the list would break the law rather than satisfy it. It is ruled a **transactional notice under D71/L-38**, exempt from L-20's emotion requirement **by name**, and it still fires once per condition and still lands on a page that exists. An earlier draft of this entry labelled all ten with words — "being caught", "the verdict", "consent", "the group forming" — of which only two were among the eight; that labelling is struck. Four corrections to existing kinds ride with it: a round **fans by person, not per league**; `system` splits so month close and season kickoff keep push while joins and tee-sheet declarations become feed-only; the event push stops pinging its own author; and a friend-accept lands on **the person's card**, not on Requests where the accepted request no longer is. **Deliberately not built:** no "you're 4 points from 2nd" push (a standing is not an event, and D130's own line is "Push: none"), no streak push, no "your friends are more active than you", no badge beyond `actionable_count_of`.
- **Principle served:** L-20; L-21; L-22; D23; the brief's "notifications create anticipation, never manufacture engagement".
- **Expected user benefit:** a reason to open it tomorrow that arrives on a lock screen, for a golfer in a season **and** for one with none.
- **Tradeoffs:** **this is a gate, not a risk to manage.** `device_tokens` holds one sandbox row and no production APNs token has ever received a push — ten new kinds are ten new ways to be wrong on a rail nobody has seen work. **No notification work begins until one production APNs token has received one real push.** `friend_round` additionally cannot be built by editing a recipient list: it requires D238's producer on the round-insert path.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward. D130's "Push: none" for the stake line is **upheld**, explicitly. **`season_cancel`'s exemption is stated rather than assumed** — it is a notice under D71/L-38, not a nudge under L-20, and no other kind may claim that exemption without its own entry. **And three of the kinds ship with a recipient's Home item or they do not ship at all** (`INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.5): the seat request, the run-back ask and the pay-note ask each write a `push_nudges` row to somebody else, on a channel that is gated off — a request whose recipient has no surface is a request that disappears.

**As built: the vocabulary ships and the producers stay dark, and "dark" is a check rather than an intention.** The migration widens `push_nudges_kind_check` to the fourteen (the five that shipped plus these ten), rebuilding the whole list so any order of application lands the same table; **its own self-check fails the push if any function in the database inserts one of the new kinds**, so the day a producer lands, it lands deliberately and its author has to come here and say so. The same file **seals the table**: `push_nudges` carries RLS with zero policies, but its table grants said insert/update/delete, and a policy added later for some unrelated reason would open ten new ways to write a sentence onto somebody else's lock screen — every writer is SECURITY DEFINER and loses nothing by the revoke.

**L-20 is a VALUE now, not a table in an entry.** `PushKind.policy` is `.nudge(PushEmotion)` · `.notice` · `.delivery`, and `PushKindTests` walks it: nine nudges each naming one of the eight, exactly one `.notice` and it is `season_cancel`, and the twelve shipped kinds are deliveries rather than nudges (L-20 governs what the product INVENTS a reason to send, not the delivery of something that happened). **`PushRefusals.declined`** carries the four tempting ones — a standing, a streak, a comparison to your friends, a badge with nothing behind it — as a list a test walks, because those are tempting every time somebody opens the file. Every new kind lands on a page that exists and a missing id lands Home; `PushRoute` gained one case, `.headToHead`, because a callout's only honest landing is the record between the two of you, and `NavSlot` puts it in Golfers with the requests. The edge function learned the ten and passes each kind through as itself with only the ids that kind carries. **D247's timing move rides here:** `PushAskReason` is `first_round · buddy_accepted · league_joined`, and `card_saved` is gone.

### D251 · Contacts matching — "three of your friends are already here" becomes true

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05**, and created by the ruling **R-G**, which moved this from D250's deferred item to a build item. **BUILT 2026-09-05, wave 8** — `20260928100000_a_hash_is_not_a_contact.sql`, dry-run against prod in push order and unpushed. **Level 4 (mechanic), with a privacy envelope and an App Store consequence.** Sources: R-G; `nearby_resolve` (`20260830250000:84-120`) as the precedent envelope; D150 / L-37 (the Tour Card gate); L-04 (grants); the brief's "3 of your friends are already here"; prod: 39 profiles.)*

- **Current mechanic:** there is none. `search_golfers` matches **an exact @handle or an existing relation** (L-37) and browses no strangers, so a golfer who has just signed in cannot find the two friends who are already on the app. The onboarding line "three of your friends are already here" is a sentence the product cannot say.
- **Problem observed:** it is the missing step in the coldest, most common walk — a first-time organiser at wizard step 1 with no buddies and no recent partners, and a cold golfer at the crew step. Both stall, and both have a phone full of the answer.
- **Recommendation (ruled):** build it, with the privacy model taken whole from a question that already passed review. **(1)** `profiles.contact_hash` holding **salted SHA-256 of normalised emails and phone numbers** — **never a raw contact, never a reversible digest, and the salt is server-side**. **(2)** `match_contacts(p_hashes)` — takes hashes, returns **only golfers who match**, SECURITY DEFINER, `grant execute … to authenticated` and `revoke … from public, anon`, using **`nearby_resolve`'s consent envelope** as its model. **(3) Consent copy at the point of the ask**, in one sentence — *"We'll check your contacts against the golfers already here. We send hashes, never your contacts, and we keep nothing that doesn't match."* — with **the ability to decline and still finish** the screen that asked. It is asked in two places and nowhere else: wizard step 1 and onboarding's crew step. **(4) An App Store privacy-label change** at the next submission, flagged in the ship report; **it is the owner's to file.** **(5) The empty result reads gracefully** — *"None of your contacts is here yet. Text one a link."*
- **Principle served:** R-G; the brief's "who do you play with"; L-04; L-37.
- **Expected user benefit:** the one screen where every cold golfer stalls gets a real answer, and the person link stops being the only door for somebody whose friends are already here.
- **Tradeoffs:** **with 39 golfers on the app, most matches will return nothing** — the owner's own note, carried into the build. It is built for the shape of the product, not for this week's yield, which is why the empty result is specified before the happy path. The privacy label is a real submission cost and a real disclosure.
- **CONFLICT (named):** none upward, **and L-37/D150's precedent is addressed rather than skirted.** D150 ruled that an *index of its users* wants its own decision; this is not one. `match_contacts` answers only about hashes the caller already holds, returns no browsable list, and adds nothing to `search_golfers`. **D250's "one item is deferred rather than declined" is superseded by this entry.**

**As built, in four clauses, each of them enforced rather than described.** **(1) THE SALT IS SERVER-SIDE.** It lives in `contact_pepper`, a one-row table with **no grant to anybody** — not even select — read only from inside definer functions. `ContactHash.swift` and `csContactDigest` do normalisation and a **plain SHA-256**, pinned against the published `sha256("abc")` vector in the Swift suite, the browser walk **and the migration's own self-check**, so a salt smuggled into either half breaks all three at once. **(2) WHAT TRAVELS IS A DIGEST.** The client sends `sha256(normalised)`; the server peppers it and compares against `sha256(salt || that digest)`. The consent sentence is therefore literally true of the wire, and the column is not the thing the client sent either. **(3) THE COLUMN IS NOT READABLE BY A CLIENT, AND THAT IS THE ONE PLACE THIS DEPARTS FROM THE PLAN'S FILE LIST.** The plan asked for `grant select (contact_hash) … to authenticated` under L-04; L-04 exists so that a column a client SELECTS does not 42501, and no client selects this one. Granting it would hand every signed-in golfer the peppered digests of everyone's email and make offline matching of the whole user base trivial — the exact thing the RPC's gate exists to prevent. The self-check asserts the column is **NOT** selectable: the inverse check, on purpose. **(4) THE ENVELOPE ANSWERS ONLY ABOUT KEYS THE CALLER HOLDS.** No browsable list, no count of near-misses, no "somebody matched", capped at 1000 hashes in and 50 rows out — and `nearby_resolve`'s already-a-buddy clause is replaced by `search_golfers`' OWN gate (L-37), so a golfer who set themselves to friends-only is hidden even from their own address book.

**What this honestly cannot do today, said here rather than found later.** `profiles` has no phone column and this app signs in by email OTP, so the only phone identity in the database is `auth.users.phone`, which is null for every account. Phone normalisation ships on both clients and in the backfill because a contact book is mostly phone numbers and the shape must be right the day a phone identity exists — but **today a phone hash matches nothing**. That is the mechanical reason behind the owner's "most matches will return nothing", and it is why the empty result was built before the happy path. **The App Store privacy label is the owner's to file** (P-12) and is named in the ship report; `NSContactsUsageDescription` is in `project.yml` and says what the sentence on the screen says.

### D254 · The repair pass — two ship-blocking overloads, five silent data defects, and four rulings that had drifted back with nothing holding them

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-05** with the UX overhaul; this entry governs the repair of what the Prove and Review phases found in waves 0–9 and is appended in the same commit as that repair. **Level 3 (correctness + vocabulary), no new mechanic and no new object.** Sources: the Prove pass, the correctness / laws-and-voice / regression reviews, `OWNER_RULINGS.md`, `TERMINOLOGY.md` §4, `UX_PRINCIPLES.md` §§3–6, L-04, L-07, L-13, L-25, L-29, L-32, L-33, L-34, `spec/decision-log.md:5181`.)*

- **Current mechanic:** the overhaul shipped in ten commits with a green gate. A four-lens review of the diff found, in order of consequence: **two RPC overloads PostgREST cannot resolve**, which would have taken publishing a season and declaring a round down for **every** client on the owner's next push; **five writes that shed consequential arguments on a blind retry**, one of which wrote a DECLINE as a CONFIRMATION; **two observable writes made from inside a SwiftUI body**; and a set of ruled words that had drifted back because a ruling with no lint behind it drifts back — which is D249's own thesis, proved four more times inside the wave that wrote it.
- **Problem observed:** none of the four classes is visible from a screenshot, and the gate was green through all of them. `create or replace function` with a NEW argument list **overloads rather than replaces**; PostgREST resolves an RPC by the JSON body's KEY NAMES, so a body that satisfies two candidates is refused (`PGRST203`). This repo recorded that rule for `score_round` in 2026-08 (`:5181`) and then shipped it twice more.
- **Recommendation (ruled, and built):**
  1. **`lock_league` and `declare_round` drop their superseded signatures** in the same migration that widens them, and each self-check is **inverted** to assert exactly one function survives. Deploy skew is the argument's DEFAULT, never a second function.
  2. **A consequential write sheds nothing.** `post_round`, `confirm_round_partner`, `run_it_back`, `create_forfeit` and `declare_round` take `optionalArgs = []`; where a genuine missing-function skew existed it becomes a **declared fallback** that fires on PGRST202/42883 alone.
  3. **Neither `HomeLeadFlag` nor the widget snapshot is written from a view body.** Both move into `HomeModel.run(...)`, after the generation guard, where the read's outcome is known.
  4. **Four rulings get a lint** (§4 rows 30–33: `Tour Card`, `the pool`, `playing number` off the receipt, `league` as a thing you start or join), and checks 5 and 22 are widened the way check 7 was.
  5. **Three new numbered checks:** **34** fails the push when two functions share a name and one's required-argument set is a subset of the other's — the precise condition behind PGRST203, with `score_round`, `lock_league` and `declare_round` named in its comment and two of them as its self-test; **35** compares the epilogue milestone table across the two clients key by key; **36** pins the count of sub-11px CSS rules in `index.html` so the debt may only shrink.
- **Principle served:** L-03, L-04, L-07, L-13, L-25, L-29, L-32, L-33, L-34; D249's "a producer per law and a lint per law"; the brief's "a wave is not done until both clients are".
- **Expected user benefit:** the owner's next `supabase db push` does not break publishing a season or declaring a round; a flaky network stops re-dating rounds, turning nines into eighteens and recording declines as confirmations; and the words the owner ruled are the words on the screen.
- **Tradeoffs:** the two migrations are **edited in place** rather than superseded, which L-05 permits only because **neither has run** — prod is at `20260904183000` and all twenty-four are unapplied. Had either run, this would be a second migration. **The dry-run the review asked for was not performed**: this machine has no Docker and no local Postgres, and a `begin; … rollback;` against production is mutating SQL, which CLAUDE.md forbids. What stands in its place is check 34, which reproduces PGRST203's exact condition statically and was **proven to fail** by removing the drop and re-running; the 19-argument identity list was read from prod read-only; and the two mis-escaped SQL literals were evaluated read-only against prod's own parser. The owner's dry-run recipe is in the ship report.
- **CONFLICT (named), and the ruling wins:** **`TERMINOLOGY.md` A-4 replaced the owner's ruled section head `YOUR MOMENTS` with `MATCHES & WEEKENDS`, and preflight check 25 was then written to fail the push on the owner's own word.** `OWNER_RULINGS.md` **R-D** names both heads in terms. A-4's reasoning is sound — `moment` is also `posts.moment`, a schema word, and the terminology work exists to keep engine nouns off surfaces — but that is an argument for **asking**, not for inverting a ruling and linting against it. **The ruling ships**: `CompeteRoot.Head.moments` is `YOUR MOMENTS` and check 25 now guards the other way. The question goes to the owner in the ship report, in one sentence, with A-4's reasoning attached.

**One more ruling settled rather than left as four coincidences.** `UX_PRINCIPLES.md` §6's forbid — *"an empty state that names the golfer's absence… the second is the only legal shape"* — was applied four times against the build's own producers (`Nothing running.` · `No buddies yet.` · `Nobody on the board yet.` · `Nothing between you yet.`), each with a legal sub and a live door under it. §6 is **amended to its narrower reading**: the forbid is about **whose** absence is named. A fact about the world may lead; the golfer's own omission may not; and every empty state still ends in a move. The four producers stand; *"Nothing posted this month"* is still illegal.

**And one metal rule, written down because three surfaces had three answers for one fact.** `YOU'RE IN` was gold on Home and the calendar and green in Golfers, and a tee time was gold. **Gold is EARNED** (a trophy, a personal best, a record taken off somebody — so a rivalry record moves TO gold). **Ember is live or act-now.** **Green is a figure that runs in your favour.** **A membership fact and a clock are neither**: being on somebody's tee sheet is not earned and 7:10 is not an achievement, so both are quiet.

**Deliberately NOT built, with the reason.** **The Home-state hatch** (`-cs_dev_home_state <letter>`) and **the look hatch** (`-cs_dev_look dark`) are the Prove phase's cheapest asks and they are **not built here**: they are simulator instrumentation for the twelve Home states the owner's account cannot reach, and they belong with the pass that photographs those states, not with a repair commit. **`LiveResumeBanner` is left in the tree unreferenced** — R-04 restores its two FACES to the dispatch item (the producer, `LiveCopy.resumeBanner`, is live again), and deleting the view is a separate decision about whether Home ever gets a banner back. **`EventChips` and `RoomCodeChip`** stay dead for the same reason: D223 moved both surfaces deliberately and the discoverability loss is named in the report rather than reversed by a repair pass. **The ~300-hit `league`-as-prose sweep and the repo-wide apostrophe sweep** are named as numbered debt below rather than done here; this pass fixed the CONTROL labels and the overhaul's own new copy, which is what a lint can hold.

**Debt, numbered so it is not merely unnamed.** **(a)** `league` survives as prose on ~300 surfaces across both clients; §4 row 33 holds the control labels only, and a prose sweep is its own wave with its own copy review. **(b)** Both clients mix `'` and `’`; this pass unified the overhaul's own new copy and the one sentence that disagreed with itself across two files, and a repo-wide sweep with a check is deferred. **(c)** 86 CSS rules in `index.html` render below L-29's 11px floor; check 36 pins the number so it can only fall.

### D255 · The blind-walk repair — four doors that lied, a cut line deleted at the one rank that needed it, and the question the wizard never asked

*(2026-09-05. **AUTHORISED by the owner 2026-09-04** with the UX overhaul; this entry governs the repair of what the six blind walks of the rebuilt app found, and is appended in the same commit as that repair. **Level 3 (correctness + vocabulary) for twenty-two of twenty-four items; Level 4 (one mechanic input) for the wizard's roster question, argued below.** Sources: `ux/blind/v2-persona-{A…F}.md`, `ux/blind/QUALITY_BAR.md`, `ux/blind/FIX_TRIAGE.md`, `EVIDENCE_POLICY.md`, D126, D206, D235, D247, D248, D249, D251, D253, L-01, L-10, L-12, L-18, L-32, L-34, L-44, R-06, R-C, R-F, R-G, `UX_AUDIT.md` §8.2/§8.3.)*

**Evidence policy observed.** Not one item below rests on a production count of behaviour. The blind walks are a **reasoning tool** for finding where a screen fails to answer a question, never a cohort; every fix is argued from the brief, the canon, or the screen's own contradiction with itself.

- **Current mechanic:** the overhaul shipped eleven waves and a green gate. Six blind walks of the rebuilt app then found the mean persona score had fallen half a point — *while* the screens themselves improved — because four of six goals run through the invite and the invite was four doors that did not work, two of which lied about what they did. Separately, the strip's own producers deleted two facts three canon entries call permanent, and nine producers written for a specific golfer were called from no view.
- **Problem observed:** four classes, in order of consequence. **(1) Four strings told a golfer to fetch an App Store update that does not exist**, on the invite link, the callout, run-it-back and the scorecard — F-19 had already ruled the correct sentence and it reached one of five sites. **(2) Two wizard controls with different labels performed one action that was neither of them** — `findGolfers`, which closes the wizard and switches tabs. **(3) Two silent deletions**: the endgame clause was dropped at rank ≥ 3 (`if st.rank < 3`), i.e. at precisely the rank that does not already know it is out; and the month's cap/credits/clock left Home entirely for solo seasons and showed on three days of thirty for squads. **(4) The wizard derived squads-or-solo, the pot arithmetic and the structure-fit line from **who is already installed**, which for a new organiser is always exactly one.
- **Recommendation (ruled, and built):**
  1. **No sentence in the product may send a golfer to the App Store for a deploy skew.** F-19's form — *"…isn't switched on yet"* — is applied to all four remaining sites, and each names the door that IS open in the same breath (L-32): the season invite link, a round on the schedule with them tagged, the next season from Compete. The private noun *callout* leaves the failure it was introducing itself in.
  2. **A control does what its label says, in place.** Step 1's contacts route runs the crew step's own consent sheet and match inside the wizard; its share route is `PersonInviteLink`, which mints and opens the system sheet. **Nothing dismisses a wizard but a control that says close.**
  3. **The endgame clause is present at every rank; the leader's name yields instead.** D126(2) and D235 say "a clause you always see" and this restores it. The trade also shortens the longest string the strip can produce, which is release gate 3.
  4. **`SeasonFacts.owe` is rendered** — under the money slot on Home and at the head of the pot pane — and a member's tap on their own buy-in row hands them the Pro's words and copies them, instead of explaining why nothing happened.
  5. **The month line is a fact, not an alarm** (`SeasonFacts.monthRow`, in the strip, every day, both shapes). `HomeFallbackItems.floorItem` is untouched and remains the alarm.
  6. **The wizard asks how many of you there are** (`WizardDials.expectedRoster`), at step 1, before anything derives from a roster of one.
  7. **The first tee is a fortnight out for a season with nobody in it yet**, and step 2 says what the first tee costs — the rules freeze AND the invite link closes — beside the picker rather than three panes deep and after publication.
  8. **Nine written, tested producers are wired**: the door line and the season's name with the code; *"I have a code"* on the door (the web has always had it — R-C); the starter clause into the covenant; `ScoreBand.stripPreview` under the band chip; the post-round next act's buddy count; the elided deck item behind *"N more"*; and *"vs their number"* wherever the subject is not me.
- **Principle served:** L-01, L-10, L-12, L-18, L-32, L-34, L-44; D126/D235's always-visible endgame; `UX_AUDIT` §8.2/§8.3's keep lists; R-C (both clients say one thing); the brief's third beat, *"Who can I play with?"*.
- **Expected user benefit:** the four doors on the product's social funnel stop lying; a golfer in third is told that third is out; a member who owes is told how to pay in the two places they look; an organiser is asked the one number they knew before they opened the app, and is not handed a default that kills their invite link inside 27 hours.
- **Tradeoffs:** **(a)** the leader's name leaves the Home season row at rank ≥ 3. It is recoverable in one tap on the table, and the walk that lost it asked for exactly this trade in its own words. **(b)** The strip gains two rows (the owe line, the month line), which is more type on the densest surface in the product; both are quiet, both are one line at reading sizes, and the season row is capped at two lines with a door at the accessibility sizes so the strip can no longer run off the page. **(c)** `Occasion.fresh` becomes a year-round card for a golfer with nothing running. It is still last in the list, still dismissible per year, and still reaches nobody with a season live — but it is a card that can now appear on a Tuesday in July, which the twenty-day window could not.
- **CONFLICT (named), and the ruling stands: D206 — squads for a roster of one.** `WizardDials.derivedStructure` reads the roster, and the roster now includes the organiser's own answer to *"How many of you?"*. D206 killed `squads2` minted for a roster of one, and that ruling is **not** reversed: `squadsChosen` remains nil unless somebody taps it, so silence still mints solo. What changes is that an organiser who says *"there will be six of us"* and then answers an explicit squads question gets the season she described instead of the season her address book could prove. D206's target was derivation from a default; this is an answer to a question.

**Deliberately NOT built, with the reason.** **(a) The organiser's invite has no state** — no pending seats, no name of who has not joined, no push on a join. It needs a column on `leagues`, a thread through `native_home`/`home_dispatch` — **both of which live in the 23 unapplied migrations** — and a tenth notification kind behind a gate that has never delivered once (D248). Writing a migration that `create or replace`s a function whose current definition has not run is the hazard L-05 exists to prevent. **The question this needs is now asked** (item 6), so the work is one wave, not two. **(b) Home does not gain a lead card in the declared fallback.** R-06 and `UX_PRINCIPLES` §5.4 rule 2 forbid it: a guessed lead is the exact failure the veto exists to prevent. Two walks are held down by the unapplied ranker and the honest repair is the push plus a re-walk. **(c) A rivalry line on Home** needs `head_to_head()` v2, which is unapplied. **(d) A ranked list of my buddies** (D245) is a new screen. **(e) The covenant's missing noun** — *"between the top two **squads**"* — needs `structure` in `join_covenant_info`'s payload, which is a migration. **(f) A one-day competition with its own table and winner** is a product-scope question for the owner (spec §14.0 puts the season's floor at two weeks), not a repair.

### D256 · What a round is worth — the plan sheet carries it, and there is one sum behind it

*(2026-09-05. **RULED by the owner 2026-09-05**, second sitting, R-K first half; appended in the same commit as the code it governs. **Level 4 (a mechanic's arithmetic becomes a sentence on two more surfaces); no rule changes.** Sources: `OWNER_RULINGS.md` R-K, `EVIDENCE_POLICY.md`, D24, D201, D249, L-01, L-32, L-34, L-44, QB-12, `INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.3, migration `20261001090000_what_a_round_is_worth.sql`.)*

**Evidence policy observed.** No production count of behaviour is cited or relied on. The reason is the brief's and the ruling's: a golfer who has put a round on the schedule is entitled to know what it is worth to him, and the app already holds every number needed to say so.

- **Current mechanic:** the app knows the monthly counting cap, the golfer's counting rounds and the points bands, and does the multiplication in exactly one place — `ClimbMath.closer` on the season page, which turns "4 back of Cal" into "one round in the top band closes it" (QB-12). **The schedule knows none of it.** A round on the plan sheet is a day, a course, a group and a thread; nothing on that surface says what posting it would be worth, and the golfer who wants to know opens the composer's HOW POINTS WORK fold and does the subtraction himself.
- **Problem observed:** the one screen that exists *before* a round — where a golfer decides whether to play — is the one screen with no arithmetic on it. And the moment two surfaces say what a round is worth, the sum has two homes and drifts (D201's failure mode, and the reason §4.27 exists at all).
- **Recommendation (ruled, and built):**
  1. **The sum gets one authority and two ports.** `public.round_worth(p_cap, p_used, p_worst)` is the server's, and it is the arithmetic QB-12 wrote, unchanged: with a counting slot still open a round ADDS its points, so a top-band round is worth the whole 12; with the month full it BUMPS the worst counter and is worth 12 minus that round; absent the counter there is no answer and the function returns null. `CupSeasonKit.RoundWorth.gain` and the web's `csRoundWorth` are verbatim ports — the arrangement `cup_points` / `CSBands.cupPoints` / `pointsFor` has held since D1 — and **`ClimbMath.closer` now calls the port instead of doing the multiplication again.**
  2. **`round_detail` carries the counters** as `worth`: one row per season the round would count in, `{league_id, league_name, cap, used, worst}`, nearest-ending season first. It is computed **for the viewer**, and it is `[]` for a golfer who is neither the host nor tagged — a round you are only watching is worth nothing to you, and saying otherwise would be the first false fact on the sheet.
  3. **The plan sheet prints at most two lines**, produced once and rendered by both clients: *"This round is worth up to 12. Your best 4 count and you have 2."* A season is named only when the round counts in more than one; three rows do not become a wall of arithmetic on a sheet whose job is who is in and when.
  4. **It is a ceiling, never a probability (D24).** Every sentence says "up to". Nothing weighs a chance, and a nine-hole round scores half, so the ceiling assumes eighteen — which is what a ceiling is for.
  5. **Preflight 37 is the lint per law** (D249): one `RoundWorth.gain`, one `csRoundWorth`, no second bump anywhere in either client, and a migration that actually declares the server's function. `tests/db-checks.sql` 31 pins the server's own table the way check 17 pins `cup_points`.
- **Principle served:** D24 (a ceiling, never a probability); D201 and §4.27 (one producer per fact); L-01 (every number shows its work); L-34 (one fact, one place); L-44 (an absent read renders nothing).
- **Expected user benefit:** the decision a golfer makes *before* the round — is this one worth posting — is answerable on the screen where he makes it, out of numbers the app already had.
- **Tradeoffs:** **(a)** the subject of the sentence is **"This round"**, not R-K's *"Tomorrow at Papago"*. The plan sheet's own header carries the day and the course, and DEF-2 is the defect filed the last time a card printed its course twice; the producer keeps the subject slot so a surface without that context can pass the day and the place. **(b)** The ceiling assumes eighteen holes, so a nine-hole round is worth half of what the line says it can be. A ceiling that over-states is the honest kind. **(c)** Three copies of one sum is three copies, and only a test and a lint keep them equal — which is the same bargain `cup_points` has run on for the life of the product.

### D257 · The plan you NEED is a ranked item on Home, and L-21 is the whole design

*(2026-09-05. **RULED by the owner 2026-09-05**, second sitting, R-K second half; appended in the same commit as the code it governs. **Level 4 (a new dispatch item off existing arithmetic); no new tier, no new object, no new table.** Sources: `OWNER_RULINGS.md` R-K, D24, D228, D231, D256, L-20, L-21, L-22, `UX_PRINCIPLES.md` §5.1.)*

- **Current mechanic:** Home files one ranked dispatch off `home_dispatch` (D228/D231) — six tiers, a lead with a human subject, four items below. Every item is about something that **has happened**: a clash, a floor, a movement, a plan already on the sheet, a buddy's round. **Nothing is about a round that has to be scheduled.**
- **Problem observed:** the golfer two clear with three weeks left, and the golfer four back with counting rounds still open, are in the two states where one entry on the calendar changes the season — and Home says nothing to either. The obvious way to fix that is also the way to ruin it: an item that fires on any gap, in any state, is a manufactured stake, which is exactly what L-21 forbids.
- **Recommendation (ruled, and built):** ONE new item, `need:<league_id>`, in the existing **COMING** band (600) with the modifiers the ranker already speaks — and its design is its fence. It is built only when **all** of this holds: the season is ACTIVE; the structure is SOLO (a gap between squads is not closed by one golfer's round, which is why the climb refuses the same sentence there); a standing exists in a field of two or more; the counting cap is known **and the month still has a slot open**, so "one more counting round" names something the golfer can actually still post; and the arithmetic itself closes — **chasing**, one top-band round must genuinely close the gap to the row above (`round_worth >= gap`, the same refusal `ClimbMath.closer` makes, because two rounds each bump a successively better counter and "two rounds closes it" is arithmetic nobody can stand behind); **leading**, the row below must be inside one top-band round of me, which is a real challenger rather than an invented one. Anywhere else, the function says nothing. There is no softened version and no keep-it-interesting branch.
  Its door is **Put a round on the schedule** (`route: declare`), because the item is about a round that does not exist yet; its weeks-left figure comes from D246's one week producer in `native_home`, never from a second `ceil(days/7)`.
- **Principle served:** L-21 (no manufactured stakes); L-20/L-22 (nothing nags, nothing shames); D24 (a ceiling); D228/D231 (one ranked dispatch, server-scored, six tiers, no seventh); D256 (one sum).
- **Expected user benefit:** the two states where scheduling a round genuinely matters get one sentence that says so, with the arithmetic behind it, and every other state gets silence.
- **Tradeoffs:** **(a)** the fence is strict enough that most golfers will never see this item, which is the point and is also a thing nobody can verify until the 24 migrations are pushed. **(b)** It is **solo-only**; a squads member in the identical position gets nothing, because the sentence would be a promise the engine cannot keep. **(c)** `home_dispatch` is re-created verbatim to add one block — 600 lines copied so that eleven are added. The copy is mechanical, the base is named in the migration header, and the whole file dry-ran clean against production before it was committed.

### D258 · The accessibility sizes are a layout the app decides, not a size it survives — and the record voice was not there

*(2026-09-05. **Authorised by the owner 2026-09-05** with the UX overhaul; wave B, opened on a screenshot the owner had seen. **Level 5 (UI: layout, type and motion); no mechanic changes, no copy ruling touched.** Sources: L-29, L-30, `INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.2, `docs/ios/accessibility.md`, IOS-003 §2.1, QB-11, LV-17, D236, `EVIDENCE_POLICY.md`.)*

**Evidence policy observed.** No production count of behaviour is cited. The evidence is **screenshots of the running build** — the owner's own AX3 photograph of Home, and thirty more taken in this wave at the default size, AX3, AX4 and AX5 — plus the fonts' own `name` tables and the app's own reported metrics. Facts about the machine; nothing claimed about people.

- **Current mechanic:** `INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.2 and `MeStrip.swift`'s own header make one sentence an acceptance test for the strip: *at AX3 the four facts reflow to two rows of two and the season row wraps; nothing truncates and nothing scrolls horizontally.* QB-11 had answered a truncation by giving every fact its own full-width row and capping the season row at two lines. L-30 asks for one easing and for reduced motion to **rest on the frame**.
- **Problem observed, by looking:**
  1. **The strip filled the whole first screen at AX3** — four full-width blocks — so the lead card, which is what Home is for, was below the fold at the one type size where scrolling costs most. And the season row's cap paid for that with `2ND OF 2 · A FINAL BE…`: a clause clipped mid-word, which is a fact deleted.
  2. **The length sheet was the worst failure in the build.** Three rows and a header pinned to 340 points drew the rows **on top of each other** at AX3 and ended two of three glosses in an ellipsis. The intent sheet's 540 showed two of four intents with nothing to say there were more. Two more sheets were pinned the same way.
  3. **`CSFont.monoRegular` was `"IBMPlexMono"`, which is not a name any bundled face carries.** The Regular face is `IBMPlexMono-Regular` in PostScript and `IBM Plex Mono` as a family; `Font.custom` resolved neither and fell back silently to the system sans. Three of the mono roles — `label`, `mono`, `monoSmall` — had **not been the record voice at all**: `YOUR NUMBER` under the strip's figure was SF Pro while `SAT · SEP 5` beside it, built on `monoMedium`, was Plex. Nothing crashed and nothing logged.
  4. **Ten places rendered below the 11pt floor**, by scaling rather than by declaring: `.minimumScaleFactor(0.7)` on an 11pt label is 7.7pt — the same sin `CSFont.label`'s own comment names the web for. The standings movement chip printed `HELD SINCE SUN` at 8.8.
  5. **Names truncated at the DEFAULT size**: `Jerecho Fisch…` in the table's name column and `You · Jere…` on the climb rung, on the phone and (as `text-overflow:ellipsis`) on the web.
  6. **Reduced motion was a habit, not a mechanism.** Six curves were in use where L-30 names one, one web keyframe rode a bouncing bezier, and roughly thirty `withAnimation` call sites animated straight through the golfer's setting because the guard was written per site and mostly not written.
- **Recommendation (built):**
  1. **The reflow is arithmetic.** The strip is set entirely in a monospaced face, so the widest unbreakable word in a column is a calculation. `MeStripLayout` (Kit) decides two-rows-of-two **while every pair fits** and one fact per row when it does not — the layout that can never truncate. The view hands it a unit MEASURED off a ten-character probe set in the real face at the real size, because `UIFontMetrics` and SwiftUI's `relativeTo:` disagree by about five points at AX5 and the computed version broke `NUMBER` in half to prove it. The season row's cap is gone; it wraps.
  2. **A fitted sheet is a reading-size decision.** `.csFittedSheet(_:)` keeps the height where it is right and hands the whole page over at the accessibility sizes; the three sheets that had no scroller got one.
  3. **The font name is read from the file, not remembered**, and every mono role is the record voice again.
  4. **`CSMotion` owns L-30 for the whole app.** `CSMotion.run` / `.csAnimation` / `CSMotion.breath` resolve to nothing under reduce motion; every call site goes through them; the roll is the only curve, at four durations. On the web a single global `prefers-reduced-motion` backstop rests every animation and transition on its end frame, and the one overshooting bezier is now the roll.
  5. **Two lints per law (D249).** Preflight **38** — a role declared or scaled below 11pt, a PostScript name no bundled face carries, or a sheet pinned to a height. Preflight **39** — a second easing, a raw `withAnimation`, an unguarded `.animation(`, a missing web backstop, or a bezier that overshoots. Both carry self-test probes. `tools/web-verify.mjs` gains a permanent **horizontal-overflow assertion** and the walk runs at **320px**, which is the web's exact twin of "nothing scrolls horizontally".
- **Principle served:** L-29 (three voices, nothing below 11pt, every layout tolerates the AX sizes); L-30 (one easing, nothing bounces, reduced motion rests on the frame); L-34 (one fact, one place — a clipped fact is not on the screen); D249 (a lint per law); LV-17 (the web's floor debt may only shrink — it is 83 now, from 86).
- **Expected user benefit:** a golfer at the largest text size can read every fact on Home, every intent on the sheet and every length under it; a golfer who has asked for less motion gets none; and every golfer gets the type the brand canon specifies rather than the system's.
- **Tradeoffs:** **(a)** the font fix changes the metrics of every mono line in the app — Plex Mono is wider than SF for letters — so a handful of lines wrap that did not, and the strip's NEXT slot now takes two lines at the default size on a long course name. That is the correct rendering; the previous one was a substitution nobody chose. **(b)** A fitted sheet at `.large` under AX leaves space below three short rows; empty space beats overlapping rows. **(c)** `MeStripLayout` measures on first appearance, so the first layout pass is one-up and the second is the grid — one extra pass, invisible. **(d)** The web's type is still declared in pixels, so it responds to page zoom and not to a browser text-size preference; converting the sheet to `rem` is its own wave and is named in the report rather than half-done here. **(e)** Preflight 39 forbids `.easeOut` and friends in the Swift clients outright, which will annoy the next person who wants a bespoke curve — that is the point.
