> the Record page's printing was ADDED by Wave 3 and never removed, and eight
> phone sites and seven desk sites print the sentence today. The clause also
> silently narrowed `spec/brand-canon.md` §3 — *"verbatim EVERYWHERE money
> appears, from one constant per client"* — with no `CONFLICT` line, which is
> the one thing a level-5 entry may not do to a level-5 document. **The canon
> governs**, and the clause is corrected below to the law the build implements
> and the false sentence deleted. See D283.

*(2026-09-06. **Authorised by the owner's "build it"**, 2026-09-06. Appended with the code it governs — Wave 5. **Level 5 (UI). No competition mechanic moves.** Sources: `BRIEF.md` §16, §27; `UI_SYSTEM.md` §8 (the ink laws), §16A.1; `docs/ui-overhaul-2026-09-06/surfaces/season.md` §1.6; the audit's §2.7 and DD-05.)*

- **Current mechanic:** money takes `pos` green and `neg` red — a red/green P&L axis, which is the grammar of a brokerage and `BRIEF` §1's named "overly minimalist fintech app". The pot pane draws a gold-spined card, a serif payout trio **in gold**, a tick list whose paid state is a `✓` at 50% opacity, a handshake emoji in a stroked circle and an `✕` used as a button label. And the ledger sentence — *"Cup Season keeps the ledger; the money moves between friends."* — appeared on **eight of thirty-four** design renders, twice on one screen 250pt apart, and on three leaderboards, a profile, an event and Home.
- **Problem observed:** a legal line used as a layout element makes a page look auto-generated rather than composed — one blind reviewer wrote that it "is a legal line being used as a layout element", another that the repetition "makes the page look auto-generated" — and a colour axis borrowed from finance is the opposite of what this product is. Meanwhile the money surface of a product **about money between friends** had no ledger character at all: opacity as state, an emoji as a glyph, and a `✕` where a word belongs.
- **Recommendation (built):** **the figure is `ink`; the pot and anything won are `gold`; `pos` and `neg` never touch money; the sign is a WORD in agate** — `YOU OWE` · `YOU'RE OWED` · `SETTLED` · `THE POT` · `PAID` · `OWES`. A negative figure takes a **minus sign in ink**, never a red fill. The buy-ins are a **printed leaf**: column heads in `leafMut`, one 29pt row per member carrying a 24pt `CSFace`, the name in title case, the sign as a word and the amount right-flush, then a closing hairline and a `COLLECTED` total. **No colour anywhere on the leaf** — no `pos`, no `neg`, and no gold, because gold ink on bone is 1.68:1.
- **THE LEDGER LINE COMES FROM ONE CONSTANT PER CLIENT, AND IT IS PRINTED ONCE PER SURFACE.** *(Corrected 2026-09-07 — D283.)* It renders verbatim from **one constant** — `MoneyCopy.ledger` on the phone, `CS_LEDGER` on the desk — and `spec/brand-canon.md` §3 governs WHERE: **verbatim everywhere money appears**. What this entry adds is the FORM, not a smaller set of surfaces: standing alone as a policy line it is **`agateS`, at the foot of the money surface, under a hairline** — not a caption, not a subtitle, not filler under a stat rail, and never twice on one page. Embedded inside a longer sentence of prose (the join flow's rules, the pass cards' *where the money goes*, the wizard's pot disclosure) it takes that prose's own role, because there it is a clause and not a policy line. **A retyped copy is a defect the day it is written**, and the same law governs any future sentence of the same kind. If two lines is the cost, the constant is shortened **once, with the owner** — never on an individual surface.
- **The pot names itself once.** `THE POT · SIX IN AT $60` was both the section head and the caption of the same figure. The head carries the **count** (`EIGHT IN`) and the figure carries the rule and its own caption (`$60 EACH · 288 / 120 / 72`) — §16A.2's right-of-rule slot, which takes a count and nothing else.
- **Principle served:** D39 and D201 (the ledger is a promise, not a feature); `BRIEF` §16 and §27; `spec/brand-canon.md`'s one rule — gold means earned, never chrome.
- **Expected user benefit:** the anti-"betting app" vaccine keeps working without becoming wallpaper, and the pot finally looks like a receipt a Pro would print.
- **Tradeoffs:** `LINT-23` must fail any string containing "keeps the ledger" outside `MoneyCopy.ledger` / `CS_LEDGER`, and that check is not written yet — it lands with the rest of the lint in Wave 9. *(2026-09-07: it also now fails a standalone printing set in any role but `agateS` — D283, because the literal check could never have caught the form drifting.)* Two printings survive this commit **deliberately**: the wizard's pot fine print prints the sentence inside a longer disclosure at the moment a Pro is agreeing to take money, which is prose in a legal paragraph rather than a policy line at a foot, and removing it is an owner's call about a disclosure rather than a layout decision.

### D276 · A down arrow means one thing, and a producer never draws it

**Level 5 (UI) · 2026-09-07 · BUILT — Wave 7 of the UI overhaul (owner-authorised "build it", 2026-09-06)**

- **Current mechanic:** four producers emit a **▼** into a string, and two of them mean opposite things by it. `StandingsMath.movement` (and the desk's `csMovement`) emit `▲1 SINCE SUN` / `▼2 SINCE SUN` for a golfer's position on the table, where a down triangle means **you fell**. `StandingsMath.awards` and the desk's two award renderers emit `Most Improved · ▼0.5` for a golfer's handicap index, where a down triangle means **the best thing that can happen to you**. Both are 11pt, both are in the same face, neither carries a colour or a word that tells them apart, and on a squads season both can be on one screen. The audit files it as DD-02, a P0.
- **Problem:** the glyph is being asked to carry a valence it does not have, and the two senses are only distinguishable by reading the sentence around them — which is exactly what a mark is for NOT having to do. It is also a **typed arrow inside a produced string**: `LINT-13` fails those on sight, because a producer that draws its own glyph has taken the renderer's job and can then never be drawn a second way (a triangle at the reading sizes, a word at the accessibility sizes, a `<i class="tri">` on the desk).
- **Recommendation:** **the producer emits the PARTS and the renderer draws the mark.** `Movement` gains `count` (the magnitude, no sign, no glyph) and `sinceShort` (the day it is measured from) and its `text` becomes `UP 1 SINCE SUN` / `DOWN 2 SINCE SUN` / `HELD SINCE SUN`; `CSMovement` and the desk's `.tri` draw the triangle. **Most Improved says the fact in words** — `Most Improved · 0.5 off the index` — and **no producer in the product emits an arrow character for it**. `long` is unchanged and is still the VoiceOver string and the accessibility-size line. The arithmetic, the two refusals (no clock, no label; no delta, no label) and the four tones are untouched; `up2` keeps its magnitude and loses its colour, because there is one `pos` and one `cool` in the system now.
- **Also decided here, because it is the same law applied to a numeral:** the movement **clock is named once, for the whole table, in the section head** — `THE TABLE · MOVED SINCE SUN` — instead of eleven times at 11pt beside eleven two-digit ranks. `StandingsMath`'s absolute rule survives the move: a movement claim names the day it is measured from or it does not render, so with no snapshot the clause is absent from the head AND the column is absent from the rows. And a **tie is drawn as a tie**: `StandingsMath.competitionRanks` shares the numeral and skips the next (04 · 04 · 06), computed over the points column the table actually prints, with `TIED` in the sub-line so a shared numeral cannot read as a rendering error.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §15 — *`▲3` should communicate more than a paragraph* — which it cannot do while it communicates two contradictory things; D201's one-fact-one-place; and `UI_SYSTEM` §17's `LINT-13`.
- **Expected user benefit:** one mark, one meaning, on the surface a golfer looks at more than any other. A golfer who has fallen two places and a golfer who has taken half a shot off their index no longer wear the same badge.
- **Tradeoffs:** `Movement.text` is a different string, so anything that pinned it pins the new one (`LeagueRoomTests` and `tests/app-tests.js` both do, in both directions — they now assert that no triangle appears). The competition rank is computed on the CLIENT over the points column rather than served: until the server carries a rank, a tie the league's own tiebreak ladder would split is still drawn as a tie, which is what the visible column says and is the honest reading of it.

### D277 · The system reaches the rest of the product — one chip, one icon family, one dismiss verb, and the ceremony is a ceremony

**Level 5 (UI) · 2026-09-07 · BUILT — Wave 8 of the UI overhaul (owner-authorised "build it", 2026-09-06)**

- **Current mechanic:** D265–D276 built the visual system and carried it to the seven surfaces Phase 3 names — Home, the card, the profile, the course, the season, the event and the boards. **Everything else in the product is still in the old vocabulary**, and "everything else" is most of it: the season ceremony, the live finish and its settlement card, the live setup, the composer, the wizard, onboarding, the door, Card & settings, the bag, the Board, the schedule, the pot, the Play cover and ninety-five sheets and covers. Twelve chip families on the web and eight on the phone; four icon systems standing beside each other on one row; three dismiss verbs in three colours at two positions plus an `✕` in a filled circle; 133 toast sites carrying an id and a text and nothing else; four share artifacts printed in the palette D270 replaced.
- **Problem:** a half-migrated product looks worse than either state, because a golfer reads the SEAM. Two rows apart, one chip is a 999px capsule with a 1px border and the next is a 3pt rectangle that inverts; the composer's `Add my round` is the system's primary and the sheet it opens closes with a coloured `Done`; the settlement card a golfer shares is printed in `#E9BE62` while every gold in the app is `#D8B25A`. **And the audit's single worst score sits here**: `SeasonCeremonyView`, the screen a golfer sees ONCE, the night a season they played for four months ends, contains **zero animation calls and zero haptics** and renders as a dialog — while the settings accordion animates its disclosure. It scores 4.9 and it is filed P0.
- **Recommendation:** the same components, applied — and four laws made general rather than surface-by-surface. **(1) One chip.** Twelve web families and every phone pill become §7.2's shape: 28pt, radius `p` 3, an agate label, `bg2` at rest, and **selected INVERTS to the panel** — never an ember fill, because a selection is not a live action. **(2) One icon family.** Ten drawn glyphs join `CSGlyph` (camera, photo, calendar, comment, bell, link, send, trash, gear, clock) and every SF Symbol standing beside a drawn one goes; the board's `📌`/`📣`/`✦`/`◆` and the push prompt's three symbols go with them, on both clients. **(3) One dismiss verb.** `SheetFrame` — which fifteen sheets are built from — loses its 44pt `✕`-in-a-circle for §7.3's `Close`, a toolbar tertiary at `topBarTrailing`, and eight more sites follow. **(4) The toast carries a kind.** Every one of the 126 `toast.show(…)` sites is classified: a confirmation takes `.confirmed` (a `pos` rail and a drawn check), a failure `.failed` (a `neg` rail and a cross), and only a genuinely neutral line stays neutral.
- **Also decided here, because it is what the wave is FOR:** **the ceremony is a takeover.** `CSTakeover` is §11.3's biggest motion, built at last: a full-bleed band on the pinned `ceremony` ground whose plate wipes from the leading edge, whose `display` lines arrive at a 60ms stagger, whose figure **tallies** (`CSTally`, 340ms, eased out), and whose medallion seals last with the thock — one haptic, at the seal, and nothing on the way there. Under it the settlement is a printed ledger: the two named finishers on rules, what you are owed as a figure on a gold rule, the pay rows on a leaf, and `MoneyCopy.ledger` once at the foot. **And the settlement card is rendered IN THE APP at the geometry it exports at** — 1080 × 1350, scaled to the measure — so the object the audit calls the most beautiful in the product is finally seen by the golfer who won it, and there is no second in-app rendering to drift from the PNG.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §26/§27 (one system, counted); `UI_SYSTEM` §7.2, §7.3, §11.3, §13.1, §13.4; non-negotiable 1 (a container needs a job) and 4 (two metals, scarce by construction); D269's ruling that ember has exactly two jobs and a *dismiss* verb, a *selected chip* and a *ball marker* are none of them.
- **Expected user benefit:** the product stops having a seam. A golfer meets one chip, one icon, one dismiss word and one toast wherever they are — and on the night their season ends they get the biggest moment in the product instead of a dialog.
- **Tradeoffs:** **the ceremony cannot be photographed on real data** — no season on any device is `complete` — so it ships behind a DEBUG fixture (`-cs_dev_open ceremony`, invented golfers on invented ids, never written to the server) and is **unjudged** by any real state, which is stated in the wave's own commit rather than glossed. The four share artifacts change palette, so a card shared today and a card shared last week do not match: that is the point, and it is one-way. Twelve web chip families were consolidated at the CSS level rather than in markup, so the classes survive with one shape each — Wave 9 deletes the names. And 126 typed `→` characters remain in `index.html`: `LINT-13` counts them at a baseline and the sweep that reaches zero is Wave 9's, not this one's.

### D278 · A rule with a lint behind it — twenty-nine checks, all of them running, nine of them at zero

**Level 5 (UI) · 2026-09-07 · BUILT — Wave 9 of the UI overhaul (owner-authorised "build it", 2026-09-06)**

- **Current mechanic:** D274 landed the ratchet — a check that fails on a RISE, with today's count written into `tests/preflight-baselines.json` — and `UI_SYSTEM` §17 declares **twenty-nine** checks. For eight waves the file ran **thirteen** of them, and nothing anywhere said which sixteen were only a sentence. A reader of §17 would have believed the product was linted for spacing, tracking, gold-on-a-control, a panel holding a sentence, a leaf holding a grid, a pushed screen naming itself twice, a photograph cropped into an avatar, the ledger line, and all five of the render-time budgets. None of it was true. Every wave since 0b closed its report with the same line: *"the counters are wired; nothing reads the total."*
- **Problem:** this repo has proved four separate times that **a ruling with no lint drifts back** — D131 was "copy-only, ~90 strings" and four of its retired phrasings were written back into this programme's own proposed copy before anybody noticed; D249 exists because of it; `TERMINOLOGY` §4 exists because of D249. A half-run lint is worse than a missing one, because the table reads as coverage. And a table that says twenty-nine while the file runs thirteen is the exact failure mode the ids were renamed to avoid.
- **Recommendation:** **write the other fifteen, and then make the table itself checkable.** The greps: `LINT-06` (a spacing literal off the ten-value scale), `-07` (a tracking literal — tracking is a RATIO of the rendered size and `CSType` is the one call site that multiplies), `-11` (the gold token inside a `ButtonStyle`'s body, a `.tint(`, or a button-style enum naming a gold case — scoped to a control's own CHROME, because every slat in this product is a `Button` and the naïve form failed the leader's rail), `-19` (a `CSPanel` holding more than twelve characters or a space), `-20` (a `CSLeaf` with no grid), `-21` (the compiler: `CSEmpty.Door` is non-optional), `-23` (the ledger line is one constant per client), `-24` (a file carrying both `CSPageHeader` and a non-empty `navigationTitle`), `-26` (a round's `photo_path` in a `CSFace`), `-27` (`TERMINOLOGY` §4's 34 laws run over **the design's own documents** — `UI_SYSTEM.md`, the seven surface specs and the eight mockups — because §17 says five of the six hits found in this design's copy were written into specs Phase 3 was going to build from). The five that are not greps become **tests**: `BudgetProbeTests` hosts a viewport for real, lays it out, and asserts what the components incremented while rendering. And **preflight check 49 reads §17's table out of `UI_SYSTEM.md` and fails if any id in it has nothing behind it — or if anything here is not in it.**
- **Also decided here, because the sweep is the other half of the wave:** **the four retired declarations are deleted.** `CSCard`, `CSStat`, `CSEmptyState` and `CSButton` were kept for eight waves with their removal wave named in the file itself, and `LINT-30` counted the call sites at a baseline that could only fall: **157 → 111 → 14 → 0**. `CSHairline`, `CSGroupHead`, `CSTabStrip`, `CSHero`, `CSWash`, `CSDuskCard` and `CSLookSky` go with them. **That closes D270's last owed clause: the product paints no atmosphere.** The look's accent reached five channels and two of them were fields of colour over a page — the hero's radial wash and the sky's 22% band over the top 260pt. Both are gone; a look now reaches the tick, the eyebrow and the spine, all three of which are a MARK. The scroll strip survives, painting `bg0` under the clock, which is the half of it that was ever doing work.
- **And the one that is a producer bug, not a style:** `RankMove.label` emitted `▲2`, `LeagueCopy.indexSub` emitted `▼ 0.3 this season` and `SeasonStats.deltaText` emitted `▼ 0.3` — the same down triangle, in the same face at the same size, meaning *you fell* on a board and *your handicap improved* on a card, with no colour between them. That is D276's DD-02 in three more producers. `label` is deleted (nothing rendered it; `Movement` superseded it); the two index deltas print **words** and a **signed figure** — `0.3 off your index this season`, `−0.3` with a true U+2212 — on both clients.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §26 (*a rule a preflight cannot fail is a wish*), §27, §32; D274's ratchet; D249's thesis, proved a fifth time.
- **Expected user benefit:** the system stops drifting back. Nine of the checks are zero-tolerance from this commit, so a golfer will never again meet three dismiss verbs, a spinner in a void, a typed arrow that means two opposite things, a gold button, or a second copy of the sentence that says what Cup Season does with money.
- **Tradeoffs:** **three baselines ROSE, and the rise is scope rather than drift.** `LINT-06`, `-07` and `-10` were turned on for `index.html` — §14.5's stated web half of this wave — so their counts went 363 → 1238, 59 → 211 and 109 → 265 when the desk's 922 spacing literals, 173 off-scale tracking ratios and 158 boxed surfaces joined the phone's. Every one of those is a debt written down, which is the only kind worth having, and the ratchet now holds the desk too. **`LINT-27` lands at 2, and both hits are real**: `surfaces/season.md` names a phase "Setup / draft phase" (the stage word is *Squads drawing*) and `mockups/leaderboard.html` prints `Par 4 · SI 14 · 402 yds` (§4.18 retires the abbreviation). Neither was fixed, because the design documents are the design phase's own record and a build wave rewriting them is how a record stops being one — they are named here and in the baselines file instead. **`LINT-06`'s phone half is untouched at 363 and `LINT-14`'s at 146**: those are the type-and-spacing sweep §17's hardening order puts after this wave's, and forty of the tracking sites are a mono-to-condensed FACE change on surfaces no wave of this overhaul has designed (draft night, the composer's hole grid, the widgets). Migrating them blind in a sweep would restyle screens nobody can photograph.


### D279 · The product knows which phone it is on, and every switch iOS offers has an answer

**Level 5 (UI) · 2026-09-07 · BUILT — Wave 10 of the UI overhaul (owner-authorised "build it", 2026-09-06)**

- **Current mechanic:** D265–D278 built the visual system and carried it to every surface. It is a system with **one shape**. `UI_AUDIT` measured the phone half: `ViewThatFits` appears **zero** times in the product and `horizontalSizeClass` twice, both meaning *is the phone sideways* — so an SE at 375pt, a 17 Pro at 402 and a Max at 440 render the identical view tree, and the nine layouts `UI_SYSTEM` §16.3 gives a default, an AX1 and an AX3 form to are a table in a document rather than a branch in the code. The desk's half is worse: 40 hover rules and **one** `[disabled]` rule, and the two objects the surface is about — the standings slat and the Golfers board row — are a `tr` and a `div` with click handlers, with no `tabindex`, no `role`, no focus ring and no way into them from a keyboard at all.
- **Problem:** the failures are not theoretical and they are not confined to the accessibility sizes. On an SE at the DEFAULT reading size Home's own eyebrow read `MON · GOLD CANYON — DINOSAUR MOUNTAIN ·…` — the course a golfer is playing today, cut off, on the front page — and the board truncated two surnames that set perfectly on a Max. At AX5 the whole of Home **sheared**: one row that would not shrink made the content box 466pt wide, a vertical `ScrollView` centred it, and the masthead ran off the leading edge while the figures ran off the trailing one. Wave 5 met the same shear on the season page, clamped six candidates, and filed it unfinished. And at AX3 the board's own rows read `+4 ▲1 15` — three numerals with the column heads correctly hidden and **nothing anywhere on the page to say which was the gap, which the movement and which the total**.
- **Recommendation:** **reflow on the measured advance of the actual characters at the size being read, never on a device breakpoint** — `MeStripLayout`'s model, which the design names as the one to copy, generalised out of Home and into `CSAdvance` (a string's width in the real face at the real size) and `CSClauseLine` (a `·`-separated line that sets on one line while it fits and **breaks on its separators** when it does not, decided by `ViewThatFits` against the real proposal). The slat's numeric columns become a fraction of the measure with a floor and a cap, so the Max's extra 38pt goes to the NAME; the board's abbreviation stops being `count >= 10` and becomes *does the longest name in this field fit the column this phone gives it*. The nine §16.3 layouts each get their stated form, and **at AX3 a board row says its own facts in words** — `UP ONE SINCE SUN · 4 BACK · 15 POINTS`, from `Movement.long`, which Wave 7 produced and nothing consumed.
- **Also decided here, because it is the half a screenshot cannot show:** **the other four iOS switches get their answers.** Bold Text and Increase Contrast were already resolved in `Theme.swift`; **Reduce Transparency** is the one this design is most exposed to, because the folio at `a16`, the contour at `a24`/`a56` and the photo scrim are not decoration over a solid thing — they *are* the credential and the title card. Each now resolves to its **composited opaque value** over the ground it is drawn on, which is the same arithmetic that produced `folioRule` `#8B8F8B` and gave it a name. **A scrim is the exception and it is stated:** flattening a `.title` ramp to its darkest stop would paint the plate solid and erase the photograph, so the ramp becomes a **hard edge at the point it crossed half its darkest value** — nothing fades into anything, the copy's band carries the ramp's own maximum, and the top of the picture survives.
- **And the contrast table is COMPUTED rather than quoted.** Every ratio §16.1 states was typed into a markdown table by hand, and two were already wrong. Measured at the shipped values: every text tier clears AA on every ground in both printings; `rule` is under 3:1 in both, as declared; **`dim` in the dark printing is 3.15:1, not the sub-3 §16.1 prints** — so *`dim` may never carry a word* is a RULING, not an arithmetic consequence, and the fence is `LINT-29`; and the `bg2` review list is stale in both directions — in light all six metals and semantics now clear 4.5 (Wave 0a's darkening), while in dark it is `brand` and `cool` that do not.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §24 and §25; `UI_SYSTEM` §16 entire; non-negotiable 9 (every component declares its states) extended to every layout declaring its forms; D274's thesis that a rule a test cannot fail is a wish.
- **Expected user benefit:** the product fits the phone a golfer actually holds. A name is not cut off on an SE, a page does not slide sideways at a reading size somebody needs, a board row is readable when the columns are gone, a chip is a 44pt target everywhere rather than in three places out of nineteen, every column of the landscape scorecard says which hole it is, and the desk can be driven from a keyboard.
- **Tradeoffs:** the slat's documented fixed-column arithmetic was **12pt optimistic** — the row pays `s3` twice, before the face and before the name — so the name column is 176 at the 402 measure and not the 188 six surface specs quote, and two tests moved with the correction. The season board's split-flap does not run at the accessibility sizes: its overlay draws over the whole row, and at AX3 the row is three times the rail's height, so the numeral floated outside its own painted field; the rest frame is the finished state, which is §11.2's own floor. The credential's three-figure columns are now measured rather than equal thirds — that fixes `HANDICAP IND…` and `WHO'S THE BIT…`, two truncations at the DEFAULT size on the product's most looked-at object, and it means the rule under them is a different width on two different cards. And `CSChip` carries its own 44pt hit area, so two call sites that added one by hand lost a redundant modifier.

### D280 · The desk is a second shape, not a wide phone — the frame, the head and the board's own columns
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-06** (owner: "build it") · UI level · `UI_SYSTEM` §14 entire, `BUILD_BRIEF` §5, R-C / D234

- **Current mechanic:** R-C ruled two clients, one product, one set of producers, two shapes, and D234 made the web half of every wave non-optional. Ten waves shipped their web halves as *system* — the merged `:root`, the nine type roles as CSS classes, the marks, the slats, the tape, the contour, the settlement palette, the hover and focus twins, the keyboard model. None of them shipped the *composition*. The desk still opened on a 232px `bg1` panel of icon rows, a sticky masthead printing the wordmark a second time, a body capped at 1120 and centred so a 1,440px screen carried ~90px of dead ground down its right edge, and a season page whose title was the league's name set at 16px inside a card, under a mono dateline that said the name again.
- **Problem:** the frame was the phone's IA in a browser wearing the desk's tokens. `UI_SYSTEM` §14.1 states the frame in five clauses and the shipped sidebar honoured none of them: 236 not 232, `bg0` not `bg1`, the mark and the wordmark at the top (absent), `agate` nav (13.5px sans with an icon each), a **3px `brand` tick** on the selected item (a 2px tick *and* a `bg2` fill *and* a 10px radius — a boxed surface, LINT-10's own finding), and a foot carrying the viewer's face, their number and the build identity (it carried the league's name, which the page already says). §14.3's "what the desk gains" — the columns the phone cannot afford — had not been built at all: the desk's board printed the phone's four columns at the phone's row height on a screen with 400px to spare.
- **Recommendation:** build the frame. **236 on `bg0` with one hairline**; the mark and the wordmark at the top, and the header's copy of the wordmark **suppressed at that width** — a masthead printed twice on one screen is a masthead that does not know which one it is. **Nav in `agate` with no icons and no fill**, a 3px `brand` tick on the left edge of the selected one — the tab bar's underline, rotated. Below one rule, the section a desk has room for and a tab bar does not: the season, the schedule, the rules, the archive. At the foot the viewer's own face on their own pigment, their number, and `v23 · <sha>` — the deploy's own stamp, never hand-edited. **The body fills**: `1fr + 340` at the desk gutter of 40, uncapped until 1264 so a 1,440px screen has no dead column. **The season page takes a head**: an eyebrow with the live dot, the league's name at `display` 42, and the dateline under it — the name said once, in the size a title is set in, instead of three times in three faces. **The board takes the desk's own columns**: `RDS` and a five-dot `LAST FIVE` inside the row, at slat 56.
- **Principle served:** R-C C-2 rejects "the phone IA reflowed" in as many words, and a 1440px screen with one column down the middle wastes the only thing the desk has. §16A.4 — one fact, one encoding, per viewport: the league's name was on screen three times.
- **Expected user benefit:** a desk that reads as a desk. The board a Pro actually looks at carries how many rounds each golfer has posted and how their last five went, inside the row, without a second block; the page names itself once, at the top, in the product's own display face; and the person reading it is at the foot of their own sidebar rather than the league's name they already know.
- **Tradeoffs:** three of §14.3's own columns do not ship, and each is a producer and not a layout. **`BEST` has no producer**: `v_rounds_ranked` carries `differential`, `index_at_post`, `playing_index`, `pvi` and `points` and no `gross`, and a gross is not derivable from a differential without the rating and the slope, which the view also does not carry — so the column is **absent**, per §10.2's own ladder rule, rather than filled with a figure that is not the one the head names. **`MONEY` is not built**: mid-season the pot's three payouts are a projection and not money anybody has, the pot block in the same right-hand column already prints the split once (`1ST · 2ND · 3RD`), and repeating it down a column of rows is §16A.4's defect with money's name on it. A settled season is where a money column would be true, and that is a settlement read nobody wrote this wave. **The desk's extra columns render on the INDIVIDUAL board only** — `standings_snapshots` snapshots squads, and a squad has no rounds count and no last five. And §14.1's `THE DESK ▸` label is not used: `LV-12` already ruled that word may not become a label on this client because it names the founder's console, which has no route of its own on the web; the section below the rule is named by its rows.

### D281 · A ranked list may not contradict its own column, and the cut counts the seats the season has
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-06** (owner: "build it") · UI level · repair pass over D267/D276/D245 · `surfaces/leaderboard.md` §4 and D-2, `surfaces/season.md` §1.4/§1.4a

- **Current mechanic:** three ranked boards ship the 44pt rail, and two of them draw a numeral that does not follow the figure printed beside it. **(1)** The Golfers board prints each golfer's average against their own playing handicap under the note `VS PLAYING HCP · PLUS IS BETTER`, and orders the rows by the server's `rank_by_form`, which ranks on BEATS. On a photographed board that came out **−2.6 (01), +1.0 (02), +2.8 (03), −3.8 (04)** — neither ascending nor descending on the only figure it shows. **(2)** The season table's cut band is a constant, `Cut · top two play the Cup Final`, drawn after row two on every board — while `ClimbMath.cut(meta)` has mapped the three shipped finish shapes to a K since D24: **one** seat for a points table, **one** for a squad-level `squads2` season, `meta.k ?? 2` otherwise. A squads2 league therefore read *top two play the Cup Final* where ONE squad advances, with the line drawn under the wrong row, and the desk repeated the hard-code at its own `i===1` while computing K correctly two thousand lines above for the climb. **(3)** The table's windowed view of a field over ten hard-codes `Set([0, 1, 2])`, the K=2 cut neighbours, where the climb it replaced used `show.insert(K − 1); show.insert(K)`.
- **Problem:** the rank rail is half the product's signature (non-negotiable 2) and on two of the three boards it carries a lie. A list a golfer cannot scan is worse than an unsorted one, because the rail makes a claim. And D127's hollow-final sentence — `EVERYONE ADVANCES — n CONTENDERS, K SEATS`, the fix the web took in August and the phone did not for two months — rode `ClimbMath.note` through `ClimbView`, which Wave 5 folded into the table; the sentence stopped rendering anywhere, so a two-golfer season went back to announcing a race with one runner. The QB-12 *closer* clause went the same way.
- **Recommendation:** **the rail follows the figure the row prints, and the seat count comes from the one function that knows it.** `FriendsBoard.ordered` sorts on each lens's own printed figure — the form average DESCENDING (plus is better; `CSBands.bandName(+3)` is *Torched it*, and the artboard's `LOWER IS BETTER` is the document that is wrong), the handicap index ASCENDING — with a golfer who has no figure taking the TAIL in name order rather than a zero or a guess. `FriendsBoard.ranked` hands the view the POSITION, so the rail and the figure cannot diverge again. `SeasonBoardCopy.cut` takes `k:` and spells it (L-33); the season table reads `ClimbMath.cut(scenarios?.meta).K` for the sentence, for the row the line is drawn after, and for the window's cut neighbours; the desk reads its own `climbCut` for all three. `ClimbMath.note`'s hollow-final sentence renders at the board's foot, and `ClimbMath.closer` returns to the chapter line, which is where `season.md` §5 put it.
- **Principle served:** non-negotiable 2 (the rail is the signature) and 3 (a golf number is a visual object — a rank is one); D201 (one fact, one place); D24's rule that the cut line's arithmetic has one home; D234 / R-C, which forbids the two clients disagreeing — and here the DESK disagreed with itself.
- **Expected user benefit:** a golfer can read a board top to bottom and the order means what the column says. A league whose Final seats one is told so, on the line drawn where that seat is. A two-golfer season is told there is no race rather than being sold one. And a golfer four points back is told again that one round in the top band covers it.
- **Tradeoffs:** the client now orders the Golfers board rather than reading the server's rank, so until `friends_board` is pushed with a matching `ORDER BY` the server's `rank_by_form` is decoded and unused — a deliberate single ordering rule rather than two that can drift, and the RPC is on the unpushed list either way. `ClimbMath.items` still has no app call site: the table expresses the window, the ellipsis rung and the cut as its own view, and merging the whole producer in would mean rebuilding the table around a rung list — the ARITHMETIC that mattered (K, the cut neighbours, the note, the closer) is single-sourced, and `items` remains covered as the producer the desk's climb reads.

### D282 · The card is an object at every name length, and the building state is said out loud
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-06** (owner: "build it") · UI level · repair pass over D265/D272/D279 · `UI_SYSTEM` §6.5/§6.7/§6.8, `surfaces/player-card.md`

- **Current mechanic:** `CSCredential.head` lays the identity block `.bottomLeading` inside a plate of **fixed** height — 58% of the card — while the block itself **grows**. A two-line name at `display` 34 over a three-clause identity is ~72% of a 180pt plate, so its top reaches the gold slot at the plate's head. The `riding` comment in that file guards the accessibility case only. Separately: the figure rule spans the sum of its measured cells and stops there, leaving 55pt of card to its right on a three-figure card with a **longer** folio hairline stacked directly beneath it; the crest card's `ceremony` ground is a ~1.05:1 step off `bg0` in the dark printing and `shadow-lift` is invisible over it; `CSContour`'s one `brand` dot is placed in the field's own coordinate space with no knowledge of the copy on top of it; and the You page prints `CredentialCopy.mine` unconditionally and never calls `CredentialCopy.status`.
- **Problem:** every one of those lands on the flagship object of the design, and four of the five land at the **default reading size on the default device**. `FOUNDER` printed through `JER` of `JERECHO` on the tab a golfer opens to look at themselves. The three-figure card carried two rules of two different lengths and read unfinished. Without a photograph — the state most golfers are in for some time — the card stopped being an object at all and became type floating on a flat screen. The ember dot landed inside the line of `GALEN MARR`, where at 7pt on a display-weight name it reads as a dust speck and spends the card's only ember mark on nothing. And `CredentialCopy.status`, whose own doc comment says it exists to move the denominator "out of two competing rails and into English", was called by the person page and not by the You page — so a **buddy's** card said *One more round sets their number* and **your own** said nothing at all, and D3's *building, not broken* was invisible on the first surface a brand-new golfer opens.
- **Recommendation:** **the plate's head band is reserved and the copy band is measured against it.** `CSCredential.PlateBand` computes the band's height from the real characters in the real face at the size being read; the name drops from `display` to `displayS` when it will not set on one line (which is what `player-card-photo.png` draws — a one-line name with clear air above the identity and clear air below the slot); and only when even that will not fit does the identity leave the photograph for the card's own ground, which is §6.7's path the accessibility branch has always taken. **Three figures fill the card's inner measure**, so the rule reaches the edge every artboard draws it at, and the two-cell exception keeps the 66%/33% its own doc comment has always claimed. **The object gets its edge**: a 1px rule at the same `a16` `ceremonyInk` the folio inside it already uses — the shape the object already has, made visible, because a shadow on near-black is not an edge. **The contour's mark takes a safe region** on any plate that carries copy. And the You page prints the status sentence with its establishing clause.
- **Principle served:** non-negotiable 1 (an object is a physical artefact a golfer would keep — it has to *look* like one); §6.5's single anatomy; D3's building-not-broken; `BRIEF` §29's bar, on the screen the bar is judged on.
- **Expected user benefit:** a golfer's own name is legible on their own card. A golfer with no photograph gets an object rather than a flat page. A golfer two rounds in is told, on their own page, that one more round sets their number.
- **Tradeoffs:** a long name renders at `displayS` 24 rather than `display` 34, so two cards in a list can carry two name sizes — which is the trade `player-card.md` §6.7 already makes for the identity block, applied one rung earlier and one rung cheaper. `CSObject`'s rim is drawn in both printings; in light it is invisible against a 15:1 step, which is the correct amount of nothing.

### D283 · The laws hold themselves — the canon says what ships, and four lints stop lying
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-06** (owner: "build it") · UI level · repair pass over D268/D270/D273/D277/D278 · `spec/brand-canon.md` §3–§4, `TERMINOLOGY.md` §3.1/§4, `UI_SYSTEM.md` §17

- **Current mechanic:** four checks report **zero, and held there** over defects that ship. `LINT-04` greps `Color(red:` / `Color(white:` / `Color(hue:` and never `Color(hex:`, which is this repo's own literal form — so eight Swift colour literals shipped, five of them the RETIRED D103b palette (Fairway `#2FA46A` and `pine` `#12271B`, both deleted by name in D270), painting the Share **control** and the ground of the screen a golfer sees the moment they finish a round; the desk's `#finish` carried the same two hexes under a comment saying it used "hexes, not the theme tokens". `LINT-11` is scoped to a control's own chrome and saw no gold on a WARNING paragraph, a colour LEGEND key, a calendar dot, a tee time, a membership tag or a decorative SF Symbol trophy. `LINT-23` greps a retyped literal, so eight ledger printings in three different type roles reported clean. Terminology check 7 carries three phrasings of the retired record sense of *your card* and a new file wrote a seventh (`on the card`); check 18 greps `\bSI \d` and a bare `SI` column head walked through on four surfaces. And `spec/brand-canon.md` §4 was **still headed LIVE** eight commits after D268/D270 replaced its palette, its type families, its radii and its motion — with no `CONFLICT` line in either entry, though `git log b3abedc..HEAD -- spec/brand-canon.md` is empty and the canon's own protocol says a palette or type change rides the design lane *with a note here*.
- **Problem:** this repo has now proved five times that **a ruling with no lint drifts back** — and this is the sixth shape of it, which is worse: a lint that reports on a codebase that does not exist. A reader of `UI_SYSTEM` §17 would have believed the product had no invented colour, no gold on chrome, one ledger printing and one vocabulary. None of it was true, and the reports said it was. Underneath that, a canon whose §4 is false is not a canon: the next person to reach for the brand green would find `#2FA46A` printed in the document that outranks everything.
- **Recommendation:** **make each check see the form the codebase actually writes, then fix what it finds.** `LINT-04` gains `Color(hex:` / `UIColor(rgb:` / `Color("#…")`; all eight sites move onto the `ceremony` ramp and `object.scrim-*`, the Share button becomes EMBER because it is the screen's one primary, and the finish's radial wash is deleted on both clients (D272 bans it by name). `LINT-11` gains a legend key and a gold SF Symbol; the warning takes `mut`, the schedule's gold taxonomy channel becomes `ink`/`mut`, the trophy becomes `CSTrophyMark`. `LINT-23` gains the FORM — a standalone printing is `agateS` or it is a hit — and the four standalone printings are normalised, the ceremony's two collapsed to one at the foot. Check 7 gains `on the card` after a round's noun (the profile sense stays exempt); check 18 gains a standalone `SI`; a new row 35 retires `snapshot`, which §3.1 always banned and the ship list never listed, so three live strings said it — one on a pane this overhaul REBUILT.
- **Also decided here, because it is the document rather than the code:** **`brand-canon.md` §4 is amended to the shipped system** — the palette, the four type families with Charter retired, five radii, two easings, and *no glow, no wash, no gradient* — with the retired names printed there so nothing writes them back, and **D268 and D270 each gain the `CONFLICT` line they owed it.** D273's own clause is corrected: it silently narrowed the canon's *verbatim everywhere money appears* to *once per client* and asserted as fact two removals that never happened. **The canon governs**; what D273 contributes is the FORM, not a smaller set of surfaces. And three more money/vocabulary strings go with it — `YOU STILL OWE` becomes `YOU OWE` (non-negotiable 8 names three money words and that was a fourth), and `best card each week` becomes `best round each week` across five producers, because `the card` is the credential now.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §26 — *a rule a preflight cannot fail is a wish* — applied to the preflight itself; D249's thesis, proved a sixth time; `brand-canon.md`'s own change protocol; the hierarchy of truth, which a level-5 entry may narrow only with a named `CONFLICT`.
- **Expected user benefit:** the moment a golfer finishes a round is drawn in the product's own palette. Nobody is handed the earned metal for a push-registration failure or a legend key. The sentence about what Cup Season does with money reads the same everywhere it appears. And the next reader of the canon is told the truth by it.
- **Tradeoffs:** the widened checks found **eight more hits than the review named** — five `on the card`, three `SI`, three `snapshot` — and every one was fixed rather than baselined, which is why this commit touches copy on surfaces no wave of this overhaul designed. Five tests pinned the old strings and were **migrated, not deleted**. `second-best card` and `your best 18-hole card` are deliberately left: those are scorecards inside a countback clause, where the noun is unambiguous and where changing it would change what a tiebreak means.

### D284 · A round you posted wrong can be deleted from the phone, and the receipt ends in a figure
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-06** (owner: "build it") · UI level · repair pass over D277/D278 · R-C / D234, `UI_SYSTEM` §6.7, non-negotiable 3

- **Current mechanic:** Wave 3 removed the per-row `×` from `RecentRoundsList` and wrote, in `YouScreen`'s own comment, that "deletion belongs on the round's own receipt". **The receipt never got one.** `RoundReceiptSheet` has no toolbar item, no context menu and no delete; a grep for *delete* across the app finds only *Delete my account* and the league delete. `RoundsRepository.deleteRound` and `YouRepository.deleteRound` are unreachable, and the desk kept its owner-only `×`, its confirm and its `delete_round` call. Separately the receipt's total — the figure the whole leaf builds to — is set as `Points` in sentence-case `body` beside `6` at `figureS`, one more row at a size barely above the rows above it, so the 2pt `leafInk` rule over it separates nothing from nothing; and the counting clause prints `COUNTING #1` with the denominator the leaf is holding left out.
- **Problem:** **the two clients differ on a capability**, which R-C / D234 forbids in as many words — a golfer who posts a wrong gross has no way to remove it from the phone at all, and that is not a design decision anybody made, it is a sentence in a comment that nothing implemented. The total is non-negotiable 3's own defect on the one surface built to end in a number: *a golf number is a visual object*, and here the product's arithmetic reverts to prose at the exact moment it resolves.
- **Recommendation:** **the receipt carries the delete, two steps, gated to the round's owner** — a tertiary that arms, then `csDestructive(busy:)` with the consequence spelled beside it, because deleting a round leaves the card AND every league standing it counted toward and cannot be undone. The sentence is a producer (`RoundCopy.deleteConsequence`) that the desk's `confirm()` now reads too, so the two clients cannot describe the same irreversible act differently. **The total is set as `lb-score-object.png` sets it**: the label in board caps, the figure at `figure` 27, and the two sub-clauses in `agateS` caps under it. **And `COUNTING #2 OF 4` carries its denominator** (L-01) — the cap was on the seed all along.
- **Also decided here:** **a moment fanned to two leagues is one wire row.** `HomeFeedFold` folds a system NOTE across leagues and stopped there, so `round_to_board()`'s fan-out printed the same personal best about the same round to the same golfer twice, one row apart, on Home's wire. Moments fold on their round id, and on their body inside the same 48-hour window when there is no round.
- **Principle served:** R-C / D234 (one product, two shapes, never two capabilities); non-negotiable 3; L-01 (the denominator is part of the fact); D201 (one fact, one place).
- **Expected user benefit:** a golfer can take back a wrong score from the phone they posted it on. The receipt ends in the figure it was adding up. Home stops saying the same thing twice.
- **Tradeoffs:** `delete_round` is an existing RPC with an existing grant, so nothing new is pushed — but a delete on the phone is a new place a golfer can lose data, which is why it is two steps and why the sentence names both consequences before the second tap.

### D285 · The wire is an edition, not a list — datelines, one league-note line, and the viewer is "You"
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on his own phone: *"Things look text heavy, sections arent differentiated"*) · UI level · repair pass over D265/D280 and `surfaces/home.md` §1.4 · `BRIEF` §5–§8, §32; `UI_AUDIT` H-05; DEF-3

- **Current mechanic:** Home's wire renders **one flat run of rows**, each one a sentence at `bodyS` 15 in `mut` behind a **34pt leading date column**, with a chevron. `surfaces/home.md` §1.4 rules it that way in as many words — *"Today / This week / Earlier survive as day markers on the rows themselves, not as three more section heads"* — and the build honours it exactly. Five weights were designed and **four of them have no data on any real account**: weight 2 needs a round photograph, weight 4 a finished season, weight 3 has **no producer at all** (`BUILD_REPORT` §3 says so). So a clash that is open, a standing that has moved, a personal best and *"Fellas · 4 earlier league notes"* are all drawn as the same 44pt object. On the owner's own account that is **fifteen rows, eight of them league-note counts**, three of which are the same two leagues at three different periods. And one of them says *"Jerecho set a personal best"* — to Jerecho.
- **Problem:** the owner installed the overhaul on his phone and filed three words about it: *"Things look text heavy, sections arent differentiated."* Both halves are the same defect. **A page with no size step has no sections**, whatever its headings say — a 12pt agate label over rows of 15pt body is not a hierarchy, it is a caption; and a column of dated rows in one type size is not a feed, it is a table, which is what `GROUP BY` looks like when you render it. `BRIEF` §7 says *do not make every feed item visually equal*, §8 wants a primary, a secondary and a tertiary on every screen, and §5 says typography carries the hierarchy. The wire had none of the three. **The date column is the mechanism**: it pushes every sentence off the margin that the masthead, the lead, the ME strip and the floor all align to, and it repeats — `Sun · Sun · Sun · Aug 31 · Aug 31` — because a period repeats.
- **Recommendation:** **three changes, in the order they answer him.** **(1) The wire runs under datelines.** `HomeWirePeriod` files every row under *Coming up · Today · This week · Earlier*, and the head is `displayS` 24 in `ink` over rows at `bodyS` 15 in `mut` — a 1.6× size step and a full contrast step, which is what an eye reads as a new section before it reads a word. It carries **no rule and no box**: `s5` of air and the size step are the separation (§32 — structure without cards). **The date column goes**, and what a row still needs to say moves to the trailing edge as a stamp; a row under `TODAY` says nothing at all, and **a rundown says a date once**, so a stamp that repeats the row above it inside its own group is dropped. **(2) Every league note on the page is ONE line.** D217 folded them per league per bucket and the audit still found four on one screen; they fold now to a single line at the **foot** of the wire, in the quietest voice the wire has, and it opens the board where the notes actually live. **(3) The ranked items take their own weight.** A clash, a standing, a plan or a circle story is `body` 17 in `ink` with **its own clock** — `Tomorrow`, `6 days` — where the shipped row threw the producer's deadline away and printed `Sun`. It does **not** wear ember: §2.4 gives the live metal two seats and the lead holds both, so a live thing reads as live through its clock and its weight, which is how a printed board does it.
- **Also decided here, and it is copy law rather than layout:** **DEF-3 reaches the wire.** `round_to_board()` writes a moment in the third person because it writes it for a league BOARD, where everybody reading it is somebody else; Home is addressed to **one** golfer, and both clients printed *"Jerecho set a personal best"* to Jerecho. `HomeWireCopy.viewerVoice` (phone) and `csYouVoice` (desk) resolve the viewer's own name to **You** in the subject seat and **you** in every other, and **second person takes its copula** — *"You have posted 8 weeks running"*, never *"You has"*. The post's own `member_id` is the authority, which is what stops two golfers who share a given name being confused for each other; D238's person-homed rail carries no member row, so there the name answers, and the only name either client will ever touch is the viewer's own.
- **CONFLICT · `surfaces/home.md` §1.4.** That spec rules the buckets into row markers and *not* into section heads, and this overrides it. The clause was written against the mockup's five-row wire, where three quiet lines with day markers read beautifully; on a real account with fifteen rows and no photographs it is the wall the owner photographed. The spec's own words — Today, This week, Earlier — are kept and `Coming up` is added, because the wire's order runs **outward from today** and what is coming leads what has gone.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §5 (typography carries the hierarchy), §7 (do not make every feed item visually equal), §8 (three tiers on every screen), §27 (remove visual debt), §32 (structure without cards); `UI_AUDIT` H-05; DEF-3; D201 (one fact, one place); R-C / D234 (the copy producer is shared, the layout is not).
- **Expected user benefit:** the front page reads as an edition — a dateline, then what is under it — instead of a table of counts. The rows a golfer can act on are the biggest things on it. Fifteen rows become eight. And the app stops talking about him in the third person.
- **Tradeoffs:** the fold means **a league-note count is now one line for every league at once**, so a golfer with four leagues sees *"4 leagues · 14 league notes"* rather than four named rows — the names stop being an aid past two and the board is one tap away either way. `Coming up` is a fourth dateline where the design named three. The desk takes **only** the copy half (D234: producers are shared, layout is not) — its Home feed is still one row per post with no fold at all, which is pre-existing and named here rather than fixed. And the wire's stamp is a clock only where the item carries a parseable date: `home_dispatch` may send `at` as an instant rather than a calendar date, and a row whose `at` is a timestamp prints no stamp instead of one that is a day out (L-07).

### D286 · Compete's sections have a size, and where you stand is a figure, not a clause
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on his own phone: *"Things look text heavy, sections arent differentiated"*) · UI level · extends D285 to the second surface · `BRIEF` §5–§8, §17, §27, §32; `UI_SYSTEM` §1.6, §8, §9.1, §9.6, §9.9; `OWNER_RULINGS` R-D

- **Current mechanic:** Compete renders a masthead, then `YOUR SEASONS` and `YOUR MOMENTS` as **`csEyebrow` — mono 12pt tracked caps in `mut`** — over rows whose own name is `name` 17 caps in `ink`. The head is the QUIETEST object in its own section, so a page of two seasons and one moment reads as one flat list with two labels dropped into it. Under each head, the season row is three stacked lines and **the standing is the fourth clause of the third one**: *"2nd of 2, 4 back of Galen"* at `columnS` 12 in `mut`, the same size, weight and colour as the week, the money and the stage word. Below the last row there is **a screen and a half of nothing**, and the page's only act is a 12pt link in the top-right corner, where a thumb cannot reach — and it wrapped, dropping its `↗` onto a second line beside the dateline.
- **Problem:** this is the tab a competitive golfer opens to find out **where he stands**, and the answer is set smaller and quieter than the name of the league it belongs to. `UI_SYSTEM` §9.9 names this failure by name for the HCP and the gap — *the two facts that keep escaping into prose* — and the rank is the third. Meanwhile §8 budgets a section head as *"an agate label + a 1px rule"*, which is right above a block whose rows carry their own weight (a table, a form) and wrong above rows that are quiet type: there the head has to BE the step, or the page has no sections whatever its headings say. D285 answered exactly this on Home's wire and built the object that answers it; a product with two answers to one question has neither.
- **Recommendation:** **three changes, and the first is the one that makes it an idiom.** **(1) ONE SECTION HEAD, AT TWO WEIGHTS.** `CSSectionHead` gains `weight:` — `.label` (the shipped agate-plus-rule, and the **default**, so the nine surfaces that take it do not move) and `.display` (`displayS` 24 in `ink`, no rule, no box, `s5` of air above). Home's dateline stops being Home's private object and becomes this weight; Compete is its second caller, which is what makes it the product's head rather than one page's. **(2) THE STANDING IS A FIGURE.** `CompeteRoot.Row.rank` carries `place` and `of`, and the row draws them as the **rule-and-figure** the leaderboard and the ME strip already are — `2ND`, a 2pt rule the width of its column, `OF 8` in agate beneath — and the sentence **stops printing the rank** (`SeasonFacts.seasonLine(rank: false)`, the producer's third grain) so the fact is said once. A row with no honest standing draws no figure and is quieter for it (§7). **(3) THE PAGE GETS A FOOT, NOT A FILLER.** `s6`, a heavy rule, and the two doors `CompeteRoot.empty` already names as the alternatives to starting something — *Join with a code* · *Find golfers* — in the product's own door-row grammar. Neither is lit: L-25 gives the page one ember and the masthead has it. Everything below them stays empty, because §27 forbids decorative UI with no purpose and §32 forbids answering white space with a card.
- **AND THE FIGURE IS DRAWN ONLY WHERE THERE IS A STANDING TO DRAW.** A **running** season takes `standing.rank of standing.of`; a **wrapped** one takes `last_season.my_rank of .of`, which is the payload's own final answer and is nil rather than guessed for a squads member and on a v1 payload. **Preseason, forming and the Cup Final draw nothing.** A season that has not teed off ranks everybody 1st of N on zero points and printing `1ST` over that is a lie in 27pt type; through the Final `rank` is the live table and never the locked seed (D138), so a figure there is the one number a finalist must not be told twice.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §5 (typography carries the hierarchy), §7 (do not make every item visually equal), §8 (a primary, a secondary and a tertiary on every screen), §17 (an invitation, not a filler), §27 (remove visual debt), §32 (structure without cards); `UI_SYSTEM` §1.6 (how a rank is set), §9.9 (the facts that escape into prose), §9.2 (a figure at 27 or above carries a rule-and-figure); D201 (one fact, one place); R-D (the two heads keep the owner's words — only their size changes).
- **Expected user benefit:** the page answers *where do I stand* from across the room. Two seasons read as `2ND OF 2` and `1ST OF 2` in board type; the section heads are unmistakably heads; the page ends in two acts a thumb can reach instead of in nothing.
- **Tradeoffs:** three `.display` heads on one viewport is the top of §8's ≤3 budget, so a fourth section on this page would need one of them to fold. The `.label` weight stays the default and **the sweep did not promote it anywhere else** — the Golfers tab and the schedule carry the same defect but also carry six sections and two cards on one scroll, and promoting six agate labels to six 24pt heads makes those pages worse, not better; they need their own pass and are named here rather than half-fixed. The desk takes **no copy** from this entry (nothing shared moved: `seasonLine`'s new grain is only called where a figure is drawn, and the desk draws none), but it does owe the head weight — `.grouphead` is still mono 11.5px tracked caps over stat blocks, and that belongs to the desk's own typography pass under §14.5, where the roles land one at a time.

### D287 · A round is on the front page once, and the wire opens with its own dateline
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on his own phone: *"Things look text heavy, sections arent differentiated"* — the review pass over D285/D286) · UI level · `BRIEF` §5, §7, §8, §27; `UI_SYSTEM` §15.1; D201

- **Current mechanic:** with D285 shipped, the owner's Home opens THE WIRE with **one loose row above the first dateline** — `Fri, Sep 4 — You posted 89 at UNM Championship` — and then draws **that same round three rows below**, under `THIS WEEK`, as the wire's 68pt slat with the face, the sentence and an `89 GROSS` rule-and-figure. The loose row is `HomeDigest`'s **quiet frame**: on a day with nothing new since the seen-mark it resurfaces the best recent round so that *"an open never reveals nothing"* (D27). It already yields to the ranked deck — `HomeDigest.make(spent:)` takes `ranked.spentRounds` — and `HomeDigest`'s own comment states the law in as many words: *"on a quiet day that is the same round the CIRCLE card is already carrying … The digest yields."*
- **Problem:** it yields to the **deck** and not to **THE WIRE**, and the wire is where rounds actually draw. So the page says one round twice, at two weights, 400pt apart — which is D201 (one fact, one place) failing on the surface D201 was written for. It is worse than a plain repeat, because the quiet frame's sentence is built as `day — line`, so the row puts a **date back at the head of a sentence**: `Fri, Sep 4 — …` is the 34pt leading date column D285 deleted, in prose, in the first row of the wire. And being `period: nil` it files **above** the first dateline, so `THE WIRE`'s agate name labels one orphan row and `COMING UP` starts immediately under it — two headers for one block, the outer one quieter than the inner one, which is the very complaint being answered.
- **Recommendation:** **two changes, and both are deletions.** **(1) THE QUIET FRAME YIELDS TO THE WIRE.** `HomePage.make` gathers the round ids the buckets are about to draw and drops the digest row when the quiet frame's `roundId` is one of them. It is decided in the **producer**, on the round id, so it is a test and not a look — and it is narrow: the `since` frame is a genuine summary of what changed and is never dropped, and a quiet frame whose round the wire is *not* drawing still renders, because that is the day the frame exists for. **(2) THE WIRE'S BLOCK NAME GIVES WAY TO ITS FIRST DATELINE.** Where the rows run under datelines, the dateline **is** the head; an 11pt agate label in `mut` stacked directly on a 24pt `displayS` head in `ink` is §27's *repetitive header*, and the parent reading quieter than the child is the hierarchy inverted. `HomeSectionRule(page.wireTitle)` is drawn on every other branch — the first-round rows, the redacted state, the failed read, the wire's empty block, the roster empty — because none of those carry a dateline and all of them need the block named.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §5 (typography carries the hierarchy), §7, §8 (three tiers, and the outer head may not be the quietest), §27 (repetitive headers, remove visual debt); `UI_SYSTEM` §15.1; D201 (one fact, one place); D27 (the quiet frame's purpose, honoured rather than removed).
- **Expected user benefit:** the wire opens on `COMING UP` and the golfer's 89 is told once, as the slat, with its gross. One row and one header leave the page.
- **Tradeoffs:** on a genuinely quiet day whose one recent round is in the feed, Home now shows **no** quiet frame — the wire's own rows are the reveal, which is the outcome D27 wanted and not the sentence it wrote. The desk takes **no** half of this: `HomeDigest` is phone-side, and the web's Home has neither the fold nor the datelines (named in D285's tradeoffs, still open).

### D288 · The desk's wire folds, and its datelines outrank their rows
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on cupseason.app in mobile Safari: *"Better but these are bland… Trophies and recent rounds also not engaging… Think Strava"* — the photograph is six consecutive rounded rectangles, each a grey circle-with-a-flag and two lines of text, with the same fact printed once per league) · UI level · `VISUAL_PASS` §1; `BRIEF` §5, §6, §7, §27, §32; `UI_SYSTEM` §1.3, §9.2, §14.5; D201, D217, D234, D285, D287

- **Current mechanic:** the web's Home feed renders **one `.hfcard` per post** (`postRow`), and `round_to_board()` fans one round into every league the golfer belongs to — so two leagues print the same sentence twice, one card apart. The dedupe was written and has never run: `renderHomeFeed` filters posts on `p.round_id`, and `round_id` is in neither post select (`HCOLS`, `PCOLS`), so the filter has read `undefined` since the day it was written. Every row is the same object at the same weight — `bg1`, a 1px border, a 14px radius — and `.hfcard.quiet` adds a **dashed** edge, which is the exact rectangle the owner photographed six of. Above them, `.feedsec` is mono 10.5 in `dim` while the rows beneath are 15px/650 in `ink`: the section head is the quietest thing in its own section. D285 and D287 fixed all of this on the phone and named the desk's half as owed in their own tradeoffs; this is that half.
- **Problem:** the phone and the desk now disagree about what the wire IS (D234). The phone folds, cuts datelines and says a round once; the desk stacks. And the desk's failure is not "no fold" alone — it is that **the fold, the hierarchy and the weights are one idea**: folding without a head leaves a shorter wall, and a head without a fold labels a wall. A screen that is ALL cards is finding 1 of the audit arriving on the desk (§6, §32): the card cannot mark rank when it is the only shape, so six items of five different kinds read as six of one kind.
- **Recommendation:** **one producer, four datelines, three weights, and one line at the foot.** (1) `csHomeFold` is a PURE function — the desk's twin of `HomeFeedFold` + `HomePage.make`'s wire pass, keeping its rules in its order: a round the deck already told is dropped (`__spentRounds`, F-2); the same league note in two leagues within 48 hours is one note carrying both names; **a moment fanned to two leagues is one moment, keyed on the round** (DF-04 — the owner's own repeat); the rest bucket into `COMING UP · TODAY · THIS WEEK · EARLIER`; and a **rundown says a date once** (`sayItOnce` — a row under `TODAY` prints no stamp, and inside a group a stamp equal to the row above it is dropped). It is a producer and not a look, so it is tested (`tests/homefold.test.mjs`, brace-extracted the way `sunnEngine` is) and the rule cannot drift between the two clients by being written twice in two idioms with no witness. (2) **`.feedsec` becomes `displayS`** — `cs-display-s`, UPPER, `ink`, no rule and no box — so the step to the row beneath is 24 → 17 **and** `ink` → `mut`. (3) **The weights:** a photographed round keeps `.hfstory` full-bleed; a round without one becomes a **slat** — a 1px rule, a 44pt face, the name in `social`, the phrase in `bodyS`, the course and stamp in `agateS`, and the gross as a **bare** `figure` 27 right-flush (§9.2 — a column takes no rule-and-figure); a moment becomes a **line** — one `bodyS` in `mut` and a trailing `agateS` stamp, no avatar and no card. `.hfcard.quiet` and the 4px brand rail on every row are **deleted**. (4) **Every surviving league note is ONE line at the foot** — `Fellas & Who's the bitch? · 14 league notes`, past two leagues `3 leagues · 14 league notes` — the desk's twin of `HomeWireNotes.line`, and it opens the board where the notes live. (5) `round_id` joins `HCOLS`/`PCOLS`, guarded by the retry those selects already carry, so the dedupe that was written finally runs. **No migration.**
- **Principle served:** D201 (one fact, one place) — the rule the repeat breaks; D234 (a change has a phone half and a web half) — this is D285/D287's web half, and both entries named it owed; `BRIEF` §6/§32 (a card is not the answer, and it may not be the only shape); §5/§7 (typography carries the hierarchy, and the outer head may not be the quietest); §27 (repetitive headers); `UI_SYSTEM` §9.2 (a figure in a column takes no rule), §1.3 (`displayS` does not spend the one `display` a viewport gets).
- **Expected user benefit:** the screen he photographed loses five of its six rectangles. Six identical cards saying three facts become: the rounds, as slats under datelines that can be read from across the room, and one grey line at the foot that says how many league notes there were and opens them.
- **Tradeoffs:** **`COMING UP` has a bucket in the producer and nothing feeds it on the desk.** Merging `watchAll` into the wire is one `.concat` and it was NOT taken, because the desk already prints the coming round in the ME strip's `NEXT` slot, in the ranked deck, and in `#homeUpNext`'s chips — a fourth printing on the same screen is D287's own complaint, and the honest order is to retire the chips first. **The stamp is a date, not a drawing** — §2's drawn card needs `api_course_id` on `home_stories` and cannot be built today, so weight 2b is a slat and not a shape. **The milestone emoji stay** (`🔥 Personal best`): both clients carry the same three strings (`HomeStream.swift:221`), so removing them is a paired change and not a desk-only one. **`Earlier` gains a head it did not have**, so a golfer with a quiet week sees one more line of type than before; it is capped at eight rows like every other bucket.

### D289 · A course carries what your golfers thought of it, and the record is the courses you like
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on cupseason.app in mobile Safari: *"Trophies and recent rounds also not engaging… what we thought of the course etc. a record of the courses we like"*) · UI + mechanics level · `VISUAL_PASS` §5; `BRIEF` §11, §12; `UI_SYSTEM` §9.2, §9.11, §16, §22; D201, D234, D272, D275, L-44

- **Current mechanic:** `course_ratings`, `course_rating(text)`, `rate_course(text, numeric)` and `unrate_course(text)` are **applied in production and granted to `authenticated`** (`20261007090000`, pushed 2026-09-07; that file's own "THIS FILE HAS NOT BEEN RUN" header is stale and rule 2 leaves it uncorrected). **Nothing calls any of them.** The desk hardcodes `csStarsSvg(0, true)` under a comment stating the function is unpushed — so every course on the web says `NOT RATED` whatever the database holds — and the phone's rail is a picture that opens a SHEET with a `Rate it` primary, which is a form for a one-tap opinion. `renderCourseBooks` / `CoursesScreen` list every kept course at equal weight in schedule-then-recency order: there is no record of the courses you like, only a list of the courses you have been to. And `course_ratings` carries `stars` and nothing else, so **"what we thought of the course" has no text home in this database at all** — the owner's own clause, unbuilt because there was nowhere to put it.
- **Problem:** the most-asked-for surface in the second round of feedback is the one that is fully unblocked and entirely unwired. Worse, the two clients disagree about what rating a course IS: the desk says it is impossible, the phone says it is a form. And a record of "the courses we like" cannot be built out of stars alone — a list of numbers is not a thing you read, which is exactly why the owner's sentence has two halves ("what we thought" AND "a record").
- **Recommendation:** **the rail is the control, the sentence has a column, and the record is one read.** (1) **`course_ratings.note`**, nullable, 140 characters, written by the SAME call: `rate_course` is dropped and recreated as `(p_course_id, p_stars, p_note text default null)` — an OVERLOAD would make every two-argument call ambiguous, so the drop is required and the grant is re-issued with it. **Null leaves the note alone, `''` takes it off**, so a client that predates notes moves a star without erasing a sentence it never saw. (2) `course_rating` returns your own note and up to **three of your golfers'** — the same set the `friends` mean is drawn from, never the stranger branch, and never an uncredited one; the predicate is extracted to `course_rating_is_mine(uuid, uuid)` so two copies of it cannot drift. (3) **`my_course_ratings()`** — every course you have rated, your star, your sentence and the community's mean and count, in ONE read, because §5.4's record is a list sorted by your own rating and twenty courses cannot be twenty round trips. (4) **The act is one tap and it is reversible**: the rail is 32pt, each star's two halves are the target, the fill sweeps left-to-right in 180ms, `rate_course` runs immediately, the returned aggregate re-tallies the figures from the server's own arithmetic, and tapping the value you already hold calls `unrate_course`. No confirm, no submit, no sheet on the way in. (5) **The aggregate is a rule-and-figure** — `figure` 40, the drawn rail beside it, a 2pt `ink` rule under both, `CUP SEASON GOLFERS · n RATINGS` in agate, and `Your golfers 4.5 · Yours 5.0` beneath. **No gold in any state**: an average of opinions is not earned (§2.4). (6) **KEPT COURSES becomes COURSES YOU LIKE** — the rated, best first, each with its rail, its drawn card as the row's own plate and its sentence in `story`; the unrated fall below a rule under `ALSO KEPT · n` with an unfilled rail and `RATE IT`.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §11/§12 (a course is an editorial object and a rating is satisfying content, not a form field); §16 (a number is an object — the mean takes a rule and a size, not a chip); D201 (one fact, one place — the predicate and the aggregate each have one home); D234 (a change has a phone half and a web half, and here the two halves currently contradict each other); L-44 (null, never zero: `NOT YOURS YET`, never a dash); §22 (the one thing that moves is the thing you touched).
- **Expected user benefit:** the answer to *"what we thought of the course"* and *"a record of the courses we like"* — both of them, in the product, on both clients. A golfer taps a star and it is set; the course page says what their friends thought and prints the sentences; the You tab's course list stops being an inventory and becomes an opinion, sorted.
- **Tradeoffs:** **`rate_course` is DROPPED and recreated, so between the client push and the database push a two-argument call from a live phone is a missing function** — the client treats every rating failure as "not rated" and the rail stays tappable, so the failure is invisible and self-healing, but the honest order is database first. **`my_course_ratings()` is a fourth RPC on a feature that had three**, and it is a convenience: without it the record still renders from the local cache the act writes, one course at a time, which is what a client older than the migration gets. **The note is ONE line, on both clients**: 140 characters, saved on blur or Enter, with no formatting and no second screen — a golfer who wants to write a paragraph about a course cannot, and that is the cap the column carries rather than a UI we can widen later without a migration. **Three of your golfers' sentences is a cap, not a page**: there is no "see all", because a course page is not a review site.

### D290 · A planned round shows the holes, and the drawing never invents one
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on cupseason.app in mobile Safari: *"Future rounds should highlight holes if we have that info… Think Strava"*) · UI level · `VISUAL_PASS` §2, §4; `BRIEF` §7, §16, §20; `UI_SYSTEM` §9.4, §10.1, §10.2; D234, D261, D272, D289

- **Current mechanic:** a planned round is a date, a tee time, a field and a comment thread. **Nothing about the golf course is on it** — the desk's `renderRoundSheet` prints `TEE · RATING / SLOPE · PAR` as one grey meta line and stops; the phone's `ScheduledRoundSheet` offers a link that says *"See the tees and the card"* and pushes a second screen. The facts the sentence asks for are all cached and all readable: `my_schedule.course_id` (`20260924093000:184`), `api_course_holes.par` and `.handicap` (readable by any authenticated golfer, `api_course_holes_read`), and `api_course_tees.par_total / total_yards / course_rating / slope_rating`. And `my_course_books` — the phone's whole offline store — selects `hole`, `par` and `si` and **not `yardage`**, so the phone draws its card height-by-PAR while the desk draws it height-by-yardage: the same course, two shapes, filed in `Course.swift`'s own header as D-2.
- **Problem:** the owner is asking for the one thing a golfer actually wants the night before — *which holes decide this round* — and the product has the data and prints a link. Worse, the two clients disagree about what a course LOOKS like (D234), and the reason is one unselected column. Separately, `csDrawnCardSvg` and `CSDrawnCard` both fill the #1 stroke hole `gold`, which spends the metal on a thing nobody won (§2.4) — already ruled and taken in D289, and named here because the drawing is this entry's subject.
- **Recommendation:** **the plan draws its course, and the drawing is the same on both clients.** (1) `my_course_books` gains per-hole **`yards`** — one key in one `jsonb_build_object`, `create or replace`, same signature and same grants — so the phone's offline card is height-by-yardage like the desk's. A client older than the file ignores the key; a client newer than it keeps the height-by-par fallback both already carry. (2) **THE PLAN'S OWN BLOCK**, above the field, on both clients: the card drawn full width; **THE THREE THAT DECIDE IT** — the three lowest stroke indexes as three `figure` 27 hole numbers on one rule with `PAR 5 · 604 · SI 1` in agate beneath each; **the turn** in `col` — `OUT 36 · IN 36 · 7,068 YDS · 73.3 / 137`; **your history here** — *"You have played Papago 4 times · best 78"*, off the 400 rounds the client already holds; and **the rating** from D289, so the night before you play you see what your golfers thought of it. (3) **THE DEGRADE IS THE POINT.** No `course_id` (a hand-typed course) → no card, no three-hardest, no invented pars: the row keeps its tee time, its field and its game. A tee whose card was never cached → the drawing returns nothing at all and the block prints `CourseBookCopy.noCard`, which already says the right thing. *Fake data as ornament is less premium than a plain colour* — three blind reviewers, in three sentences.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §7 (an item earns its weight from what it can prove) and §20 (the imagery ladder — the drawn card is rung 2 and it is drawn from real par, stroke index and yardage or not at all); §16 (a golf number is a visual object: three hole numbers on a rule, not a sentence with numbers in it); `UI_SYSTEM` §10.2 (a plate carries no caption teaching the reader how to read it); D234 (a change has a phone half and a web half — and here the two halves were drawing different courses); L-44 (nothing is invented).
- **Expected user benefit:** the answer to *"future rounds should highlight holes if we have that info"*. A plan stops being a calendar entry and becomes the course you are about to play: its shape, the three holes that will decide it, its length and rating, and how you have done there before.
- **Tradeoffs:** **THE FEED ROUND STILL CANNOT DRAW.** `home_stories` returns `course text` — a LABEL — and no `api_course_id` and no `live_round_id` (`20260908090000:104–109`), so a round in the wire has nothing to draw FROM and stays D288's slat.
