Unblocking it is a `drop function` + recreate (adding a column to a `returns table` is a 42P13) plus its grant, and that migration is NOT written here: this wave already carries two, and a third that changes the shape of the front page's own producer deserves its own. **`OUT`/`IN` on a plan are the COURSE's pars, not a score** — the block is labelled with the tee it is drawn from so the two can never be read as one. **The three-hardest is stroke index alone**, which is a fact about the card and not about the golfer: a scratch player's three hardest holes are not a bogey golfer's, and the product has no model that would know the difference. **The desk's block does not open a course page**, because the desk has no per-course page other than the record on You; the row is a door there and not here. **AND THE RECEIPT IS NOT DRAWN.** `VISUAL_PASS` §2's third rung — a posted round showing its COURSE's card with the gross sitting on it, under `THE COURSE, NOT THE ROUND` — is free on the desk (`window.career.rows` now carries `api_course_id`) and is NOT free on the phone: `ReceiptSeed` has no course id, `round_card` does not return one, and threading it through would touch the seed, its decoder and every caller. A desk-only half breaks D234, so it waits for its own pass rather than shipping as one client's feature.

### D291 · The case gets three shelves, the record becomes one figure, and a milestone opens the afternoon it happened
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on cupseason.app in mobile Safari: *"Trophies and recent rounds also not engaging. Maybe that is waiting photo dynamic but it should be more of a visual. Think Strava"*) · UI level · `VISUAL_PASS` §3; `BRIEF` §6, §7, §8, §16, §32; `UI_SYSTEM` §5.2, §9.2, §9.5, §17; D67, D177, D210, D234, D288, D289

- **Current mechanic:** the display case is already right in every way the audit measured and wrong in the only way the owner noticed. `renderTrophyCase` (`index.html:17763`) and `TrophySlats` (`RecordPage.swift`) both draw **slats, not tiles**: a 28pt DRAWN mark, the name in `name` caps, a dated `agateS` sub-line, one `rule` on the top edge, and C4's engraver on a fresh arrival. `ACH_META` / `TrophyMeta.ach` give ten distinct glyph keys and `threshold` / `streak` / `lowRound` carry a numeral, so **no two achievements share a mark** (§5.2 kept) and there is no colour emoji anywhere in it. But **every slat is the same height, every mark is 28pt, and THE CUP sits at exactly the weight of "Posted"** — a run of eleven identical 50pt rows in which nothing outranks anything. Above it, `renderCareerRecord`'s `.recgrid` is four **bordered `bg1` boxes** carrying 26px serif numerals in `gold` — four cards in a row on a page the owner already photographed six cards of. Below it, `#youRecent` is `.fine` rows: a 13.5px bold sentence, a mono `79 GROSS` and a second grey line, six of them, identical. And `#trophyCase` still carries `class="room-dusk"` from the retired tile era — the class re-asserts the dusk **ink** (`#F4F1EE`) and asserts **no ground**, so in the light theme the whole case is near-white type on paper.
- **Problem:** the owner's three words are *"not engaging"*, and the diagnosis is not compliance — it is **scale and consequence**. `BRIEF` §7 says do not make every item visually equal; §8 wants a primary, a secondary and a tertiary on every screen. A case with a Cup, a broken 80 and a four-week streak at one size has none of the three. And the ONE thing on the surface that is genuinely engaging is invisible: `my_achievements` has returned **`round_id` since 2026-09-02** and `renderTrophyCase` already emits `data-achr` → `openRoundReceipt`, so BROKE 80 already opens the afternoon it happened — buried under an undifferentiated run of equal slats where nobody finds it. *A badge is inert; a milestone that opens its round is not.*
- **Recommendation:** **three shelves, three sizes, three heads, and one door.** (1) `TrophyCase.tiles` gains a **shelf** on every tile and both clients render the case grouped: **HARDWARE** (every `my_trophies` row — the Cup, the points crown, a Major, the Ryder, runner-up) at a **44pt** mark with the year trailing; **BESTS** (`sub_100/90/80`, `personal_best`, `low_round`, `most_improved` — what your scoring did) at 28pt, its sub-line rewritten to **the round it was won on** — `79 at Papago · Aug 24` — and **the whole slat a door into that round's receipt** — and **a milestone prints the figure it is ABOUT**, so a threshold reads `79 at Papago · Aug 24` and a personal best reads `4.1 vs course · Papago · Aug 24`, because taking the gross for both put the identical sentence under BROKE 80 and PERSONAL BEST whenever one round earned them together, which is the owner's own complaint arriving inside the fix for it; **ALONG THE WAY** (`first_round`, the streaks, Iron Man — what your turning up did) at 28pt in `mut`, quiet and **doorless even where the row carries a `round_id`** — three shelves have to read as three ranks, and the ladder is the 44pt mark, then the door, then neither; that round's receipt is still reachable from Recent rounds, the board and the form row. The shelf rule, the head, the mark size and the sub-line are **one producer on both clients** (`TrophyShelf`, `TrophyCase.shelves`, `TrophyCase.milestoneSub` in the Kit; `csTrophyShelf` / `csMilestoneSub` on the desk, D234). (2) **The record is a rule-and-figure** (§9.2): the largest count as `figure` 40 over a 2pt `ink` rule with `CUPS` beneath, the rest as bare `figure` 20 on the same baseline, and the settled money as its own `figure` 27 under `SETTLED ACROSS 3 SEASONS`. **In `ink`, not gold** — §9.5 already rules money `ink`, and a *tally of* cups is not the cup: gold stays on the trophy itself, which is where the engraver's needle already spends it. (3) **Recent rounds become `formRowHtml`'s big brother**: the gross as a `figure` 27 right-flush on a shared right edge, the course in `name-s` 15, `AUG 24 · 4.1 VS YOUR PLAYING HCP` in agate beneath, and — where the round carries an `api_course_id` this device has kept a card for — **a 60 × 18 drawing of that course** between the two, from `csDrawnCardSvg`, the same function the plan and the record already draw with. (4) **The empty gets a shape** (§17): four **uncut** marks at 12% under `THE CASE IS EMPTY` and one line. (5) **`room-dusk` comes off the case**, which is a legibility fix and not a design one — and the record and the recent list lose their `.card` wrappers with it, because slats inside a card inside a page is the object he photographed (§32). `TrophyCase.emptyLine` — one 118-character grey sentence — is deleted with them.
- **Principle served:** `BRIEF` §7 (feed items at different weights — a Cup is not a Posted), §8 (a primary, a secondary and a tertiary), §16 (a golf number is an object — the record is one figure on a rule, not four numerals in four boxes), §32 and §6 (a card is not the answer, and the record was four of them); `UI_SYSTEM` §9.2 (the rule-and-figure is reserved for a number that matters, and a repeating column takes a **bare** figure with no rule — which is why the recent-rounds grosses carry none), §9.5 (money is ink), §5.2 (the drawn mark, kept; no glyph shared); D234 (the shelf rule and every produced sentence are one producer, two shapes).
- **Expected user benefit:** the case reads at a glance — silverware first and biggest, the numbers you beat next and each one a door into the round that beat them, the participation quiet at the foot. The record above it is one number you can read across the room. And the recent list stops being six grey paragraphs with numbers in them and becomes a column of grosses with the shape of the course each was shot on.
- **Tradeoffs:** **TWO OF THE TEN MILESTONES CANNOT FIRE.** `low_round` and `most_improved` are declared in `ACH_META` and `TrophyMeta.ach` on both clients, each with its own drawn mark, and **nothing anywhere in the database ever inserts either kind** — not the round trigger (`20260921090000:225-263`, which mints `first_round`, `sub_100/90/80`, `personal_best` and `streak_4/8/12`), not `close_month`, not `close_season`, not any edge function. They are **kept, not deleted**: the marks are correct drawings, `UI_SYSTEM` §5.2 and §9.3 name the stepped bar for MOST IMPROVED by name, and deleting a mapping a future season-close migration would need is how a real trophy silently becomes a `medal`. The honest statement is that the case can hold **eight** kinds today, and the dead pair is filed here rather than dressed up in a doc as evidence the catalogue is ten deep. **The BESTS door degrades to nothing** on an achievement with no `round_id` — a pre-2026-09-02 row — and the slat is then exactly what it is today. **The 60 × 18 drawing is the COURSE, not the round**: the strokes are not in `window.career.rows` and `home_stories` still carries no course id (D290's open tradeoff), so a round whose course this device has never kept a card for draws nothing at all rather than eighteen invented par 4s (L-44). **The recent-rounds list is web-only.** The phone deleted `RecentRoundsList` deliberately in Wave 3 (YRS-22 — an identity page is not an admin tool, and deletion belongs on the round's own receipt) and has the form row in its place; D234 shares the producers and the sentences, not the layout, so the row's words are `RoundCopy`'s and its shape is the desk's alone.

### D292 · A moment yields to the round it is about, and the record counts the course it leads with
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, on cupseason.app in mobile Safari: *"Better but these are bland"* — the review pass over D288–D291, standing in for him) · UI level · `VISUAL_PASS` §1; `BRIEF` §7, §27; `UI_SYSTEM` §11; D201, D217, D234, D285, D288, D289, D291

- **Current mechanic:** `round_moments()` writes its post with **`round_id = new.id`** — the ROUND's own id (`20260921090000:315` and `:330`, both rails). Both folds key a moment on that id and both start their `seen` set **empty**: the desk's `csHomeFold` rule 2b seeds `seenR` from nothing, and the phone's `HomeFeedFold.fold` seeds `seenRounds` from nothing. So the key deduplicates a moment **against other copies of itself** across leagues — which is what D217 and D288 were written to do — and never against **the round row standing in the same wire**. A golfer who breaks 80 therefore gets both: the slat, `Jade · ⛳ Broke 80 — first time · 78 · TROON NORTH`, and three rows above it the line, `Jade broke 80 for the first time.` One round, one bucket, two rows.
- **Problem:** this is the owner's own photograph — *the same fact printed twice* — surviving the entire wave that was authorised to remove it, in a new costume. D288 deleted the repeat that came from `round_to_board()` fanning a round across leagues and left the repeat that comes from a moment and its round both being in the wire, which is the same failure of D201 by a different producer. It hid behind the fixture: `tests/homefold.test.mjs` and the desk's shooter both gave the moment a round id (`R3x`) that no round row carried, so 25 assertions and four screenshots agreed the fold was right. **A rule with a witness that cannot see the production shape has no witness.** And the milestone is not lost by dropping the line — both clients already print it on the round row itself (`HomeCopy.milestone`, `feedRow`'s `milestone`), from `home_stories`' own `is_pr` / `is_sub80` / `is_first`.
- **Recommendation:** **rule 2b's set opens with the rounds the wire is already drawing.** On both clients, before the moment loop runs, seed the seen-rounds set with the `round_id` of every round item that survived rule 1; a moment whose round is in that set is dropped, exactly as a moment whose round another league already claimed is dropped. It is one statement in each idiom and it keeps the rules in their order (D234). The round row is the better rendering — it carries the face, the course, the gross AND the milestone phrase — so, as with `spent`, the line yields to it. Where the round is NOT in the wire (spent by the deck, or older than the feed window) the moment survives and is the only telling, unchanged. **Separately (D289's record):** `renderCourseBooks` heads the list `Courses you like · N rated` where `N` counts only the rows beneath, and the LEAD — the biggest, most-liked course on the page — is excluded from its own record. A golfer who has rated three courses reads *"2 rated"* under a heading naming the thing he does most. When the lead is rated it belongs **inside** the group it leads: the head moves above it and counts it. When the lead is unrated (the course you are about to play, which outranks a rating) the order is unchanged and the count is already honest. **And the phone's record dek says `a 80`** where `RecordPage.swift:14`'s own comment quotes the intended sentence as *"the best of them **an 80**"* — the article is picked by the numeral's spoken form, which is the same arithmetic `csOrdinalSuffix` already does for a hole.
- **Principle served:** D201 (one fact, one place) — third time on this surface, and the first two fixes did not generalise; D234 (a change has a phone half and a web half) — the hole is identical in both idioms and so is the fix; `BRIEF` §27 (a screen may not say a thing twice), §7 (weights exist so a thing is told at ONE of them); `UI_SYSTEM` §11 (a course is an editorial object — a record that omits its own front page is not a record).
- **Expected user benefit:** the wire stops printing a milestone twice on the day it is earned, which is the exact shape of the complaint that opened this wave. The record counts what he has actually rated. And the sentence at the top of his own record is grammatical.
- **Tradeoffs:** **the moment's LEAGUE names go with it.** A moment folded across two leagues carries `Fellas & Who's the bitch?` on its line; the round slat it now yields to names the course and not the leagues, so on a milestone day the wire says *which round* and no longer *which leagues heard about it*. That is the right trade — the leagues are one tap away on the board, the round is the fact — and it is the same trade rule 1 already makes for `spent`. **The fixtures were the real defect and are corrected with the rule**: `tests/homefold.test.mjs` gains the production shape (a moment carrying its round's own id, with that round in the wire) so this cannot silently return, and the desk shooter's `R3x` becomes `R3`. **The `ALSO KEPT` count is untouched** — an unrated lead still sits above `Courses you like`, un-headed, because a course you are about to play is not evidence of a course you like. **No migration, no new read, no producer change**: both folds already hold every round they need, and the article is arithmetic on a numeral already in hand.

### D293 · A photograph is not a score — a photo can go on a round you already posted
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, from his own phone on build 733: *"I just posted a round at Dinosaur mountain but I cant go back to add a photo. I may have missed that option to."* · and *"Our scorecard looks good lets show it off."*) · MECHANIC level, because it touches §16 · `BRIEF` §20; `UI_SYSTEM` §10.1; spec §16; D36, D37, D59, D234, D284, D289

- **Current mechanic:** a round photograph reaches a round **exactly once, at post time**. `post_round` takes `p_photo_path`, the composer uploads to `media/{uid}/{uuid}.jpg` and rides the path on the write, and that is the whole of it — `grep p_photo_path` over `Generated/Rpc.swift` returns `post_round` and `set_profile` and nothing else. There is no RPC anywhere that attaches, replaces or removes a photograph on a round that already exists, and there never has been: §16 says a posted round is not mutated, D37 killed `rounds_owner_update` by name, and the only write left on a posted round is `delete_round`. At post time the option does exist and is **buried** — `Add a photo` and `Scan the card` are `CSMini` pills under a `Details` head, below the fold, beside the date chip. On the desk they are the same two buttons in `#postPhotoRow`.
- **Problem:** the owner posted a round at Gold Canyon Dinosaur Mountain and could not go back to photograph it, and his second sentence — *"I may have missed that option to"* — is the more damning half: he assumed the failure was his. It was not. **The product asks for the photograph at the one moment a golfer is least able to supply it**: the score is typed in the car park when the round is over, and the photograph was taken on the 12th, gets picked over dinner, or arrives from somebody else in the group two days later. The audit and the re-score reached the same conclusion independently — *photography is the single biggest ceiling on this product's emotional appeal and premium feel* — and the product currently makes it hard to supply. A golfer who attached the **wrong** photograph had no way back either, which is the same hole from the other side.
- **Recommendation:** **two narrow security-definer RPCs, `set_round_photo(p_round, p_photo_path)` and `clear_round_photo(p_round)`**, each touching `rounds.photo_path` and nothing else, on a round the caller owns, granted to `authenticated` and never to `anon` (D37). Two names rather than one nullable argument, because `set_profile`'s convention is that **null leaves a field alone** and a single call would have to mean the opposite of what this codebase's other photo writer means by the same shape; `rate_course` / `unrate_course` (D289) is the precedent that reads correctly. The replaced or removed object is **reclaimed from storage in the same statement that drops the reference** — the lesson `delete_round` learned on 2026-09-01, where *"prod already carries orphans from this"*. The path is fenced to `^{auth.uid()}/`, which is `set_profile`'s own guard: without it a signed-in golfer could point his own round at somebody else's private object and then read it through the round's signing call. On both clients the affordance lands **on the round's own receipt, in the photograph's own slot** — the same place D284 put the delete, and the place a golfer looking at a round he posted is already looking. A round of his with no photograph offers `Add a photo`; one with a photograph offers `Replace photo` and a two-tap `Remove photo`.
- **Principle served:** **§16, correctly scoped.** §16 protects a NUMBER: its subject is the chain from a standing back to the arithmetic that produced it — gross, rating, slope, tee, date, course, the index that day, the differential the trigger derived, the season it scored in. Change any of those after the fact and a table that was true on Sunday is false on Monday with nothing in the record saying so, which is the whole of what the law forbids and the whole of why `rounds_owner_update` was killed. **A photograph is in none of that chain**: it is not an input to `score_round()`, it is read by no standing, no `cup_points()` band, no `month_rank`, no `close_month()`; `home_stories`, `home_feed` and `round_card` all read `rounds.photo_path` **live** rather than snapshotting it, and no `posts` row carries a copy — so a photograph attached on Tuesday changes what an afternoon looks like and changes no figure anywhere in the product. It is metadata about the round in exactly the sense the profile photo is metadata about the golfer, and `set_profile` has always let that one change. D36 (the photos arc: the round is the fact, the photo is garnish — which is the same distinction from the other end); D234 (both clients, one commit); L-32 (a failed write says so where the finger is).
- **Expected user benefit:** the golfer photographs the round when he has the photograph, not when he has the score. The scorecard he wants to show off can be scanned into the composer **and** photographed onto the round afterwards. And a wrong photograph has a way back, which is the half of "attach" that nobody asks for until they need it.
- **Tradeoffs:** **the argument above is the whole safety of this, so it is enforced rather than trusted.** The migration's self-check derives its forbidden list from `information_schema.columns` — every column on `rounds` except `photo_path`, `id` and `profile_id` is forbidden **by name** in the deployed source, so a column added to `rounds` next season is sealed the day it is added and nobody has to remember this file; the check also raises if either function writes anything but `update rounds set photo_path`, if any touch of `rounds` is not fenced to `profile_id = v_me`, if the grant to `authenticated` is missing, or if `anon` can reach either one. **No new photograph is imagery the product does not own** (`BRIEF` §20): this is the golfer's own camera roll, the one rung §10.1 already ranks first. **`api_courses.latitude` / `longitude` are 0-populated of 93 rows** and the upstream API returns a street address and no coordinates, so aerial or satellite imagery would need geocoding plus a paid tile service and would still yield only a course-level thumbnail, because nothing in the cache describes hole geometry — the imagery question is answered by leaning into what we own, and no imagery API is added here. **The migration is written and NOT run.** Both clients ship the affordance in the same commit and both degrade honestly against a database that does not have the functions: the act is offered, the attempt is made, the just-uploaded object is taken back out so no orphan is left, and the golfer is told *"a photo on a posted round needs the next database push"* — the sentence form `csRateCourse` set. **The album's empty line stops naming the composer** as the only door, because it is no longer the only door.

### D294 · The card a round actually has — the scorecard is the round's own object
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (owner, from his own phone on build 733: *"Our scorecard looks good lets show it off."* · and *"APIs we can pull for interesting visuals, or do we lean into individual holes or scorecard photo/scanning options for the post."*) · MECHANIC level, because it opens a new server read over the scoring spine and it defines when a set of per-hole strokes IS a round's card · `BRIEF` §16, §20, §33; `UI_SYSTEM` §3.3; L-44; D2, D37, D60a, D92, D95, D234, D261, D293

- **Current mechanic:** the product draws a real scorecard — the bone leaf with `HOLE · PAR · HCP` — in **exactly one place**, `CourseCardLeaf`, inside the course page, where it describes a COURSE. A ROUND, which is the object every surface in the product opens, shows a gross, a points figure and a receipt of arithmetic. The per-hole data exists and nothing reads it: `round_holes` (baseline) holds the strokes, written by the composer in holes mode and by the live round's finalize; `round_holes_of()` (20260827130300) reads them under `round_card`'s own visibility rule, is declared in `Generated/Rpc.swift`, and **is called by nothing on either client** — a live read with no reader; `api_course_holes` (20260714050000) caches par, stroke index and yardage per tee, 14,130 rows over 87 courses. The one place a round's holes ARE drawn is `ScorecardSheet` / `openScorecard`, and it is reachable only from a LIVE round, as a link at the foot of the receipt.
- **Problem:** the owner is right that the card looks good, and the product hides it. Two failures compound. **The beautiful object is not on the object it describes**: a golfer opening the round he just posted sees the number he already knew and no picture of how he got there. And **the one place the product does draw a golfer's holes is a link off a foot**, on a sheet that exists for the whole group, so the round's own page has never had a card. The audit's finding 9 names this exact pattern one level up — the settlement card, *"the product's most beautiful object"*, exists **only as a share PNG**, so the golfer who won the match reads a bulleted list while the beautiful thing goes to everybody else. Repeating it here would have been the easy build: render a card into the share artifact and leave the receipt as it was.
- **Recommendation:** **one new read, `round_scorecard(p_round)`, and the card drawn on the round's own receipt on both clients before it is drawn on anything that leaves the app.** The function joins the three caches that already exist and resolves three facts SEPARATELY, returning each only when it can be proved: (1) **the golfer's strokes**, from `round_holes`, and only when the set is WHOLE and it AGREES — exactly `holes_played` rows, 1..n with no gap, summing to `rounds.gross`; (2) **par**, either from the tee the golfer played, pinned by the round's own `rating` and `slope` against `api_course_tees` (`par_source = 'tee'`, and the tee's NAME rides back), or — when that does not pin exactly one tee — from the course, when every cached tee agrees hole for hole (`par_source = 'course'`, and no tee is named because none was identified); (3) **the stroke index**, resolved the same way but asked SEPARATELY. Null, not an empty shape, when there is nothing to draw. On both clients the card lands **between the figures and the receipt**: the figures are what the round was WORTH, the card is what the round WAS, the receipt is how the one became the other. `CSScorecard` is the component, and the SAME component draws the 1080×1350 share artifact — so the golfer sees the object first, on paper, in his own theme, at his own text size.
- **Principle served:** **L-44, which is the whole of the design.** *Never draw eighteen holes you do not have.* Each of the three facts is fenced by a rule that can be checked rather than trusted: the strokes are refused unless they sum to the gross printed above them (a scorecard whose columns do not add up to its own total is worse than no scorecard); par is refused unless the cache PROVES it, either by identifying the tee or by every tee agreeing; **a nine never takes par at all**, because `round_holes` numbers a nine 1..9 whichever nine was walked (`PostCard.inputs` sums `0..<9` for `side == 9`) and nothing in the schema records which — the owner's own Palo Verde round is labelled `· Back` and its strokes are stored as holes 1 through 9, which is the proof rather than the worry. **§33, no badge spam:** the card carries ONE metal. A cell under par is `gold`, the system's EARNED metal; everything else is ink. A card that paints five results in five colours is a heat map with golf written on it. **§20's imagery question, answered by leaning into what we own:** `api_courses.latitude`/`longitude` are 0-populated of 93 rows and nothing in the cache describes hole geometry, so no imagery API is added — par, stroke index and yardage ARE the visual, and they are already ours. **§16 is untouched**: this function writes nothing, changes no mechanic, and no figure it returns was computed by it.
- **Expected user benefit:** the round a golfer posts becomes a thing worth opening. He sees his own front and back nines against the tee he actually played, the two holes he beat in gold, and the two totals that make the number at the top of the page. And the thing he shows the group is the card, not a restatement of the score — the artifact he already wanted.
- **Tradeoffs:** **coverage today is honest and small, and it is measured rather than hoped.** 6 of 214 prod rounds carry strokes; 25 of the 59 that name an API course pin a tee exactly (0 ambiguous); 49 more resolve par by course agreement; **50 of 214 rounds would draw a card at all, and 50 of the 59 that name a real course would.** Every future round that picks a course from the API is in the second group. The 164 that draw nothing draw NOTHING — no empty grid, no invitation, because a posted round cannot be given holes after the fact (§16) and offering a door that does not open is L-32's own failure. **A hole-by-hole post is the composer's `holes` mode and most golfers use `total`** — that is why only 6 rounds have strokes, and moving that number is a composer change this entry does not make. **The migration is written and NOT run.** Both clients fall back to `round_holes_of`, which is live, so a round with strokes draws a strokes-only card TODAY on build 733 and gains its par row the day the owner pushes. **The gold on paper is `leaf-gold` (#795912), 6.4:1 on bone** — the receipt's own comment that "gold ink never touches a leaf (1.68:1)" is about the PAGE's gold, a different value, and the distinction is now written down in the CSS beside the rule.

### D295 · A card with no scores on it is the course's card — AMENDS D294
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (the review pass over D293/D294 and IOS-064–IOS-067, standing in for the owner, against his own account in prod) · MECHANIC level, because it changes the rule D294 exists to define — when a set of holes IS a round's card · `BRIEF` §16, §27; `UI_SYSTEM` §3.3, §11; L-32, L-44; D289, D294

- **Current mechanic:** D294 shipped `round_scorecard(p_round)` resolving three facts separately and returning null "when there is nothing to draw". The line that decides *nothing* is `if v_strokes is null and v_pars is null then return null`, and both clients agree with it: `RoundScorecard.isEmpty` is `holes.isEmpty || (!hasStrokes && !hasPar)`, and `csRoundCardFrom` returns a card for any payload with holes in it. So **par alone is enough to draw a card.**
- **Problem:** par and the stroke index resolve out of `api_course_holes`, which describes the **COURSE** and knows nothing whatever about this round. A round that named a cached course and typed one total therefore resolves a complete eighteen-column par row and a complete index row and **not one score**, and the receipt draws it — under a section head reading `THE CARD`, on the page of a round the golfer played, beside a `Share the card` button offering to render his name and his marker over a grid with nobody's numbers in it. That is the course's card on the round's page, which is precisely the confusion D294 opened by naming: *"the product drew a real scorecard in exactly one place, `CourseCardLeaf`, where it describes a COURSE."* It is also L-32 — a door that does not open — and the "empty grid" L-44 forbids by name, arrived at from the one direction the rule did not look.
  **The owner's own round is the example.** `cbaa7d98` — Gold Canyon Dinosaur Mountain · Black, 2026-09-07, the round the whole wave came from — pins its tee at 70.1/137 and carries **zero `round_holes` rows**. Under D294 as written, the day he pushes the migration that round grows a blank par card and an offer to share it. All three of his rounds that DO carry strokes are on courses with no `api_course_id` at all, so the card in `card-full-17pro.png` is reachable by none of his 19 rounds either way.
  And the mistake propagated into the record: D294's tradeoffs say **"50 of 214 rounds would draw a card"**, and its own deploy-time `notice` counts rounds that "carry strokes **or** name a cached course". The real number is **6** — measured read-only against prod, `with_strokes 6 / would_draw 6`. The other 44 are the blank-card state, counted as coverage.
- **Recommendation:** **the strokes are the card.** `if v_strokes is null then return null` on the server; `isEmpty` is `holes.isEmpty || !hasStrokes` on the phone; `csRoundCardFrom` returns null when no hole carries a stroke on the desk. Par and the stroke index are what the strokes are **printed against** — real, worth resolving, and not a card on their own. The self-check gains a regex for the new line, so the seal enforces this the way it enforces the gross seal, and the closing `notice` counts rounds that carry strokes and nothing else.
- **Principle served:** L-44 (*never draw eighteen holes you do not have* — eighteen pars you did not play are eighteen holes you do not have); L-32 (an act that cannot succeed is not offered — `Share the card` over an empty grid); `BRIEF` §27 (a screen may not say a thing twice — the course's card belongs on the course's page, where it already is); D289's shape (a read answers *this object*, not the catalogue behind it); D234 (one rule, both clients, one commit).
- **Expected user benefit:** the golfer never opens a round he played and finds a scorecard of somebody's course with no scores in it. What he sees is either his card or nothing — and *nothing* is the honest answer for 208 of 214 rounds today.
- **Tradeoffs:** **the coverage number falls from 50 to 6, and that is the point.** The number was never 50; the 44 were the bug. Stating it truthfully makes D294's own deferred item — *the composer defaults to `total`, which is why only 6 rounds have strokes* — the headline it should always have been, and it is the next thing this feature needs rather than a footnote under a coverage figure that flattered it. **D294's tradeoffs paragraph is left standing, wrong number and all.** The log records what was decided, not what turned out to be true; correcting it in place would erase the mistake instead of showing it, and this entry names it by number so the record is auditable in the direction it is read. **The migration was still not run**, so nothing in prod ever saw the old rule — the fix costs one edit to an unrun file rather than a second migration correcting a live function.

### D296 · The server says the sentence the golfer reads — the voice canon wins over D165's copies, D77's pot line and every lowercase raise
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-07** (the owner, on the voice review: *"no doc rewrites just edits as needed"*; the judge's ruling — 186 kept, 5 killed — is the list; this entry records the SERVER half and the two edge-function edits) · UI level (5), copy only: no competition rule, query, guard or grant changes, and one migration under rule 2 · `spec/voice-and-tone.md` (canon); `docs/audit/voice-2026-09-01/ruling.md` rows 10, 57, 60, 66, 68–70; `TERMINOLOGY.md` §2.3, §2.4, §3.1, §4; D37, D77, D82, D111, D160, D165, D201, D234, D249

- **Current mechanic:** 36 kept server findings sit in functions across 20 migrations that have all run in production (prod at 217 applied, through `20261009093000`). Three generators written after D165 re-shout — `set_profile` "GALEN NOW GOES BY …", `run_it_back` "SEASON 2 IS ON. FIRST TEE …", `create_forfeit` "STAKE POSTED: …" with `upper()` on the golfers' own names. Twelve guards raise `'commissioner only'` / `'organizer only'` and a dozen more raise lowercase fragments (`'index out of range'`, `'invalid league code'`, `'crew only'`, `'not your league'`, `'nothing to vote on'`, `'no squads — run form_squads first'`, `'name a rivalry only once it has history'`) that fail the web's `looksLikeOurSentence` gate, so the desk prints *Something went wrong* while the server had said why; the phone has no gate and prints the raw P0001 (ruling row 60, still open). Board posts and pushes carry retired words the SQL lint pins in one inflection only: *session* (`generate_pairings`, `resolve_session`, `delete_event`, `add_event_player`, `create_event`), *duel*, *the tee sheet* / *on the sheet*, *league mate*, *players* / *members*, *Bylaws locked*, *Exhibition* / *the clubhouse*, *champs*, *on the books* for a plan, *counting rounds*, *season bye*, *Tour Card*. `remove_member` promises "mid-season tools are coming" — `suspend_member` shipped on 2026-09-02 (`20260902100000`). `home_dispatch` says "Season two starts when you say it does" to a league in season three. `close_season`'s pot post welds " · settle between yourselves" onto the ledger line, and its champion story is a middot chain that `push/index.ts` cannot split into a title and a body, so the season's biggest push clamps at 80 characters.
- **Problem:** the canon says the joke is delivered straight-faced, function comes first, and the voice never shouts; TERMINOLOGY says one word per thing and a push inherits every row of §2; D160 named the middot chain; D165 ruled natural case at the generator *permanently* and three later files copied pre-D165 bodies. And rule 2 forbids the obvious fix — none of the 20 files may be edited after it has run.
- **Recommendation:** ONE new migration, `20261012090000_the_server_says_the_sentence_the_golfer_reads.sql`, re-creating **45 functions from their LIVE definitions** (`pg_get_functiondef`, the way `20260831120000` was built; each body md5-checked against the newest migration that defines it before a word was touched) with only the sentence changed — **87 edits**. Applied by the six patterns of the judge's §5, **by class, not by line**: (4) natural case at the three shouting generators, and the pride bet is a *forfeit*; (5) the golfer's sentence in every raise — `Only the Pro can do that.` / `Only the organizer can do that.` (the web's own `humanError` substitution, now said at the source), `Index looks off — anywhere from -10 to 54.` (one sentence at all five sites, with V-43 / W-16), `That code didn't match — check it and try again.`, `They're already in.`, `Not your league.`, `No squads yet — set the squads first.`, `Name a rivalry once it has history.`; (3) the ruled word in every form the live functions carry — including four sites the readers did not name, found by grepping prod's own `prosrc`: `'organizer only'` in `open_major` and `resolve_session`, `'not your league'` in `set_league_marker`, `'tagged players'` in `set_round_rsvp`, and *counting rounds* in `close_season`'s last-place post; (6) `Tag up to seven.` — a validation is a field; (2) the pot post says the ledger sentence whole (*Cup Season keeps the ledger; the money moves between friends.* — brand-canon §3, everywhere money appears), the champion story becomes sentences (*… takes the Cup 412–388. Tiebreak: months won this season. Points King: Tash.*), and *Welcome to the league.* is cut. The two false sentences become true (*mid-season, suspend them instead*; *The next season starts when you say it does*). Two edge-function edits ride with it as files: the friend-request email footer names the sender and drops the Tour Card (row 68); the season email says who sends the money — *The Pro sends it on / back* (D129, row 69) — and the cancel mail stops saying the season is off three times (D201, row 70). Grants mirror prod exactly — 41 authenticated, 4 engine-only (`close_season`, `daily_season_tick`, `round_major_story`, `sched_major_story`) — and the file's self-check raises on any overload (preflight 34's rule), lost or gained grant, anon leak, or surviving sentence.
- **Principle served:** the canon (*confidence without volume*; *function comes first*; *the restraint is the joke*); TERMINOLOGY (one word per thing; a push inherits every row); D160 (the copy says what happens to you); D165 (natural case at the generator, permanently — this is its enforcement on the three files that regressed); D234 (one sentence, both clients — the server is the producer both read); rule 2 (a fix is a new migration); D37 (explicit grants, every file).
- **Expected user benefit:** the Pro who taps a guarded control reads *why*, on both clients, instead of a shrug or a P0001; a name change and a new season are announced, not shouted; the champion's push carries the champion as its title and the rungs as its body; the Ryder's board says *week*, the schedule says *schedule*, a forfeit is posted under the name of the sheet that posts it, and the pot post says the one money sentence the brand says everywhere.
- **Tradeoffs:** **two client twins are owed** (D234, named so they land): the web's `humanError` allowlist (`index.html` ~5980) passes `still in the pool` verbatim and must gain `not on a squad yet` — S-11's sentence opens with a count, so the shape gate alone will not pass it; the phone's `HumanError` (`PeopleModels.swift` ~162) passes `already in the league` and must gain `already in` (S-30). Until those land, those two raises print the generic line on that client. The phone still has no shape gate (ruling row 60). `season_payouts.reason = 'Points king'` is a stored key, matched by `close_season` and `recompute_season_payouts`, and is untouched — only the story's separator and case change. The re-creation carries 235 KB of unchanged bodies so that 87 changed sentences can be read against them; that is the price of rule 2, paid once, and the file says which lines moved. **AMENDS:** D165 (its ruling stands; this names the three regressions it did not cover), D77 (the pot line's " · settle between yourselves" clause, replaced by the brand's ledger sentence per brand-canon §3), the D111 lock copy (*Bylaws locked* → *The rules are set*; *Only the Pro can lock the bylaws* → *Only the Pro can start the season*, TERMINOLOGY override 7), and ruling row 57 (the friend-request push body is the email's own sentence, *Their rounds land in your feed* — not *Accept and…*, because the banner tap routes to Requests and does not accept). **CONFLICT (named):** none upward — the voice canon is the higher level and it wins; where a copy decision below it disagreed, it is amended here rather than silently diverged from.

### D298 · The camera roll is a door, not a fallback — a photograph comes in through whichever one the golfer picks
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-08** (owner, from his own phone on build 748: *"when I open a posted round I cant add a photo from camera roll only take one."*) · UI level · D234, D284, D293, IOS-065, IOS-066; `BRIEF` §20; `UI_SYSTEM` §10.1

- **Current mechanic:** every photo door on the phone is one line, and it is the same line in both places (`RoundReceiptSheet.openPicker`, `PostRoundScreen.present`): `if PostPhoto.cameraAvailable { showCamera = true } else { showLibrary = true }`. It was written as a **fallback** — the camera needs `NSCameraUsageDescription` or iOS kills the app, so the library was what a phone got when the app was not allowed to open the camera. The key has been in `project.yml` all along and every phone has a camera, so the condition is **always true on a device** and the else branch has never run on one. The camera roll was bound to a working `.photosPicker` that nothing could reach. The desk has never had this: `#postPhotoFile` and the receipt's `rcptPhotoFile` are `<input type="file" accept="image/*">` with **no `capture`**, which is iOS's own menu — Photo Library · Take Photo · Choose File.
- **Problem:** the owner opened a round he had posted, pressed **Add a photo**, and the camera opened. The picture he wanted was already on his phone. D293 built the second chance precisely because *the score is typed in the car park and the photograph was taken on the 12th* — and then the only door it opened was the one that assumes the photograph does not exist yet. **Two clients differed on a capability**, which is the class D234 forbids and the same class as the receipt's missing delete (D284). It survived five waves of screenshots for a reason worth writing down: `cameraAvailable` is **false on a simulator**, so every shot this repo has ever taken went down the branch a phone never takes, and photographed the picker the phone could not open. And the composer's accessibility hint said *"Opens your camera roll"* over a control that opened the camera — the one place the product stated the intent, and it was already wrong.
- **Recommendation:** the door **asks**. `RoundPhotoSource.offered(cameraAvailable:)` is the list — `[.library, .camera]` on a phone, `[.library]` on a machine with no camera — and `csPhotoSource` draws it as a `confirmationDialog`, which is iOS's own furniture for an either/or and the same control `RootView` uses for sign-out. **The roll is first**, because that is D293's own argument applied to the door instead of the act. One door needs no question, so a simulator and a camera-less iPad still open the roll directly. The title over the menu is the act the finger pressed (`Add a photo` / `Replace photo`). No `Cancel` is typed: LINT-25 says the product has one dismiss verb and it is `Close`, and an action sheet's cancel is the system's word, supplied in the system's localisation. **The scan keeps the camera** and that is deliberate — `Scan the scorecard` photographs the card in the golfer's hand, it is an alternative to the keypad rather than to the picture (IOS-066), and the desk says the same thing in one attribute: `capture="environment"` on `#postScanFile`, absent on `#postPhotoFile`.
- **Principle served:** D234 (one product; two clients never differ on a capability) · D293 (the photograph arrives when the golfer has it, not when the product asks) · L-32 (a control says what it does — the hint now describes the menu that exists).
- **Expected user benefit:** the picture from the 12th goes on the round. The one act a golfer most wants after posting — *show it off* — stops depending on him not having taken the photograph yet.
- **Tradeoffs:** the fix is a **menu**, and a menu is the one thing this machine cannot open: `simctl` has no finger. So `-cs_dev_photo_menu` draws it on appear and forces the camera row on, because the simulator's honest menu is a menu of one — which is exactly the state that hid the bug. **The web needs no change**, which is worth saying plainly rather than leaving as an absence: both of its photo inputs already carry the choice, and this commit brings the phone up to the desk rather than the other way round. The guard is a pure function with a test (`RoundPhotoSource`), because the assertion that catches this is not "does `showLibrary` exist" — every grep for it succeeded — but "is the roll in the list at all". The PROFILE photo is the same class in the opposite direction (the phone's `PhotosPicker` is library-only where the desk's input offers both) and is **named here and not changed**: nobody has asked for a self-portrait from the settings pane, and a beta morning is the wrong time to restructure a control on a settings screen. It is the next one to close.

### D299 · A pride bet is called a pride bet — the noun stops meaning the opposite of the act — AMENDS D131 / T-02
**AUTHORISED 2026-09-08** (owner, from his own phone on build 748: *"In the fellas league it says I can 'Post a forfeit' which sounds like a quit game but then it says its like a side bet."* · ruling: **a pride bet**) · UI / TERMINOLOGY level · D47, D64, D131, D234, D242, T-02; `TERMINOLOGY` §1 def 9, §2 row 138, §3

- **Current mechanic:** the optional, never-money bet between golfers is **a forfeit**. D64 built it; **D131 named it**, and named it to solve a different collision: *stake* meant money on one pane and never-money on the next, so *stake* was fenced to live-game money (§13.2) and the Pot tab's pride bets took `forfeits` — the table's own noun, already in the schema since `20260724120000`. The word ships in about twenty user-facing places across the two clients: the ledger head *Bets for pride · on the record*, the control *Post a forfeit*, the sheet, *Settle the forfeit*, *Scrap this forfeit*, the callout's stake row *A forfeit*, the plan's gloss *a forfeit — a bet in words*, and the frozen-league line *You can put a forfeit on it.*
- **Problem:** **the word means the opposite of the act.** In ordinary English and in golf specifically, to forfeit is to concede — to quit and hand the other man the win. The product uses it for a bet a golfer goes out of his way to POST. The tell was already on the screen and had been read as ornament: the sheet's title says *Post a forfeit* and the sentence directly beneath it has to correct it — *A forfeit is a bet for pride.* **A label that needs a definition under it to stop being misread is the wrong label**, and D202's rule (say it once) was being satisfied by saying it twice in opposite directions. Two more things this exposed. (1) **The good noun was already on screen, one line above the bad one**: the ledger head reads *Bets for pride*. (2) **The product already uses `forfeit` in its ordinary sense in its own schema** — `floor_penalty` is `none | deduct | forfeit`, where forfeiting a month is exactly what the owner thought the button meant. One word, two opposite senses, inside one codebase. And LV-02's *one composer, one set of words* was still unmet: the Pot pane's sheet was titled *Post a forfeit* while the season-less sheet (`ForfeitSheet`) was titled *What's on it?* — two titles for one act.
- **Recommendation:** **a pride bet.** *Post a pride bet* · *Settle the pride bet* · the ledger head *Pride bets · on the record* · the definition drops its self-correcting opener and becomes **"A bet for pride. It settles on a tap and goes on the record — never on the books."** Both composers take **one** title, `ForfeitCopy.title`, which closes LV-02 for real. It is **copy only**: `forfeits`, `create_forfeit`, `settle_forfeit`, `scrap_forfeit` and `floor_penalty` keep their names, because a schema word is not a product word (the `#obJoin` *league code* debt is the same class from the other side) — so there is **no migration**, and check 29 is untouched. The retired phrasings join preflight's *one money noun* rule, which is how D131's own rename was held.
- **Principle served:** **D47's line, extended.** *The books* means money, full stop — and by the same logic a word that means conceding may not also mean betting. TERMINOLOGY §1's ledger is a set of definitions, and definition 9 was the only one whose sentence existed to contradict its own headword. D202 (say it once) · D234 (both clients, one commit) · L-32 (a control says what it does).
- **Expected user benefit:** a golfer who has never read a definition reads the control correctly the first time. The owner did not, and he wrote the product.
- **Tradeoffs:** **"bet" stays in the copy and that is deliberate** — it was already there (*a bet for pride*), and the alternative the owner weighed, *a side bet*, is the one option that reads as money to most people and would have leaned on the never-money sentence to undo it. D39/D64's posture is unchanged and nothing here prints an amount; `moneyWords` still guards every string on the sheet. **`forfeit` survives in identifiers, RPC names, the table, the route hatch and `floor_penalty`**, and that is the point rather than an oversight: those are not read by golfers. **This AMENDS D131's assignment** (pride bets → *forfeits*) and TERMINOLOGY §1 def 9, §2 row 138 and §3's mapping; D131's other four assignments — *card*, *stake*, *tee sheet*, *cup*, *the books* — are untouched, and *stake* stays fenced to live-game money, which was D131's actual problem and is still solved. **The docs are edited, not rewritten** (the owner's standing instruction): the terminology rows that define the noun move, and the audit and overhaul documents that quote *Post a forfeit* as historical evidence stay as written, because they are a record of what shipped.
